studies.title: Docetaxel Addition in Metastatic Castrate-Sensitive Prostate Cancer (ASPIRE)

amendments.text: Current version (pre-activation revision responding to CTEP review). Primary statistician changed; imaging substudy, PSMA PET correlative, and PROMIS measures removed; serum potassium removed from labs; stratification note added that metachronous low volume is ineligible; baseline TSH now as needed; follow-up revised to every 6 months for up to 10 years from randomization; treatment may continue past PSA progression until radiographic progression.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: High-volume (de novo or metachronous) or de novo low-volume mCSPC on conventional imaging, with tissue NGS results available. ADT +/- ARSI started within 120 days allowed. Treatment starts within 14 days.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Timing/volume: de novo high volume vs de novo low volume vs metachronous high volume (high volume = 4 or more bone metastases, any location, or visceral disease). TSG alteration count in PTEN, RB1, TP53: 0 vs 1 vs 2+.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Open-label. 12-week cycles. All patients get ADT (investigator choice) plus apalutamide 240 mg PO daily until progression or withdrawal.

arms.label: Arm 1: ADT + apalutamide
arms.text: No chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 2: ADT + apalutamide + docetaxel
arms.text: Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 21 days (±7 days) for 6 doses (C1D1, C1D22, C1D43, C1D64, C2D1, C2D22), with dexamethasone 20 mg IV premedication.

schema.label: Local therapy
schema.text: Radiation to the prostate primary is at investigator discretion (not protocol-specified).

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Every 6 months for up to 10 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival. Target 1,200 patients; HR 0.75 assumed.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2. Candidate for docetaxel.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma without small cell histology.

M1 disease on conventional CT/MRI and/or bone scan: bone metastases (PCWG3), non-regional nodes above the aortic bifurcation (short axis 15 mm or more), or visceral/soft tissue lesions. Regional (N1) nodes only, or PSMA-PET-only disease, are not eligible.
No metachronous low-volume disease (recurrence after definitive local therapy with 4 or fewer bone metastases and no visceral disease).
Tissue-based CLIA NGS result available at registration (soft tissue or visceral preferred; bone or primary accepted; blood-based not allowed). Failed NGS is not eligible.
ADT (LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy), with or without a first-generation anti-androgen or ARSI, only if started within 120 days of registration. No prior chemotherapy for prostate cancer.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin at most 1 x ULN (Gilbert's eligible if direct bilirubin at most 1 x ULN), AST/ALT at most 1.5 x ULN, CrCl above 30 mL/min.
No seizure or seizure-predisposing condition (stroke within 1 year, brain AVM, or condition needing CNS surgery or RT). Seizure-threshold-lowering drugs stopped before entry.
Treated leptomeningeal metastases allowed if brain imaging 30 days after CNS therapy shows no progression.
Cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class II or better. Stable asymptomatic DVT on anticoagulation allowed.
No uncontrolled hypertension (resting systolic 160 or diastolic 100 mmHg despite treatment).
HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (stop before registration) or strong inducers (stop 14 days before treatment). No hypersensitivity to study drugs.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

studies.title: A Phase III Randomized Clinical Trial of Proton Craniospinal Irradiation Versus Involved-Field Radiotherapy for Patients with Breast Cancer or Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Leptomeningeal Metastasis (Radiate-LM)

amendments.text: Amendment 1. Listed in the document history. These opening pages do not summarize what changed.
Initial. Listed in the document history. These opening pages do not summarize what changed.

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Register after financial clearance for proton therapy.

schema.label: Step 2
schema.text: Step 2 must occur no later than 30 days after Step 1. Stratify by histology (breast versus NSCLC), systemic disease status (active versus stable or none), and use of intrathecal therapy and/or immunotherapy and/or targeted therapy, including antibody-drug conjugates, within 4 weeks before Step 2 and/or planned within 4 weeks after RT (yes versus no). Randomize 1:1. Protocol treatment starts within 21 days after randomization. Intrathecal therapy is not given on radiotherapy days in either arm. Systemic therapy may be given on radiation days at investigator discretion. Primary endpoint is overall survival.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Involved-field photon RT, 3 Gy x 10 daily fractions, to focal radiographic and/or symptomatic sites, then standard-of-care therapy per the investigator. Treatment of the entire craniospinal compartment is not allowed.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Proton craniospinal irradiation, 3 Gy x 10 daily fractions, to the entire craniospinal compartment, then standard-of-care therapy per the investigator. Proton dose is reported in Gy (RBE) with RBE 1.1.

eligibility: Step 1: Pathologically, histologically or cytologically, proven breast cancer or NSCLC, age 18 or older, and a candidate for radiation for leptomeningeal metastasis. The patient must be able to undergo MRI with and without gadolinium.

Newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis, shown by positive CSF cytology, or by radiographic linear and/or nodular disease plus typical clinical signs meeting EANO-ESMO diagnostic criteria type IIA to IIC when cytology is equivocal or negative or CSF sampling is not suitable. CSF cytology with suspicious cells is positive. Atypical cells are equivocal and are not positive. For prior or current immunotherapy, CSF sampling rather than MRI enhancement alone is strongly recommended, to exclude immune-related aseptic meningitis.

Step 2 registration is no later than 30 days after Step 1 and requires financial clearance for proton therapy, standard-of-care systemic imaging such as CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis or body PET/CT, and Karnofsky performance status at least 60.
Not pregnant and not nursing. A person of childbearing potential needs a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before registration.

Hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL, ANC at least 1,000/mm3, and platelets at least 100,000/mm3. Transfusion, growth factor, or another intervention may be used to meet those blood counts. Total bilirubin at or under 1.5 x institutional ULN. Gilbert disease without other clinically significant liver abnormalities is not excluded. AST and ALT at or under 3 x ULN.

No prior radiation to the spinal cord with EQD2 more than 40 Gy, or to the cauda equina with EQD2 more than 50 Gy, using an alpha/beta ratio of 3. No prior treatment for leptomeningeal metastasis. Prior CNS treatment for other non-leptomeningeal disease is allowed.

No history of unstable angina requiring hospitalization in the last 3 months. No myocardial infarction within the last 3 months. NYHA class III or IV is not eligible, and class II or better is required. No active infection currently requiring intravenous antibiotics. No active COPD exacerbation or other acute respiratory illness precluding study therapy. No CTCAE v5.0 grade 2 or higher encephalopathy.

studies.title: A Randomized Phase II Trial of Nivolumab and Ipilimumab Compared to Nivolumab Monotherapy in Patients with Deficient Mismatch Repair System Recurrent Endometrial Carcinoma

amendments.text: Amendment 7, the current version.
Amendment 6. Safety lead-in accrual hold wording revised (accrual continues if 6 or fewer of the first 25 have a DLT).
Amendment 5. Second safety lead-in component opened to all NCTN sites.
Amendment 4. Eligibility section revised.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Recurrent mismatch repair deficient endometrial carcinoma with measurable or non-measurable (detectable) disease.

schema.label: Safety lead-in
schema.text: Two-step safety lead-in embedded in the phase II design: DLT review after 12 and after 25 patients evaluable over 3 cycles. Since Amendment 5 the second component is open to all NCTN sites.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior radiation, prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, measurable disease (yes vs no).

schema.label: Randomize 2:1
schema.text: Arm 1 vs Arm 2. Treatment starts within 7 days of registration.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Nivolumab 360 mg IV every 3 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks (every other cycle) for 4 doses, then nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or CR.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Nivolumab 360 mg IV every 3 weeks for 8 cycles, then 480 mg IV every 4 weeks, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or CR.

schema.label: Maintenance
schema.text: Patients with CR continue nivolumab for up to 12 additional months after confirmed radiologic CR.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival.

eligibility: Recurrent endometrial cancer with measurable disease (RECIST 1.1) or non-measurable detectable disease (small lesions, tumor-related ascites or effusion, or non-target imaging abnormalities).
Mismatch repair deficient by institutional IHC (loss of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, or EPCAM) and/or MSI-high by MSI testing or NGS; equivocal IHC allowed with documented MSI.
Histology: endometrioid, mucinous, dedifferentiated/undifferentiated, clear cell, mixed epithelial, or adenocarcinoma NOS. No serous carcinoma or carcinosarcoma.

1-2 prior lines of systemic therapy. Prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 allowed only if given with chemotherapy or RT in the adjuvant or primary metastatic/recurrent setting, with CR and a treatment-free interval of 12 months or more since the last checkpoint inhibitor dose.

Prior RT for endometrial cancer (pelvic, extended field, vaginal brachytherapy, palliative) allowed if completed at least 4 weeks before registration. Hormonal therapy stopped at least 3 weeks before; other anticancer therapy at least 4 weeks before (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C). At least 4 weeks since major surgery.
Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2.

Platelets 100,000/mcL or more, ANC 1,500/mcL or more, creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less, bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (3 x ULN or less with Gilbert's), AST and ALT 3 x ULN or less, within 14 days. Oxygen saturation with hypoxia below grade 2 within 28 days.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better with QTc below 450 msec.
Treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression and the patient is stable off steroids for at least 1 month.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.

No prior CTLA-4 inhibitor or other T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint agent beyond the allowed anti-PD-1/PD-L1. No grade 3-4 or recurrent grade 2 immune-related toxicity on prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 that led to delay or discontinuation.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that might recur and affect vital organs or need systemic immunosuppression (vitiligo, replaced endocrinopathies, and topically controlled psoriasis allowed). No known immune impairment.
No chronic steroids above prednisone 10 mg daily or equivalent, and no immunosuppressive therapy (inhaled, topical, intranasal, local injections, and hypersensitivity premedication allowed).
No uncontrolled intercurrent illness, including active infection, interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis, symptomatic heart failure, unstable angina, or arrhythmia.
No severe hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies or to nivolumab or ipilimumab.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

studies.title: A Randomized Phase III Study of BRAF-Targeted Therapy vs Cabozantinib in RAI-Refractory Differentiated Thyroid Cancer with BRAF V600Em

schema.label: Eligibility
schema.text: Advanced RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer with BRAF V600E, measurable by RECIST 1.1, radiographic progression on or after first-line multikinase inhibitor, 1-2 prior multikinase inhibitors including lenvatinib and/or sorafenib, ECOG 0-2.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Baseline tumor burden: sum of all target lesions < 4 cm vs >= 4 cm.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: N=240. 1 cycle = 28 days.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Dabrafenib 150 mg PO BID plus trametinib 2 mg PO daily, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily (tablets), until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Crossover
schema.text: Crossover to the other arm allowed at RECIST progression (not for toxicity); continue until second RECIST progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Response until progression and survival for 5 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival (RECIST 1.1 progression or death).

eligibility: Age >= 18 years; ECOG performance status 0-2.
Differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary or follicular, including variants such as tall cell, Hürthle cell, and poorly differentiated) with BRAF V600E by local testing; prior biopsy results accepted.
Previously treated with, or ineligible for, I-131, and receiving thyroxine suppression therapy.
Prior treatment with at least one VEGFR-targeting TKI for DTC (lenvatinib or sorafenib); up to two prior VEGFR-targeting TKIs allowed.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 on chest CT and abdomen/pelvis CT/MRI within 4 weeks before randomization, with radiographic progression by RECIST 1.1 on or after the most recent systemic therapy.
No prior cabozantinib or prior BRAF-targeted therapy for thyroid cancer; prior checkpoint inhibitor allowed.
No anaplastic histology or transformation on any recurrence specimen after initial thyroidectomy/neck dissection.

Prior local therapy (surgery, radiation, ablation) completed at least 4 weeks before randomization, with complications resolved. No major surgery within 8 weeks (wound healing 4 weeks after major and 10 days after minor surgery).

No NYHA class 3-4 heart failure, unstable angina, or serious arrhythmia; no uncontrolled hypertension (sustained > 150/100 mm Hg despite optimal treatment); no stroke, MI, or thromboembolic event within 6 months (recent DVT allowed if stable on therapeutic anticoagulation for at least 6 weeks).
No clinically significant hematemesis or hemoptysis > 2.5 mL or other significant bleeding within 3 months; no cavitating pulmonary lesions or lesions invading major pulmonary vessels.

No oral anticoagulants or platelet inhibitors except low-dose aspirin, or therapeutic anticoagulation in patients without known brain metastases on a stable dose for at least 6 weeks without significant hemorrhagic complications.

No GI disorders with high perforation or fistula risk (tumor invading GI tract, active peptic ulcer, IBD, diverticulitis, acute pancreatitis, biliary or gastric outlet obstruction, etc.); no abdominal fistula, GI perforation, bowel obstruction, or intra-abdominal abscess within 6 months.

Labs within 28 days: Hgb >= 8 g/dL, leukocytes >= 3,000/mcL, ANC >= 1,500/mcL, platelets >= 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin <= 2.0 x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3.0 x ULN (< 5.0 x ULN with liver metastases), eGFR >= 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
QTcF <= 500 ms within 28 days before randomization (average of 3 ECGs if the first is > 500 ms).
Treated brain metastases allowed if post-treatment imaging shows no progression, stable for at least 4 weeks, neurologically asymptomatic, and off corticosteroids.

HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it does not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 14 days for patients of childbearing potential).
English or Spanish speaking for the QOL component.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Age 45 or older and under 70 at qualifying colonoscopy, with a first diagnosis of 1-2 non-advanced adenomas at a complete qualifying colonoscopy within the previous 4 years.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Age at qualifying colonoscopy (45-55 vs 56 to under 70), sex, time from qualifying colonoscopy to randomization (under 2 years vs 2-4 years).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Dynamic minimization with biased coin.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Surveillance colonoscopy at 5 years and 10 years after the qualifying colonoscopy (each +/- 1 year).

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Surveillance colonoscopy at 10 years after the qualifying colonoscopy (+/- 1 year).

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Annual contact for disease and vital status; long-term follow-up up to 30 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Colorectal cancer incidence in years 4 through 11 (non-inferiority of the 10-year-only schedule).

eligibility: Age 45 or older and under 70 at the time of the qualifying colonoscopy.

First-time diagnosis of 1-2 non-advanced tubular adenomas (under 10 mm, no tubulovillous or villous features, no high-grade or severe dysplasia) on a qualifying colonoscopy within 4 years before randomization. Sessile serrated polyps that do not meet advanced criteria count as non-advanced.
Qualifying colonoscopy complete to the cecum with adequate preparation, with complete excision of all adenomatous polyps (excision of hyperplastic rectosigmoid polyps not required).
Able to read or understand English or Spanish.
No prior colorectal cancer or colorectal adenoma (including sessile serrated lesions) other than those found on the qualifying colonoscopy.
No hyperplastic polyp 1 cm or larger, either previously or on the qualifying colonoscopy. No traditional serrated adenoma on the qualifying colonoscopy.
No colonoscopy between the qualifying colonoscopy and randomization.
No subtotal colectomy or total proctocolectomy (segmental resection allowed).
No first-degree relative with CRC diagnosed at age 60 or younger, and no two first-degree relatives with CRC at any age.
No clinical diagnosis or known germline mutation for familial adenomatous polyposis or Lynch syndrome. No inflammatory bowel disease.
No prior malignancy unless disease-free for 5 or more years and at low risk of recurrence; in situ cancers and basal or squamous cell skin cancer within 5 years allowed.
No life expectancy under 10 years from comorbidity, and no condition that would prevent colonoscopy or follow-up.

studies.title: Phase 1/ 2 Study of Dinutuximab/ Cyclophosphamide/ Topotecan/ Sargramostim (GM-CSF) with or Without Iberdomide in Children with Relapsed, Refractory, or Progressive Neuroblastoma Following Prior Chemoimmunotherapy

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG groupwide Phase 1/2 (US sites only) for relapsed, refractory, or progressive neuroblastoma after exactly one prior chemoimmunotherapy regimen. 28-day cycles, up to 12 cycles absent progression or unacceptable toxicity. Up to 76 patients.

schema.label: Backbone (DIN/CPM/Topo/GMCSF)
schema.text: Cyclophosphamide 250 mg/m2 IV and topotecan 0.75 mg/m2 IV days 1-5; dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2 IV over 10 hours days 2-5; sargramostim 250 mcg/m2 starting day 6 or 7 for at least 7 doses or until count recovery post-nadir.

schema.label: Phase 1 dose escalation
schema.text: Rolling six design adding enteral iberdomide to the backbone: dose level -1 0.4 mg/m2 (max 0.75 mg) days 1-14; level 1 0.6 mg/m2 (max 1 mg) days 1-14; level 2 0.6 mg/m2 (max 1 mg) days 1-21. Primary aim: RP2D.

schema.label: Phase 2 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified by MYCN status (amplified vs non-amplified/unknown) and relapsed vs refractory disease. Primary aim: response rate with vs without iberdomide.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: DIN/CPM/Topo/GMCSF.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Iberdomide at the RP2D plus DIN/CPM/Topo/GMCSF.

schema.label: Disease evaluations
schema.text: After cycles 2, 4, 6, 9, and 12 and at end of therapy, with confirmatory evaluation at least 4 weeks after a first response. Surgery of the primary allowed after confirmed response; no radiation on protocol therapy.

eligibility: Age ≥ 1 and ≤ 30 years at enrollment.
Neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma by histology, or marrow tumor cells with urinary catecholamines > 2 x ULN, at initial diagnosis.

Primary refractory disease after at least 4 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy (as induction, extended induction, or pre-consolidation), or first relapse after induction or post-consolidation chemoimmunotherapy, or second relapse after chemoimmunotherapy given as first salvage.
Exactly one prior chemoimmunotherapy-containing regimen; a change in chemotherapy or anti-GD2 antibody counts as a second line.
No progression during or within 30 days of completing chemoimmunotherapy (last anti-GD2 dose) in induction or extended induction, and no stable disease after chemoimmunotherapy for first relapse.
Measurable MIBG-avid or FDG-avid soft tissue disease, or evaluable MIBG-avid lesions, or a new FDG-avid bone site with CT/MRI correlate or biopsy. No marrow-only or catecholamine-only disease.
Previously irradiated lesions count as targets only with progression after RT or viable tumor on post-RT biopsy.
Karnofsky or Lansky corresponding to ECOG 0-2.

Washouts: myelosuppressive chemotherapy 14 days; antibodies 21 days; small-port RT 7 days; large-field RT (TBI, CSI, whole abdomen, total lung, > 50% marrow) 12 weeks; other substantial marrow RT 6 weeks; autologous SCT 6 weeks.
No prior 131I-MIBG therapy for relapsed/refractory disease or poor end-of-induction response (frontline induction 131I-MIBG allowed after 6 weeks).
ANC ≥ 1000/µL and platelets ≥ 100,000/µL transfusion independent; creatinine within age limits or GFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 by direct measurement.
Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, ALT ≤ 135 U/L; shortening fraction ≥ 27% or ejection fraction ≥ 50%.
No untreated CNS disease (adequately treated CNS disease without progression is allowed).
No prior allogeneic SCT, MDS, or other malignancy.
No pharmacologic systemic steroids within 7 days or expected need on study; no other immunosuppressants.
No permanent discontinuation of anti-GD2 therapy or GM-CSF for toxicity, no prior iberdomide, and no serious allergy to thalidomide, lenalidomide, or pomalidomide.
No enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants within 7 days or strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors within 14 days.
No prior unprovoked thrombosis; provoked events allowed if off anticoagulation or on a stable dose ≥ 6 weeks.
No peripheral neuropathy ≥ grade 2, no inability to take enteral medication, and not pregnant or breastfeeding; two contraception methods required with iberdomide.

Phase III Study of Local or Systemic Therapy INtensification DIrected by PET in Prostate CAncer Patients with Post-ProstaTEctomy Biochemical Recurrence (INDICATE)

schema.label: Step 0
schema.text: Register, then obtain a standard-of-care PET/CT or PET/MR (PET1) with any FDA-approved prostate radiotracer before treatment planning. PET1 may be done during Step 0 or up to 16 weeks before Step 0. Record prostate fossa, intra-pelvic, and extra-pelvic sites. Extra-pelvic means any bone metastasis, or soft tissue, node, or organ disease above the common iliac bifurcation or outside standard prostate bed plus whole-pelvis fields. Step 1 randomization must occur within 7 days of Step 0 registration.

schema.label: Step 1, after Amendment 11
schema.text: The schema figure for patients enrolled after Amendment 11 shows only PET-positive extra-pelvic disease. Stratify lymph node sites only versus any non-lymph node site. Every patient on Arms C and D receives standard salvage therapy: prostate bed and pelvic lymph node external-beam RT plus a protocol-listed GnRH agonist or antagonist for 6 months. ADT may start from 7 days before Step 0 through 14 days after Step 1. RT starts after Step 1, from 7 days before ADT through 3 months after ADT starts. Apalutamide 240 mg by mouth once daily starts after Step 1 and within 28 days of ADT, and continues for 6 months. No randomization ratio is printed. The prostate bed and pelvic dose is institutional standard of care, not a fixed protocol dose.

arms.label: Arm C
arms.text: Standard salvage RT, 6 months of ADT, and apalutamide, with no upfront metastasis-directed RT. Metastasis-directed RT is allowed later for radiographic progression by PET or conventional imaging, or for persistent extra-pelvic PET disease after protocol treatment.

arms.label: Arm D
arms.text: Standard salvage RT, 6 months of ADT, and apalutamide, plus upfront metastasis-directed RT to all technically feasible PET-positive metastases during the 6 months of ADT. Options are SBRT 30 Gy in 3 fractions, with at least 40 hours between treatments for an individual field, reducible to as low as 35 Gy in 5 fractions, or non-SBRT 50 Gy in 10 fractions. Non-SBRT dose reductions are also permitted to meet constraints.

schema.label: PET2
schema.text: On Arms C and D, if PET1 used Axumin or flotufolastat F 18 (Posluma), repeat that tracer at PSA recurrence, at a clinical indication, or at 12 months after systemic therapy, whichever comes first. Other PET1 tracers do not receive a protocol PET2.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival from randomization: radiographic progression by conventional imaging or standard PET, cancer-related symptoms, or death.

eligibility: Step 0: Male and age 18 or older, with histopathologically proven prostatic adenocarcinoma treated by radical prostatectomy, ECOG performance status 0-2, and a candidate for standard post-prostatectomy RT to the prostate bed and pelvic nodes with ADT.

Biochemical recurrence meets one of three rules: PSA at least 0.2 ng/mL if the first detectable PSA was within 12 months after prostatectomy, and a persistent post-prostatectomy PSA of at least 0.2 ng/mL is eligible; PSA at least 0.5 ng/mL if the first detectable PSA was more than 12 months after prostatectomy; or any detectable PSA if baseline standard PET shows at least one positive lesion.

From Addendum 11, conventional imaging within 26 weeks before Step 0 must show no definite extra-pelvic metastatic disease. If there is no prior conventional imaging, it is optional when PET is positive for extra-pelvic lesions and is not required when PET is negative for extra-pelvic lesions. Non-osseous pelvic lesions are allowed if they fit in standard salvage fields.
Short-term ADT must not start before baseline PET. It may start after PET and up to 7 days before registration. A short course of low-dose antiandrogen, generally after PET1, is allowed as a bridge.

The patient must not be on another therapeutic trial, must tolerate lying flat for PET and radiation planning, and a PET/MR must meet local MRI safety rules. No seizures, and no stroke or head trauma with loss of consciousness, within 1 year. No inflammatory bowel disease or absorption disorder expected to make pelvic RT risk unacceptable by institutional standard.

Labs within 8 weeks before Step 0: hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, independent of transfusion or growth factors within 3 months; leukocytes at least 3,000/mcL; ANC at least 1,500/mcL; platelets at least 100,000/mcL; total bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN, or for Gilbert syndrome a direct bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN; AST and ALT at or under 2.5 x ULN; creatinine under 1.5 x ULN or measured creatinine clearance over 30 mL/min.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class I or II, or objective class A or B. No prior pelvic external-beam RT that would overlap standard fields so that normal-tissue constraints cannot be met. The patient must agree not to father children. English or Spanish is required for the quality-of-life component.

Step 1: Baseline standard PET/CT or PET/MR with an FDA-approved prostate radiotracer must be completed after Step 0 and before randomization, or up to 16 weeks before Step 0, and must establish extra-pelvic disease as positive or negative. PET-negative patients need known intra-pelvic node status. Equivocal or positive extra-pelvic disease must be classified as lymph node sites only versus any non-lymph node site. A PSMA lesion is positive if at least likely prostate cancer, including a PSMA-RAD score of 3 or higher.

studies.title: Phase III Trial of Radiotherapy Followed by Adjuvant Temozolomide in Combination with the IDH Inhibitor Vorasidenib vs Placebo in IDH-Mutated Newly-Diagnosed Grade 3 Astrocytomas

schema.label: Pre-registration
schema.text: Central biomarker testing and histopathology review must confirm WHO grade 3 astrocytoma with intact 1p/19q, an IDH mutation, and absence of CDKN2A/B homozygous codeletion. One cycle is 28 days.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Both arms receive radiotherapy, a 4-week break, 12 months of adjuvant temozolomide with blinded daily vorasidenib or placebo, then the blinded agent alone until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Radiotherapy is 59.4 Gy in 33 fractions at 1.8 Gy per day. Temozolomide is oral, 150 mg/m2/day on days 1-5 of cycle 1 and 200 mg/m2/day on days 1-5 of later cycles. Vorasidenib or placebo is 40 mg orally once daily on days 1-28. Under age 18, the blinded dose is 40 mg if weight is at least 40 kg and 20 mg if weight is under 40 kg. Doses are from the treatment-plan table; the schema page names the agents and schedule but not the gray or milligram amounts. Real-time central imaging confirms progression. Follow-up continues for 10 years or until death.

arms.label: Control arm
arms.text: Radiotherapy, a 4-week break, then temozolomide on days 1-5 plus placebo on days 1-28 for 12 months, then placebo alone on days 1-28 until progression.

arms.label: Experimental arm
arms.text: Radiotherapy, a 4-week break, then temozolomide on days 1-5 plus vorasidenib on days 1-28 for 12 months, then vorasidenib alone on days 1-28 until progression.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review, for vorasidenib plus adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy compared with placebo plus adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy, in newly diagnosed IDH-mutant WHO grade 3 astrocytoma.

eligibility: Step 0 requires a histologic diagnosis of IDH-mutant astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 3, with diagnostic H&E and immunohistochemical slides for central review and tissue for central CDKN2A/B and 1p/19q testing, plus IDH1 or IDH2 testing if needed.
Step 1 requires central confirmation of IDH-mutant astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 3, an IDH1 R132 or IDH2 R172 mutation, no CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, and intact whole-arm 1p/19q.
There is no evidence of spinal or leptomeningeal disease.
No prior chemotherapy, cranial irradiation, IDH-inhibitor therapy, radiotherapy, vaccine therapy, small-molecule therapy, or laser ablation is allowed.
Diagnostic surgery, resection, or biopsy is within 8 weeks before registration, and radiotherapy plus adjuvant chemotherapy is planned.
Age is 12 or older, with ECOG performance status 2 or better or Karnofsky performance status at least 60%.

Required labs are ANC at least 1,500/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (at most 1.0 x ULN in Gilbert syndrome), AST and ALT at most 2.5 x ULN, alkaline phosphatase at most 2.5 x ULN, and creatinine at most 2.0 x ULN or calculated creatinine clearance greater than 40 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault at age 18 or older, Bedside Schwartz under 18).
Patients are not pregnant and not nursing, and women of childbearing potential need a negative pregnancy test within 14 days before registration.
There is no severe intercurrent illness, no active infection requiring systemic anti-infective therapy, and no unexplained fever above 38.5 degrees C within 7 days before registration.
A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment, and the patient must be able to undergo MRI.

HIV is allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration; chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; hepatitis C must be cured, or undetectable on current treatment.
There is no NYHA class III or IV heart failure, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or stroke within 6 months, and patients should be class 2B or better.
There is no history of grade 2 or higher intratumoral or peritumoral hemorrhage.

Active inflammatory gastrointestinal disease, chronic diarrhea, prior gastric resection or lap-band dysphagia, short-gut syndrome, gastroparesis, or inability to swallow oral agents is excluded; treated gastroesophageal reflux is allowed.
There is no known hypersensitivity to vorasidenib or temozolomide.
No concurrent investigational agent and no concurrent alternating tumor treating fields are allowed.

Therapeutic corticosteroid doses for glioma are not allowed, physiologic steroids at or below 10 mg prednisone daily are allowed for conditions unrelated to glioma, and glioma-related corticosteroids should be the smallest dose that controls edema and stopped whenever possible.
Warfarin and other coumadin-derivative anticoagulants are not allowed and must be stopped at least 7 days before registration; low molecular weight heparin and factor Xa inhibitors are allowed.
Strong or moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors, moderate CYP1A2 inducers, and CYP3A substrates for which a small concentration change can reduce efficacy must be replaced before registration.

studies.title: Phase II Study of Cytarabine + Daunorubicin (7 + 3) + Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin vs. Cytarabine + Daunorubicin (7 + 3) + Venetoclax for the Treatment of Newly Diagnosed Core Binding Factor Acute Myeloid Leukemia (CBF-AML) in Younger Adults: A MyeloMATCH Substudy

amendments.text: Update #01, the current version. Clarified GO dosing windows (first dose days 1-3, second dose days 4-6, at least 3 days apart), corrected cardiac eligibility to NYHA class II or better, clarified the end-of-treatment timepoint, added a 5 half-life washout when prior-malignancy therapy could interfere, made radiation for myeloid sarcoma or other malignancy a reason for removal from protocol, updated venetoclax toxicity tables, and removed the medication diary.

schema.label: Step 0: MYELOMATCH registration
schema.text: Registered to the MYELOMATCH Master Screening and Reassessment Protocol and assigned to MM1YA-A04 by the MATCHBox Treatment Verification Team.

schema.label: Registration and cohort assignment
schema.text: Cohort 1: RAS/KIT mutated. Cohort 2: RAS/KIT nonmutated (pathogenic KIT or RAS mutation, VAF ≥ 5%). The two cohorts accrue and are analyzed as separate parallel studies. Stratified by t(8;21) vs inv(16)/t(16;16).

schema.label: Randomize within each cohort
schema.text: 1 cycle of induction only (no reinduction, no day 14 marrow). Treatment starts ≤ 14 days after registration; WBC must be < 25 x 10^9/L before starting.

arms.label: Regimen 1 (control): 7+3 + GO
arms.text: Cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CI days 1-7; daunorubicin 60 mg/m2/day IV days 1-3; gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 (max 4.5 mg) IV days 1 and 4 (first dose may slip to day 2 or 3, second to day 5 or 6; doses at least 3 days apart).

arms.label: Regimen 2 (experimental): 7+3 + venetoclax
arms.text: Cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CI days 2-8; daunorubicin 60 mg/m2/day IV days 2-4; venetoclax PO ramp-up 50 mg day 1, 100 mg day 2, 200 mg day 3, then 400 mg daily days 4-11 (adjusted for CYP3A interactions such as azole antifungals).

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: Bone marrow about day 28 (± 3 days), delayed up to 14 days for count recovery (ANC ≥ 1.0 x 10^9/L or PLT ≥ 100 x 10^9/L).

schema.label: After induction
schema.text: Persistent disease: reassignment to a higher-tier MYELOMATCH study if available, otherwise institutional treatment. MRD-negative: off-protocol consolidation per treating physician (recommended 3-4 cycles of intermediate/high-dose cytarabine; GO in consolidation per institutional practice). Follow-up to 5 years.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: CR without measurable residual disease (CR MRD-negative) by multiparameter flow cytometry after induction, compared between arms within each cohort.

eligibility: Registered to MYELOMATCH and assigned to this substudy.

AML with t(8;21)(q22;q22.1)/RUNX1::RUNX1T1, or inv(16)(p13.1q22) or t(16;16)(p13.1;q22)/CBFB::MYH11. Secondary CBF-AML (prior pre-leukemic hematologic malignancy or prior chemotherapy/radiation) is allowed.
No FLT3 mutation (these patients go to a FLT3-focused MYELOMATCH study).

No prior AML- or MDS-directed therapy, except urgent leukocytosis control with leukapheresis, hydroxyurea, or cytarabine up to 1 g. Prior intrathecal chemotherapy for CNS AML, ATRA, BCR-ABL TKI, ESA, TPO receptor agonist, and lenalidomide are allowed.
Age 18-59 years.
ECOG performance status ≤ 3.
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert syndrome allowed if direct bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN); AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN; GFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Not pregnant and not nursing; negative pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if its natural history or treatment will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
CNS disease allowed, treated with intrathecal chemotherapy per institutional guidelines.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration. Chronic HBV allowed if viral load undetectable on suppressive therapy. HCV must be treated and cured, or viral load undetectable if on treatment.
Known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class II or better.
No medical condition preventing swallowing of oral medications.

amendments.text: Initial protocol.
Amendment 1. Baseline pre-chemotherapy requirements are dated this day.
Amendment 2, the current version. The schema, required chemotherapy before entry, post-chemotherapy requirements, pretreatment table, and treatment-arm descriptions are dated this day.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Protocol-mandated chemotherapy received: mFOLFIRINOX, FOLFIRINOX, or NALIRIFOX versus gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel. If both a 5-FU-based regimen and a gemcitabine-based regimen were used during the required 4-8 months, stratify by the category given for more months. If the months are equal, use the regimen given first.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Primary endpoint is 3-year overall survival from randomization.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard of care: continue chemotherapy, or standard-dose chemoradiation of 50.4 Gy or 54.0 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions, or observation. Observation is suggested only for patients who completed 6 months of chemotherapy before enrollment.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Dose-escalated RT. The default prescription is 10 Gy x 5 fractions (BED10 100 Gy). If 5 fractions are not feasible, 3 Gy x 25 fractions (BED10 97.5 Gy) may be used after contact with the principal investigator or a radiation oncology chair.

eligibility: Pathologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that is locally advanced and unresectable by NCCN guidelines and institutional tumor board review. Age 18 or older and ECOG performance status 0-2. Baseline pre-chemotherapy staging must be CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, CT chest with MRI abdomen and pelvis, CT chest and pelvis with MRI abdomen, or PET/CT.

Before enrollment the patient must have received 4-8 months of active chemotherapy with mFOLFIRINOX, FOLFIRINOX, or NALIRIFOX, or with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel. Active time excludes treatment breaks. More than one regimen is allowed for toxicity or for CA19-9 that is not declining, not for radiographic progression by RECIST. Chemotherapy after restaging is allowed if restaging is after at least 4 months and total chemotherapy duration does not exceed 8 months. Registration must be within 45 days of the last day of that chemotherapy.
A prior or concurrent malignancy is eligible when its natural history or treatment will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of the neoadjuvant regimen or the primary endpoint.

Labs any time before chemotherapy through 30 days after chemotherapy starts: ALT and AST at or under 3 x ULN. If baseline CA19-9 is above 37 U/mL, the concurrent bilirubin must be at or under 1.5 x ULN, and both may be repeated until bilirubin is at or under 1.5 x ULN within that window. If baseline CA19-9 is at or under 37 U/mL, concurrent bilirubin is unrestricted.

After month 4 of chemotherapy and before study entry, if baseline CA19-9 was above 37 U/mL, the later CA19-9 must be under 200 U/mL or at least a 70% decline from baseline. A value of 200 U/mL or higher still qualifies if the decline is at least 70%, and a decline under 70% still qualifies if the absolute value is under 200 U/mL. If baseline CA19-9 was at or under 37 U/mL, it must remain at or under 37 U/mL.
Restaging CT, MRI, or PET/CT must show at least stable disease. No active duodenal or gastric ulcers. No direct tumor invasion of the bowel or stomach.
No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap radiation fields. Prior non-overlapping radiation, for example breast, head and neck, or extremity, is permitted.

Not pregnant and not nursing. No cardiac condition that was the primary reason for hospitalization in the last 6 months. NYHA class III or IV is not eligible, and class II or better is required. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.

studies.title: Prospective Treatment of Types I, II and III Pleuropulmonary Blastoma (PPB)

amendments.text: Current version, updated at CTEP request: 'gender' replaced with 'sex'; section 14.4 central pathology timing aligned with eligibility (Type II/III may start therapy before central review results).

schema.label: Enrollment
schema.text: Newly diagnosed Type I, Ir, II, or III PPB, age 21 or younger. APEC14B1 and MCI submission recommended. Rapid central pathology review with treatment-assignment callback via OPEN; Type II/III may start therapy before central review if clinically needed.

schema.label: Type Ir, or Type I age 5 or older, or Type I under 5 with R0 resection and no residual cysts 1 cm or larger
schema.text: Surgery alone, then surveillance. Post-operative chest CT at about 1 month (15-60 days).

schema.label: Type I, under 5 years, less than R0 and/or unresectable residual cysts 1 cm or larger
schema.text: Second-look surgery considered; VAC1200 (vincristine, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide) / VA chemotherapy, 8 cycles over 24 weeks. No radiation for Type I/Ir.

schema.label: Type II or III: window therapy
schema.text: +/- upfront surgery, +/- CNS RT for brain metastases. VTC400 (vincristine, topotecan, cyclophosphamide) for cycles 1-2 (weeks 1-6), then RECIST response assessment and callback.

schema.label: Type II or III: CR, PR, or SD after window
schema.text: IVADo (ifosfamide, vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin) cycles 3-6 (weeks 7-18) with surgery after cycle 2, 4, or 6 if complete resection is feasible; +/- thoracic RT starting with cycle 7 (week 19); then alternating VTC250 and VAC1200 for cycles 7-12 (weeks 19-36); +/- RT to extrathoracic non-CNS metastases at end of therapy.

schema.label: Type II or III: progressive disease after window
schema.text: IVADo cycles 3-6 with surgery as above, +/- thoracic RT from week 19, then IVA (ifosfamide, vincristine, dactinomycin) cycles 7-12 (weeks 19-36); +/- RT to extrathoracic non-CNS metastases at end of therapy.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall response rate (CR+PR, RECIST) to 2 cycles of VTC window in Type II/III PPB. Secondary: 3-year PFS and OS for Type II/III and for Type I.

eligibility: Age 21 years or younger.
Newly diagnosed Type I, Ir, II, or III PPB by institutional diagnosis within 60 days before enrollment; central pathology review determines assignment for Type I/Ir.
Known germline DICER1 variant or mosaicism with a large, solid unresectable thoracic mass typical of Type II/III PPB is eligible without histology if biopsy is not safe or feasible.
Type I/Ir: no organ function requirements and no labs required before enrollment; must not start chemotherapy before central pathology callback.

Type II/III: creatinine within age/sex limits or measured creatinine clearance or GFR 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher (eGFR not acceptable); bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less; ALT 135 U/L or less; shortening fraction 27% or higher or ejection fraction 50% or higher.
Type II/III: staging imaging within 21 days before enrollment and therapy; enrollment within 5 days of starting therapy.
HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months and not on strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
No prior PPB-directed chemotherapy (prior treatment for another malignancy is allowed).
No known Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
Not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

studies.title: A Phase 2 Window of Opportunity Trial of Neoadjuvant Agonistic Anti-CD40 Antibody CDX-1140 and Cemiplimab (REGN2810) in AJCC Stage III-IV Head and Neck Cancer Patients Prior to Surgery
A Phase II Trial Evaluating Chemotherapy Followed by Response-Based Reduced Radiation Therapy for Patients with Central Nervous System Germinomas

schema.label: Induction
schema.text: Pathologic or clinical diagnosis of germinoma, enrollment on APEC14B1, rapid central review on APEC14B1-CNS, study entry on ACNS2321, then induction chemotherapy, 4 cycles of carboplatin and etoposide. Response evaluation with rapid central review. Progressive disease is off protocol therapy. Progressive disease includes tumor markers at the end of chemotherapy (serum and/or CSF), or progressive disease and no second-look surgery, or viable tumor at second-look surgery. If second-look surgery reveals viable tumor, the patient is taken off protocol therapy.

schema.label: Callback via OPEN and stratum assignment
schema.text: After response evaluation, callback via OPEN assigns a stratum by site and response. Each stratum dose below is followed by a 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 1
arms.text: Localized radiographic CR with normalization of markers. Second-look surgery; mature teratoma or non-viable tumor. 12 Gy whole ventricular irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 2
arms.text: Localized radiographic PR with normalization of markers. No second-look surgery. 18 Gy whole ventricular irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 3
arms.text: Localized less than radiographic PR with normalization of markers. Second-look surgery (mature teratoma or non-viable tumor) or no second-look surgery. 24 Gy whole ventricular irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 4
arms.text: Metastatic CR. Second-look surgery; mature teratoma or non-viable tumor. 18 Gy craniospinal irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 5
arms.text: Metastatic less than radiographic CR with normalization of markers. No second-look surgery. 24 Gy craniospinal irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 6
arms.text: Basal ganglia or thalamic CR. Second-look surgery; mature teratoma or non-viable tumor. 18 Gy whole brain irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

arms.label: Stratum 7
arms.text: Basal ganglia or thalamic less than radiographic CR with normalization of markers. No second-look surgery. 24 Gy whole brain irradiation plus 12 Gy boost.

eligibility: Age >= 3 years and < 30 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed primary localized germinoma of the suprasellar and/or pineal region by pathology and/or serum and/or CSF hCGβ 5-50 mIU/mL and institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL if no institutional normal exists), including contiguous ventricular or unifocal parenchymal extension. Histologic confirmation is not required for this group.

Also eligible without histologic confirmation: bifocal (pineal plus suprasellar) disease, or a pineal lesion with diabetes insipidus, with hCGβ <= 100 mIU/mL in serum and/or CSF and institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL) in both serum and CSF.
hCGβ 51-100 mIU/mL in serum and/or CSF with institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL) in both serum and CSF requires histologic confirmation of germinoma.

Germinoma of the basal ganglia and/or thalamus is eligible. Metastatic germinoma, including non-contiguous or distant disease in the brain, ventricles, or spine, is eligible. Germinoma admixed with mature teratoma is eligible.
ECOG 0, 1, or 2. Karnofsky if > 16 years and Lansky if <= 16 years.

Rapid central imaging review and rapid central tumor marker review on APEC14B1-CNS must be available before ACNS2321 entry. Cranial MRI with and without gadolinium; pre-operative and post-operative MRI if resected, post-operative MRI within 72 hours (recommended but not required after biopsy only). Spine MRI with gadolinium. Imaging within 31 days before enrollment.

Lumbar CSF cytology before enrollment unless medically contraindicated, and not before the spine MRI. If not obtained at surgery, obtain it at least 10 days after surgery. CSF tumor markers before enrollment unless contraindicated; ventricular CSF at diversion is acceptable and lumbar CSF is preferred.

Serum AFP and hCGβ within 7 days. CSF markers and cytology within 31 days. Eligibility labs within 7 days. Protocol therapy must begin no later than 31 days after definitive surgery or clinical diagnosis, whichever is later.
For solid tumors: ANC >= 1000/µL, platelets >= 100,000/µL and transfusion independent, and hemoglobin >= 8.0 g/dL (RBC transfusion allowed).

Pediatric renal function (age 3-17 years): serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 3 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 17 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 70 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection. Creatinine within 28 days, actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, minimum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL used in the estimate, multiplied by 0.85 if female.
Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, and ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
No dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry > 94% if there is a clinical indication to measure it.
Seizures are allowed if on anticonvulsants and well controlled. CNS toxicity must be <= Grade 2. Patients must not be in status epilepticus, coma, or assisted ventilation.
HIV-infected patients on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load are eligible.

No malignant elements of endodermal sinus (yolk sac), embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, or malignant or immature teratoma and mixed germ cell tumor. No isolated mature teratoma with negative tumor markers. No prior tumor-directed therapy other than surgery and corticosteroids.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. Pregnancy tests may be falsely positive because of hCGβ-secreting tumors; confirm by institutional standards. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

studies.title: A Randomized Phase II Study of Sacituzumab Govitecan Alone, Ivonescimab Alone, or Sacituzumab Govitecan and Ivonescimab in Participants with Previously-Treated Actionable Genomic Alteration Positive Stage IV or Recurrent Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (Lung-MAP Sub-Study)

schema.label: Step 1: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Tissue for biomarker profiling or results from an approved biomarker test. SWOG SDMC assigns participants with an actionable genomic alteration (ALK, EGFR, HER2/ERBB2, MET, NTRK, RET, or ROS1) previously treated with targeted therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy to S1900N.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: EGFR driver mutation (yes vs no); brain metastases (yes vs no). Dynamic balancing.

schema.label: Step 2: S1900N randomization (3 arms)
schema.text: 35 eligible participants per arm (105 eligible, 117 enrolled). Treatment starts within 10 calendar days of randomization. 21-day cycles until progression or other removal criteria (any radiation therapy removes the participant from protocol treatment). Arm 1 has a safety run-in with weekly toxicity checks in Cycle 1.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV day 1, then (after at least 30 minutes of observation) sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8, every 21 days.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8, every 21 days.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV day 1, every 21 days.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after randomization, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS for Arm 1 vs Arm 2 and Arm 1 vs Arm 3; response rate (confirmed and unconfirmed, complete and partial) of each arm against historical single-agent chemotherapy.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900N by the SWOG SDMC based on stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with an actionable genomic alteration: an activating driver with an approved lung cancer targeted therapy in ALK, EGFR, HER2 (ERBB2), MET, NTRK, RET, or ROS1.
Prior appropriate targeted therapy for the alteration and prior platinum-based chemotherapy for stage IV or recurrent disease, with progression during or after the most recent systemic therapy.
No more than 3 prior lines of cytotoxic therapy (chemotherapy or antibody-drug conjugates) for NSCLC.
No prior TROP2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate or sacituzumab govitecan/SN-38-containing therapy, and no prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody.

No systemic lung cancer therapy within 21 days before randomization (oral agents within 10 days). Prior radiation therapy must be completed before randomization (7-day rule; see notes). No planned concurrent systemic lung cancer therapy.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity (except alopecia).

Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before randomization (non-measurable sites within 42 days). Effusions, ascites, or labs alone do not qualify. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before randomization. Brain metastases or cord compression allowed without residual neurologic dysfunction (unless no further recovery is expected and on weaning steroids, prednisone 10 mg daily or less); lesions needing local treatment must be treated and controlled and asymptomatic for at least 7 days after stereotactic radiation or 14 days after whole brain radiation.
No leptomeningeal disease requiring CNS-specific treatment before randomization or planned during the study.
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before randomization.

Unresectable disease not amenable to curative surgery or radiation, or recurrent or metastatic disease on imaging.
HER2-positive cohort: measurable or non-measurable disease (RECIST 1.1). HER2-low cohort: measurable disease.

ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL within 14 days (HER2-low cohort: no transfusion or G-CSF to meet this).

Toxicities from prior chemotherapy or palliative RT recovered to ≤ grade 1.

schema.text: Screening under the MYELOMATCH Master Screening and Reassessment Protocol; assigned to AL.6/MM1YA-CTG01 (Tier 1) by the MATCHBox Protocol Assignment Team.

schema.text: n = 153. Treatment starts within 7 working days of enrollment; WBC must be ≤ 25 x 10^9/L (< 25 x 10^9/L before venetoclax).

arms.text: One 28-day cycle: daunorubicin 60 mg/m2/day IV days 2-4; cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CI days 2-8; venetoclax ramp-up 50, 100, 200 mg days 1-3, then 400 mg days 4-11. arms.text: Two 28-day cycles: azacitidine 75 mg/m2/day IV or SC days 1-7 (or days 1-5 and 8-9); venetoclax cycle 1 ramp-up 100 mg day 1, 200 mg day 2, 400 mg days 3-28; cycle 2 400 mg days 1-28. Day 21 (± 3) marrow guides interruption for hypoplasia. No reinduction.

arms.label: Arm 3: 7+3
arms.text: One 28-day cycle: daunorubicin 60 mg/m2/day IV days 1-3; cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CI days 1-7. Optional day 14 marrow; reinduction (cytarabine days 1-5, daunorubicin days 1-2) if marrow > 20% cellular with ≥ 5% blasts.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Rate of undetectable MRD among patients achieving CR after induction, compared across 7+3, azacitidine + venetoclax, and 7+3 + venetoclax.

eligibility: Registered to MYELOMATCH and assigned to this study by the MATCHBox Protocol Assignment Team; diagnostic labs and marrow done under MYELOMATCH.
Previously untreated de novo AML (≥ 20% blasts in blood or marrow, current WHO) of modified intermediate risk.

Excluded subtypes: CBF-AML (t(8;21), inv(16), t(16;16)); biallelic CEBPA; NPM1 mutation; PML-RARA; any adverse cytogenetics, TP53, RUNX1, or ASXL1 mutation, or 11q23/KMT2A rearrangement; FLT3-ITD; therapy-related AML or AML after MDS or MPN.

No active uncontrolled bacterial, fungal, or viral infection or other serious illness compromising safety.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

studies.title: A Phase II Study of Venetoclax, Ibrutinib, Prednisone, Obinutuzumab, and Revlimid (ViPOR) in Relapsed or Refractory CD10-Negative Diffuse-Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 Rearrangements (HGBCL-DH-BCL2)

schema.label: Pre-registration testing
schema.text: CD10 IHC and/or FISH for MYC and BCL2 rearrangements before registration to confirm eligibility and assign cohort.

schema.text: Relapsed/refractory CD10-negative DLBCL (N=80).

schema.text: Relapsed/refractory HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements, CD10-positive or negative (N=40).

schema.label: Treatment (both cohorts): ViPOR
schema.text: 21-day cycles, maximum 6 cycles: venetoclax 800 mg PO daily days 2-14, ibrutinib 560 mg PO daily days 1-14, prednisone 100 mg PO daily days 1-7, obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV days 1 and 2, lenalidomide 15 mg PO daily days 1-14 (10 mg if CrCl 30-60 mL/min), with G-CSF prophylaxis (pegfilgrastim 6 mg SQ day 8 preferred). Inpatient start if high TLS risk.

schema.text: After cycles 2 and 6 (end of treatment).

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Clinical and imaging every 6 months for years 1-2, annual clinical evaluation years 3-5, survival contact through 10 years from registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Complete response rate of ViPOR in each cohort.

eligibility: Age >= 18 years; ECOG performance status 0-2.

Cohort 1: histologically or cytologically confirmed CD10-negative DLBCL (non-GCB or GCB DLBCL NOS, HGBCL-DH-BCL6 without BCL2, HGBCL NOS, or T-cell/histiocyte-rich LBCL). Cohort 2: CD10-positive or negative HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (with or without BCL6).
Relapsed and/or refractory disease after at least 1 prior anthracycline- and anti-CD20-containing regimen; measurable disease.
No more than 3 prior lines of cytotoxic chemotherapy (cytoreduction followed by ASCT or CAR-T counts as 1 line if no intervening progression).

No chemotherapy, targeted therapy, anti-cancer antibodies, ADCs, or bispecifics within 2 weeks; no radio- or toxin-immunoconjugates within 10 weeks. Short-course corticosteroids or palliative RT before registration allowed.
No prior treatment with more than one of: venetoclax (or other BCL2 inhibitor), ibrutinib (or other BTK inhibitor), lenalidomide (or other IMiD).
No ASCT, CAR-T, or allogeneic transplant within 3 months; no active GVHD or immunosuppressants within 28 days. Prior treatment toxicities recovered to <= grade 1 or baseline.
No confirmed or suspected primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma and no primary CNS lymphoma. Secondary CNS lymphoma allowed if post-treatment brain imaging shows no progression.

Labs within 7 days: ANC >= 1,000/mcL without G-CSF, Hgb >= 8 g/dL, platelets >= 75,000/mcL without transfusion, total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN (<= 3.0 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT <= 3.0 x ULN, creatinine <= 1.5 mg/dL or CrCl >= 30 mL/min.
No warfarin or strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers within 7 days before registration.
No active infection or uncontrolled intercurrent illness. Patients with cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it does not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Adequate FFPE tumor tissue (archival or new research biopsy) for mandatory molecular analysis.
Not pregnant and not nursing; lenalidomide pregnancy-prevention requirements apply (pregnancy test within 14 days and within 24 hours before cycle 1 day 1).

A Phase II Study of Tailored Adjuvant Therapy in Pole-Mutated and p53-Wildtype/ NSMP Early-Stage Endometrial Cancer (RAINBO BLUE & TAPER)

schema.label: US assignment
schema.text: This file is the NRG appendix to CCTG EN.10, not a randomized schema. US patients enroll to EN.10A, RAINBO BLUE, POLE-mutated, Cohort A1 only, or to EN.10B, TAPER, p53 wild type or NSMP. US sites do not participate in Cohort A2. Table 1 then assigns adjuvant management by stage and molecular group. This file plans 120 POLE-mutated Cohort A1 patients and 180 p53wt/NSMP patients, recruited in 3 years. Molecular results should allow protocol treatment or active surveillance within 10 weeks of hysterectomy and staging.

schema.label: Cohort A1, POLE-mutated
schema.text: Histotype may be endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated or dedifferentiated, carcinosarcoma, or mixed. LVI is none, focal if fewer than 3 foci, or substantial or extensive if 3 or more foci.

arms.label: Group A1.1
arms.text: Observation. Stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI.

arms.label: Group A1.2
arms.text: Observation. Stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI; or stage IB, grade 3, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI; or microscopic stage II, grade 1 or 2, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI.

arms.label: Group A1.3
arms.text: Observation. Stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with substantial or extensive LVI; or stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with substantial or extensive LVI.

schema.label: Sub-study B, p53wt/NSMP
schema.text: Endometrioid histology only, and ER positive. p53wt/NSMP carcinoma with MELF myoinvasion and/or substantial or extensive LVI is not eligible.

arms.label: Group B1
arms.text: Observation. Same stage group as A1.1: stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI.

arms.label: Group B2
arms.text: Vaginal brachytherapy. Same stage group as A1.2.

schema.label: Radiation doses, when radiation is given
schema.text: Table 1 assigns observation or vaginal brachytherapy to the groups above and does not assign pelvic EBRT to them. Section 10.1 still prints the NRG template. EBRT, when used, is IMRT to the upper vagina and pelvic nodes: 45 Gy in 25 daily fractions of 1.8 Gy, or 48.6 Gy in 27 daily fractions of 1.8 Gy. Brachytherapy alone: HDR 7.0 Gy x 3 prescribed at 0.5 cm depth (21 Gy), HDR 6.0 Gy x 5 to the surface (30 Gy), HDR 4.0 Gy x 6 to the surface (24 Gy), or PDR/LDR 60 Gy in 1 fraction to the surface. HDR boost after EBRT is 5.0 Gy x 2 to the surface, total EQD2 56.8 Gy after 45 Gy or 60.3 Gy after 48.6 Gy. PDR/LDR boost is 25 Gy in 1 fraction to the surface, total surface dose 70 Gy after 45 Gy or 73.6 Gy after 48.6 Gy. Per protocol, EBRT starts 6-8 weeks after surgery, with 4-12 weeks acceptable. The appendix says full sub-study details are in the master protocol.

eligibility: Complete molecular classification is required before inclusion, on the hysterectomy specimen or the preoperative specimen: POLE exonuclease-domain mutation status, MMR immunohistochemistry, ER immunohistochemistry, and p53 immunohistochemistry or TP53 sequencing, reported by an accredited laboratory. NGS is acceptable when those data are available in time for protocol treatment within 10 weeks of surgical staging.
US sites enroll only EN.10A Cohort A1, RAINBO BLUE, for POLE-mutated cancer, or EN.10B, TAPER, for p53 wild type or NSMP cancer. US sites will not participate in Cohort A2.
POLE-mutated histotypes may be endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated or dedifferentiated, carcinosarcoma, or mixed. p53wt/NSMP disease must be endometrioid and ER positive.

Eligible stage groups are those in Table 1: stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with no or focal LVI; stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with no or focal LVI; stage IB, grade 3, pN0, with no or focal LVI; microscopic stage II, grade 1 or 2, pN0, with no or focal LVI; and, for POLE-mutated Cohort A1 only, stage IA grade 3 pN0 or stage IB grade 1 or 2 pNx or pN0 with substantial or extensive LVI.

p53wt/NSMP endometrial carcinoma with a MELF pattern of myoinvasion and/or substantial or extensive lymphovascular invasion is not eligible. Focal LVI is fewer than 3 foci. Substantial or extensive LVI is 3 or more foci.
HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.

amendments.text: Revision 2, the current version. Expanded the safety run-in description, added a hierarchical MRD-negative CR primary objective, broadened the AML definition to WHO AML-defining genetic abnormalities, merged prior-therapy criteria, added a CNS criterion, updated treatment tables and MRD assessment, and combined the Cycle 6 and pre-transplant specimen timepoints.

schema.label: myeloMATCH registration
schema.text: Master screening protocol testing; central confirmation of an IDH2 mutation and assignment to this substudy.

schema.label: MM1OA-S03 registration
schema.text: Newly diagnosed IDH2-mutant AML in adults ≥ 60 or unfit adults ≥ 18. Treatment starts within 14 days.

schema.label: Safety phase
schema.text: First 6 participants non-randomly assigned to Arm 2 and monitored for toxicity through 2 cycles before randomization opens.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Age (< 70 vs ≥ 70); performance status (0-1 vs 2-3), dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 28-day cycles until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or allogeneic transplant.

arms.label: Arm 1 (control)
arms.text: ASTX727 (oral decitabine 35 mg/cedazuridine 100 mg) 1 tablet Days 1-5 + venetoclax 400 mg PO daily (Cycle 1 ramp-up 100 mg Day 1, 200 mg Day 2, 400 mg Days 3-28).

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: ASTX727 + venetoclax as in Arm 1 + enasidenib 100 mg PO Days 1-28.

schema.label: Disease assessment
schema.text: Bone marrow after Cycles 2, 4, and 6 (or before transplant). A new myeloMATCH assignment may be requested after the primary endpoint is reached.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Safety of Arm 2 in the run-in; then rate of MRD-negative (multiparameter flow) CR or CRh after 2 cycles, with hierarchical comparison of MRD-negative CR if significant.

eligibility: Registered to the myeloMATCH master protocol with an IDH2 mutation on central testing and assigned to this substudy via MATCHBox.
Newly diagnosed, untreated AML (≥ 20% blasts in marrow or blood, or a WHO AML-defining genetic abnormality); APL with PML-RARA excluded.

Bisphosphonates are allowed for bone metastases. No unresolved CTCAE grade 2 or higher toxicity from prior anticancer therapy, except alopecia and vitiligo.

Step 1 clinical: age 18 or older, able to receive platinum, etoposide, and durvalumab, and Zubrod 0-2 within 28 days. Recovered from prior surgery in the investigator's opinion. No allogeneic organ transplant. No contraindication to immunotherapy, including non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids or active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past two years. Replacement therapy such as thyroxine or insulin is allowed.

Step 1: not pregnant or nursing. People of reproductive potential use effective contraception during protocol therapy and for 6 months after, and do not breastfeed during therapy and for 6 months after.

Step 1 tissue: adequate small cell lung cancer tissue for BostonGene per section 15.2, with leftover tissue kept for future studies. After Step 1, submit tissue to BostonGene. Measurable or non-measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, assessed by CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 28 days if measurable or within 42 days if non-measurable. All known sites are documented. A non-diagnostic PET/CT makes those lesions non-measurable.

Step 2 brain: CT or MRI of the brain within 42 days. No leptomeningeal disease, spinal cord compression, or symptomatic brain metastases unless the metastases were locally treated, have stayed clinically controlled and asymptomatic for at least 14 days, there is no residual neurological dysfunction, and corticosteroids have been stopped for at least 24 hours. Untreated brain metastases must be asymptomatic and stable off steroids. Allowed steroid exceptions are intranasal, inhaled, topical, or local injection; physiologic doses up to 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent; and steroid premedication.

Step 2 therapy: no progression during induction in the treating investigator's opinion. Frontline induction of 4-6 cycles of platinum plus etoposide with durvalumab is complete, and Step 2 is no more than 8 weeks after the last induction dose. No atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, or prophylactic cranial irradiation.

Step 2 infection history: known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy and an undetectable viral load within 6 months. Known chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load.

eligibility: Age ≥18, Zubrod PS 0-2.

Measurable disease by PET-CT (preferred) or CT (extranodal ≥1 cm or nodal ≥1.5 cm); splenic MZL eligible if spleen SUV > liver background and/or spleen >13 cm. Staging imaging within 42 days.

Needs systemic therapy: symptomatic or bulky nodal disease, organ-threatening progression, B symptoms, symptomatic extranodal disease, cytopenias from marrow infiltration or hypersplenism, or accelerating tempo.

Relapsed/refractory after ≥1 prior CD20-directed systemic therapy; prior antibiotics or radiation for localized MZL allowed and do not count as a line.
Prior BTK inhibitor or CD3/CD20 bispecific allowed only if completed ≥180 days before registration with best response PR or CR. No prior polatuzumab vedotin.
No CAR-T within 28 days, autologous SCT within 100 days, or allogeneic SCT within 180 days; no active GVHD needing ≥10 mg prednisone; no active PTLD.

No warfarin or other vitamin K antagonist within 7 days; no severe bleeding disorder or spontaneous bleeding needing intervention; no stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 180 days.
No history of PML; no uncontrolled AIHA or ITP; no uncontrolled intercurrent illness (infection, autoimmune disease, arrhythmia, angina, neuropathy, hypertension, malabsorption).
NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.

HIV allowed with effective ART and undetectable viral load within 180 days; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy (HBcAb-positive patients need antiviral prophylaxis); HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No live or attenuated vaccine within 28 days. No severe allergy to compounds similar to the study agents.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

studies.title: A Randomized Phase III Study Comparing Temporally-Modulated Pulsed Radiation Therapy (TMPRT) Versus Standard Radiation Therapy with Temozolomide for Adults with Newly Diagnosed MGMT-Unmethylated Glioblastoma

amendments.text: Initial protocol.
Pre-activation revision, the latest date in the document history. The opening pages do not summarize what changed.

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Register for central pathology review confirming glioblastoma histology and unmethylated MGMT promoter status, and for central review that baseline neurocognitive scores are in range. Tumor tissue must be received and central review completed, and all neurocognitive tests completed, before Step 2.

schema.label: Step 2
schema.text: Stratify by RPA class (III versus IV versus V), radiation fractionation intent (conventional 6000 cGy in 30 fractions versus hypofractionated 4000 cGy in 15 fractions), and intent to use tumor treating fields (yes versus no). Randomize 1:1. No more than 50% of randomized patients may be younger than 65. Age is part of RPA class and is not its own stratification factor. RPA III is age under 50 and KPS 90-100. RPA IV is age under 50 with KPS under 90, or age 50 or older with KPS 70-100 and no worse than minor neurologic impairment. RPA V is age 50 or older with KPS 70-100 and worse than minor neurologic impairment. Protocol treatment starts within 8 weeks after surgery. Primary endpoint is time to neurocognitive failure.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard photon RT, 6000 cGy at 200 cGy per day for 30 fractions or 4000 cGy at 267 cGy per day for 15 fractions, with temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during RT, then adjuvant temozolomide 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles. Tumor treating fields may start in the adjuvant phase after the post-concurrent brain MRI.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Temporally modulated pulsed RT at the same total dose and daily dose as Arm 1. Each daily treatment is 10-13 pulses of 20 cGy with a 3-minute interval between pulses. Concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide, and tumor treating fields, are the same as Arm 1.

eligibility: Step 1: Age 18 or older, Karnofsky performance status at least 70, and proficient in English or French Canadian, with no known IDH mutation, and a patient already known to have an IDH mutation on local or other testing is ineligible and should not be registered.

Surgical resection is required, stereotactic biopsy alone is not allowed, and an FFPE tumor block and H&E slide must be shipped to the NYU Center for Biospecimen Research and Development on or before postoperative calendar day 30 for central histology and MGMT promoter review.

If that tissue cannot ship by postoperative day 30, the patient may not enroll, because treatment must start no later than 8 weeks after surgery, and after a further resection the tissue must ship within 30 days of the most recent resection, which itself must be within 30 days of the initial resection.

Not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before Step 1 for a person of childbearing potential, and no known leptomeningeal disease or metastatic disease outside the brain.

Hemoglobin at least 10 g/dL, with transfusion or another intervention allowed, leukocytes at least 2,000/mm3 or ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min, total bilirubin at or under 1.5 x institutional ULN, and AST and ALT at or under 3 x ULN.
No prior cranial radiation that would overlap treatment fields, and no previous therapy for glioblastoma except surgery, laser interstitial thermal therapy, or a Gliadel wafer.
ALA-mediated fluorescence-guided resection, photodynamic therapy, or fluorescein given to aid resection is allowed and is not counted as chemotherapy or an intracerebral agent.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization in the last 3 months, no myocardial infarction within the last 3 months, and NYHA class III or IV is not eligible (class II or better is required).

No active infection currently requiring intravenous antibiotics, no COPD exacerbation or other acute respiratory illness precluding study therapy, no movement disorder that would prevent lying still in an immobilization mask for about 40 minutes, no significant sensory deficit such as blindness or mutism that would prohibit neurocognitive testing, and no history of allergic reaction to temozolomide or a related compound such as dacarbazine.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible, chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated, hepatitis C must have been treated and cured or current treatment must have an undetectable viral load, and a prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Step 2: Central review must confirm IDH-wildtype glioblastoma with an unmethylated MGMT promoter, standard-of-care IDH testing by at least one method such as immunohistochemistry for IDH1 R132H must show no mutation, and insufficient or inadequate tissue, failed MGMT testing, or an indeterminate or methylated MGMT promoter is excluded.

Baseline HVLT-R, Trail Making Test, and COWA within 28 days before Step 2 must meet HVLT-R Total Recall greater than 5, Delayed Recall greater than 3, Delayed Recognition greater than -10, Trail Making Test Part A at or under 2738, Part B at or under 3724, and COWA at least 12, and scores outside those ranges are excluded.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

After neoadjuvant therapy (cisplatin-based, cisplatin plus PD-1/PD-L1, or enfortumab vedotin plus PD-1/PD-L1), ypT2-T4N0/Nx or ypTanyN+.
Signatera pathway: commercial result from blood drawn 3-16 weeks after surgery (16-target, exome-designed assay), or central testing with samples submitted 3-12 weeks after surgery.

Not on hemodialysis. No current or prior myocarditis.
No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event with prior neoadjuvant PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.

No active or recurrence-prone autoimmune disease that may affect vital organs or require immunosuppression (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, replaced endocrinopathies allowed). No pneumonitis requiring steroids within 5 years.

No active HBV or HCV. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment. HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No concurrent antineoplastic or anti-hormonal cancer therapy. No steroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression within 14 days of pre-registration.

Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment. Not pregnant and not nursing.
