studies.title: A Pragmatic Randomized Phase II Trial Evaluating Total Ablative Therapy for Patients with Limited Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Evaluating Radiation, Ablation, and Surgery (ERASur)

schema.label: Initial systemic therapy
schema.text: Newly diagnosed limited metastatic colorectal cancer receives physician-choice systemic therapy for at least 12 weeks and at most 52 weeks before registration. A 5-FU cycle is 14 days, a capecitabine cycle is 14 or 21 days, and a total-ablative-therapy cycle is 90 days. Patients may pre-register before or during that chemotherapy, or pre-register and register together after 12 weeks.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Institutional standard-of-care therapy before progression, including added systemic therapy, maintenance, a treatment pause, or restart, counts as on-protocol treatment. Patients are followed for 5 years or until death. Surgery, microwave ablation, and radiotherapy of metastatic sites are done at the registering institution. Chemotherapy may be given elsewhere.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Total ablative therapy, then institutional standard-of-care therapy. Total ablative therapy may be SBRT, microwave ablation, surgical resection, or any combination.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Institutional standard-of-care therapy, which may include more systemic therapy, maintenance chemotherapy, or a treatment pause, as the treating physician decides.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival from randomization, comparing total ablative therapy plus standard-of-care systemic therapy with standard-of-care systemic therapy in newly diagnosed oligometastatic colorectal cancer.

eligibility: Step 0 requires pathologically proven colorectal adenocarcinoma with metastases, from a primary or metastatic biopsy, with no known microsatellite instability and no known BRAF V600E mutation.

Treated brain metastases are allowed if follow-up brain imaging shows no progression, known peritoneal or omental metastases are excluded, and liver-only disease on baseline imaging before chemotherapy is not allowed.
Patients with liver metastases must have at least one other metastatic site on initial imaging, and they remain eligible if later imaging after systemic therapy shows liver-only disease.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 is required at pre-registration and at registration.
Step 1 requires no overt progression during pre-registration systemic therapy, and the patient is not eligible for hepatic artery infusion pump therapy or the benefit of that therapy is undefined.

The primary tumor is already resected, a rectal primary has had a clinical complete response without resection and no local regrowth, or a surgeon or multidisciplinary tumor board judges the primary resectable; an unresectable primary is not eligible.

After at least 12 weeks of systemic therapy there are 4 or fewer apparent metastatic sites, not counting the primary or regional nodes, each radiographically evident and amenable to resection, microwave ablation, SABR, or a combination.

One site means each hemiliver, each lung lobe, each adrenal gland, nodes treatable in one resection or one SABR field, or bone metastases treatable in one SABR field, and lung nodules smaller than 5 mm count as metastases unless they were stable for more than 2 months before systemic therapy.

First-line systemic therapy for metastatic disease lasts at least 12 weeks and at most 52 weeks, and prior definitive therapy, including adjuvant chemotherapy, must have finished at least 6 months before the metastatic diagnosis.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 0-2, and patients are not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

Labs are ANC at least 1,000/mm3, platelets at least 50,000/mm3, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or Cockcroft-Gault clearance at least 30 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN, and AST or ALT at most 3.0 x ULN, or at most 5 x ULN with metastatic liver disease.
In Gilbert disease, direct bilirubin replaces total bilirubin and must be at most 1.5 ULN if FOLFIRI is planned and at most 3.0 x ULN if mFOLFOX6 is planned.

Patients with known cardiac disease, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy should be class 2B or better, a prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it would not interfere with assessment, HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is allowed without required HIV testing, and no other concurrent investigational agent is planned.

schema.label: Step 1: Screening and initial treatment
schema.text: Confirmed de novo stage IV oligometastatic (5 or fewer lesions) HER2-positive breast cancer. Physician's choice of NCCN/ASCO guideline-concordant systemic therapy for 12-24 weeks. One week is seven calendar days. Preferred regimens are those used for stage III disease.

schema.label: Step 2: Cohort assignment
schema.text: Response per section 5.2 is assigned to Cohort A and randomized 1:1. Progression or no response per section 5.2 is assigned to Cohort B.

schema.label: Cohort A randomization
schema.text: After randomization, continue NCCN/ASCO concordant systemic therapy to complete at least 1 year. Preferred regimens are those used for residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Definitive locoregional therapy to the breast and lymph nodes plus SRT to all metastatic sites, per section 7.2.a.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: No surgery or radiation unless required for palliation, per section 7.2.b.

schema.label: Cohort B
schema.text: Physician's choice of NCCN/ASCO guideline-concordant HER2-directed systemic therapy, continued for at least 1 year or until disease progression, then follow-up.

eligibility: Step 1, disease: histologically confirmed de novo metastatic (AJCC stage IV, no prior breast cancer) HER2-positive breast cancer with 1 to 5 distant lesions. Confirm metastasis by biopsy of a distant site unless biopsy is not feasible or safe, in which case imaging and laboratory studies must show unequivocal metastasis. Confirm HER2 in the breast tumor and a metastatic site per NCCN guidelines version 4.2025. If bone HER2 is equivocal, or biopsy is not feasible or safe, breast-tumor HER2 is acceptable. If there is no breast lesion, confirm HER2 in at least one metastatic site.

Step 1, brain metastases are allowed when there are 5 or fewer intracranial lesions and each is no larger than 2 cm. The brain counts as one distant site. Brain imaging is not required without neurological symptoms, but symptom assessment and brain MRI are encouraged. No known leptomeningeal disease.

Step 1, prior therapy: either treatment-naive and planning to start standard HER2-targeted therapy, or already started it and completed at least 1 and no more than 3 cycles without progression. Baseline scans within 28 days before treatment starts.

Step 1: no investigational systemic therapy before disease progression. No whole-brain irradiation. Up to five brain metastases may have received SRS or SRT before or after systemic therapy starts. Small asymptomatic lesions may be observed if the regimen has CNS penetration.

Step 1, clinical: age 18 or older and Zubrod performance status 0-2. Known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy and an undetectable viral load within 6 months. Able to receive the physician's choice of standard HER2-targeted therapy per the package insert, physician judgment, and institutional guidelines.

Step 1: a candidate for definitive surgery and radiotherapy of locoregional disease, and able to receive ablative SRT to every metastatic lesion identified at baseline, in the treating physician's opinion.
Step 1: offered optional specimen banking (non-US sites are exempt). Informed consent is required. A legally authorized representative may consent when decision-making is impaired.

Step 2, Cohort A: register within 14 days of the staging scans done after Step 1. Those scans and breast imaging follow 12-24 weeks (at least 4 cycles) of initial systemic therapy and are within 14 days before Step 2. Use the same imaging modality as Step 1.

Step 2, Cohort A response: partial or complete response in the breast in the treating physician's opinion. A breast lesion at diagnosis needs a clinical response on breast imaging. Metastatic lesions are at least stable by RECIST and bone criteria. Brain metastases treated with SRS or SRT are at least stable by RANO-BM and do not require steroids. If there was no breast lesion at diagnosis, metastatic sites must show at least a partial response.

Step 2, Cohort A local therapy: still eligible for definitive surgery and radiotherapy of locoregional disease, and every metastatic lesion can receive ablative SRT. A lung lesion that resolves completely is not targeted, because dose buildup is not possible. A new sclerotic bone lesion after systemic therapy is not called progression, and such lesions are targeted with SRT.

Step 2, Cohort B: register within 14 days of staging and breast imaging after 12-24 weeks (at least 4 cycles), using the same modality as Step 1. Assignment requires stable disease or progression: progression in metastases by RECIST or bone criteria, or stable metastases with progression or no clinical response in the breast.

schema.text: Post-menarchal female < 40 years, newly diagnosed first cancer (not breast carcinoma), with planned curative alkylating-agent chemotherapy. Cancer treatment itself is at the treating oncologist's discretion.

arms.text: Triptorelin 22.5 mg IM once, preferably before chemotherapy (up to 14 days before and no later than 7 days after starting systemic chemotherapy). Optional second dose 24 weeks later if alkylator-based chemotherapy exceeds 24 weeks.

arms.label: Arm B: no triptorelin
arms.text: Chemotherapy without any GnRH agonist.

schema.label: Study measures

schema.label: Primary aims
schema.text: Feasibility of a cross-network randomized trial of triptorelin in AYA females, and ovarian reserve by AMH 2 years after completion of alkylator-containing chemotherapy.

eligibility: Age < 40 years at enrollment; post-menarchal female with first menses > 6 months before enrollment.
Newly diagnosed first cancer, excluding breast carcinoma (other tumor types arising in the breast, such as sarcoma or lymphoma, are allowed).

Planned curative therapy including at least one alkylator (cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, procarbazine, chlorambucil, carmustine, lomustine, melphalan, thiotepa, busulfan, nitrogen mustard, or dacarbazine), with alkylator therapy expected to finish within 1 year of enrollment.

Age < 20: expected cumulative cyclophosphamide equivalent dose ≥ 4 g/m2 (dacarbazine does not count). Age 20 to < 35: any dose of a CED-contributing alkylator. Age ≥ 35: any CED alkylator dose and/or dacarbazine.
No planned or prior radiation to the pelvis, no cranial radiation ≥ 30 Gy to the hypothalamus, and no TBI.
No planned bilateral oophorectomy (embryo, oocyte, or ovarian tissue cryopreservation is allowed and encouraged).
No congenital syndrome with infertility or reduced ovarian reserve (for example Turner syndrome, Fragile X premutation, Down syndrome).
No seizure disorder, congenital long QT, pseudotumor cerebri, or history of pulmonary embolism, venous thrombosis, or MI.
No depot GnRH agonist within 6 months (short-acting GnRH agonist for oocyte retrieval and hormonal contraception are allowed).
No systemic chemotherapy started more than 7 days before enrollment (steroids and intrathecal chemotherapy excepted).
Not pregnant, and not breastfeeding during triptorelin therapy (24 weeks per dose).

schema.text: Newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 2018 stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC1, IIIC2, or IVA.

schema.text: FIGO stage III versus IVA, and presence or absence of para-aortic nodes (N2). Randomize 1:1.

schema.text: Concurrent chemoradiation: weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for 5 weeks, external-beam radiotherapy, brachytherapy, and pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 5 cycles, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for 14 maintenance cycles.

schema.text: Induction weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 for 6 weeks, plus pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 2 cycles, then the same chemoradiation and pembrolizumab, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for 15 maintenance cycles.

eligibility: Pathologically confirmed newly diagnosed cervical squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma.
Locally advanced disease: FIGO 2018 IIIA (T3aN0), IIIB (T3bN0), IIIC1 (T3aN1 or T3bN1), IIIC2 (T3aN2 or T3bN2), or IVA (T4aN0-N2).

No prior hysterectomy, defined as removal of the entire uterus. A prior partial hysterectomy for a reason other than cervical cancer may be allowed. No plan for hysterectomy as part of initial therapy.
No para-aortic node metastasis above the T12/L1 interspace. Node status may be confirmed by imaging or biopsy, as the protocol specifies.
No prior definitive surgery, radiation, or systemic therapy for cervical cancer. No prior immunotherapy. No prior pelvic radiotherapy for any disease.
ECOG performance status 2 or better. Not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit, AST and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit.
No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics. No live vaccine within 30 days. No immunodeficiency and no chronic systemic steroid therapy, as defined in the protocol.

No active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment in the past 2 years. No history of non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids, and no current pneumonitis. No allergic reaction to the study agents or similar compounds.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Adjuvant therapy for pathologic high-risk squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. Use the phase III schema. The phase II schema is marked complete.

schema.label: Step 1 registration
schema.text: For oropharyngeal primaries only, mandatory p16 analysis is required before Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Step 2 registration
schema.text: Stratify by Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1) and primary site (oral cavity vs larynx vs hypopharynx vs p16-negative oropharynx). Randomize to Arm 1, Arm 3, and Arm 4 in a 1:1:2 ratio. Arm 2 was dropped after phase II. Required phase III sample size: 480 randomized patients. Protocol treatment must begin within 14 days after Step 2.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Radiation plus cisplatin. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks (2 Gy x 30 fractions) and cisplatin 40 mg/m2 intravenously weekly for 6 doses.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Radiation plus docetaxel plus cetuximab. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks, cetuximab loading dose 400 mg/m2 then 250 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses, and docetaxel 15 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses. The loading dose is given 4 to 8 days before the first radiation and docetaxel, with no radiation or docetaxel on the loading day.

arms.label: Arm 4
arms.text: Radiation plus cisplatin plus atezolizumab. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks, cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses concurrent with radiation, and atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks at week -1 (before radiation) and at weeks 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, and 21.

schema.label: Radiation details
schema.text: IMRT is mandatory. Proton therapy is not permitted. IGRT is optional unless reduced margins are used, in which case IGRT is mandatory. PTV_6000 is 60 Gy in 30 fractions. PTV_5600, where used, is 56 Gy in 30 fractions (1.87 Gy). An optional integrated boost, PTV_6600, is 66 Gy in 30 fractions (2.2 Gy). A sequential 3D conformal 6 Gy boost is not permitted.

eligibility: Pathologically proven head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity (lips excluded), p16-negative oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx.
Oropharyngeal cancer must be p16-negative on central review before Step 2. Every oropharyngeal primary must consent to mandatory tissue submission for central p16 confirmation.

Gross total surgical resection of the high-risk primary within 63 days before registration. A biopsy under general anesthesia followed by definitive ablative surgery is allowed if that gross total resection is within 63 days. Re-resection for short-interval recurrence or persisting disease after an ablative resection is not eligible.
At least one high-risk pathologic feature: extracapsular nodal extension, or invasive cancer at the primary resection margin (tumor on ink, or tumor in a final separately submitted margin).

Pathologic stage III or IV by AJCC 7th edition, with no distant metastases. History and physical examination by a radiation oncologist or medical oncologist within 84 days before registration. Examination by an ENT or head and neck surgeon before surgery. Laryngopharyngoscopy is recommended but not required. An intraoperative examination is acceptable documentation.

Preoperative head and neck imaging within 84 days before surgery: diagnostic-quality contrast neck CT, or diagnostic-quality contrast PET/CT, and/or diagnostic-quality neck MRI (T1 with gadolinium and T2). The scan is submitted in DICOM via TRIAD and the report is uploaded to Rave. Chest CT or PET/CT that includes the chest, with or without contrast, either within 84 days before surgery or within 120 days before registration.
Zubrod performance status 0 or 1 within 14 days before registration. Age 18 or older. Patients with feeding tubes are eligible.

CBC within 14 days: leukocytes at least 2,500 cells/mm3, absolute neutrophil count at least 1,500 cells/mm3, platelets at least 100,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention is allowed).

Hepatic function within 14 days: total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal (Gilbert disease may be enrolled at or below 3 times that limit), AST or ALT at or below 3 times that limit, and alkaline phosphatase at or below 2.5 times that limit.

Creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min within 14 days, by 24-hour collection or Cockcroft-Gault. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days for women of childbearing potential. Study-specific informed consent is required before entry.

HIV-positive patients are allowed with a stable HAART regimen, no requirement for concurrent antibiotics or antifungals to prevent opportunistic infections, a CD4 count above 250 cells/mcL, and an undetectable HIV viral load on standard PCR-based tests.

Step 1 is registration. Step 2 is randomization. Oropharynx patients complete Step 2 after central p16 results. Oral cavity, hypopharynx, and larynx patients may complete Step 2 after the Step 1 confirmation email. Protocol treatment starts within 14 days after Step 2.

No prior invasive malignancy unless disease-free for at least 1,095 days (3 years), except non-melanoma skin cancer and resected T1-2 N0 M0 differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Noninvasive cancers, for example carcinoma in situ of the breast, oral cavity, or cervix, are allowed even if diagnosed and treated within 3 years.
Simultaneous primaries or bilateral tumors are excluded, except bilateral tonsil cancers and the resected differentiated thyroid carcinoma exception above.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer, including cytotoxic chemotherapy, biologic or targeted therapy such as anti-EGF therapy, or immune therapy. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed, but a prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent is not permitted. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap fields.

Patients with known or current cardiac disease, or prior cardiotoxic agents, must be New York Heart Association class 2B or better within 6 months before registration. No transmural myocardial infarction within 6 months.

No severe infection within 4 weeks before registration, including hospitalization for infection, bacteremia, or severe pneumonia. No acute bacterial or fungal infection requiring intravenous antibiotics at registration. Prophylactic antibiotics, for example for urinary infection or COPD, are allowed. No COPD exacerbation or other respiratory illness requiring hospitalization or precluding study therapy at registration.

No history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, pneumonitis including drug-induced pneumonitis, organizing pneumonia, or active pneumonitis on the screening chest CT. Radiation fibrosis in a prior field is allowed if that field does not overlap the planned study field. Active tuberculosis is excluded.

No known clinically significant liver disease, including active viral, alcoholic, or other hepatitis, cirrhosis, fatty liver, or inherited liver disease. Past or resolved hepatitis B (HBsAg negative and anti-HBc positive) is eligible. HCV antibody is eligible only if PCR is negative for HCV RNA. No allogeneic bone marrow transplant or solid organ transplant. AIDS, by the current CDC definition, is excluded. HIV testing is not required.

No systemic immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks before registration, including prednisone, cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, methotrexate, thalidomide, and anti-TNF agents. A one-time low dose, such as dexamethasone for nausea, is allowed. Inhaled corticosteroids and mineralocorticoids for orthostatic hypotension or adrenocortical insufficiency are allowed.

History or risk of autoimmune disease is excluded, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, antiphospholipid thrombosis, Wegener granulomatosis, Sjogren syndrome, Guillain-Barre syndrome, multiple sclerosis, vasculitis, and glomerulonephritis. Exceptions: asymptomatic autoimmune hypothyroidism and/or a stable thyroid replacement dose, controlled type 1 diabetes on stable insulin, and eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo limited to the skin if psoriasis has a baseline eye exam excluding ocular disease, rash covers less than 10 percent of body surface area, disease is controlled on low-potency topical steroids only, and there has been no acute exacerbation within 12 months requiring PUVA, methotrexate, retinoids, biologic agents, oral calcineurin inhibitors, or high-potency or oral steroids. Psoriatic arthritis is excluded.

No grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormality (CTCAE v4) within 14 days that persists despite intervention: calcium below 7 mg/dL or above 12.5 mg/dL, glucose below 40 mg/dL or above 250 mg/dL, magnesium below 0.9 mg/dL or above 3 mg/dL, potassium below 3.0 mmol/L or above 6 mmol/L, or sodium below 130 mmol/L or above 155 mmol/L.

Pregnancy is excluded. Women of childbearing potential and sexually active men who are unwilling or unable to use medically acceptable contraception for up to 5 months after the last study treatment are excluded. Women who are breastfeeding and unwilling to discontinue are excluded.

No history of severe allergic, anaphylactic, or other hypersensitivity reactions to chimeric or humanized antibodies or fusion proteins. No prior allergic reaction to cisplatin, docetaxel, cetuximab, or atezolizumab. No known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or other recombinant human antibodies.

Bisphosphonate therapy for symptomatic hypercalcemia is excluded. Use for other reasons, such as osteoporosis, is allowed. A RANKL inhibitor such as denosumab for a non-oncologic reason must be discontinued before registration if the patient cannot stop it. Known distant metastatic disease is excluded.

No major surgical procedure within 28 days before registration, and no anticipated need for a major surgical procedure during the study. This exclusion does not apply to the cancer resection in section 3.2.3. No live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks before registration, during the study, or, for patients receiving atezolizumab, until 5 months after the last atezolizumab dose. Live attenuated influenza vaccine is not allowed within 4 weeks before registration or at any time during the study. Psychiatric illness or social situations that would limit compliance are excluded.

studies.title: A Randomized Phase III Study of Pirtobrutinib Plus R-CHOP vs. R-CHOP for Participants with Previously Untreated Richter Transformation (PIRAMID)

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Previously untreated Richter transformation of CLL/SLL to large B-cell lymphoma.

schema.label: Safety run-in (Arm 1, non-randomized)
schema.text: 6 participants <75 and 6 participants ≥75 assigned to pirtobrutinib plus R-CHOP or R-mini-CHOP, monitored for toxicity through cycle 2. Randomization opens for each age cohort by memo once its run-in is complete.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior progression on a covalent BTK inhibitor (yes vs no) and age (<75 vs ≥75).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles x6; R-mini-CHOP for age ≥75. G-CSF prophylaxis every cycle. Treatment starts within 7 days.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Pirtobrutinib 200 mg PO daily plus R-CHOP (rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1.4 mg/m² max 2 mg day 1, prednisone 100 mg days 1-5) for cycles 1-6, then pirtobrutinib maintenance until progression, up to 5 years. Age ≥75: cyclophosphamide 400 mg/m², doxorubicin 25 mg/m², vincristine 1 mg, prednisone 40 mg/m².

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: R-CHOP (or R-mini-CHOP for age ≥75) for cycles 1-6, then off protocol treatment.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 7 years after registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Safety run-in: safety. Randomized: investigator-assessed PFS, then OS by hierarchical testing.

eligibility: Age ≥18, ECOG/Zubrod PS 0-2.
Richter transformation (CLL/SLL to LBCL) with histologically or cytologically confirmed LBCL.
Measurable disease by PET/CT or hematopathology (morphology or flow) and staging PET/CT within 42 days before registration.

Prior CLL/SLL therapy allowed except pirtobrutinib. No prior treatment for Richter transformation except corticosteroids up to prednisone 700 mg total for <7 days; CLL-directed drugs after RT diagnosis allowed for disease control (targeted agents stopped 3 days and chemotherapy or anti-CD20 stopped 2 weeks before protocol therapy).
No contraindication to anthracycline; prior doxorubicin-equivalent ≤100 mg/m² for R-CHOP or ≤250 mg/m² for R-mini-CHOP.
No required strong CYP3A inducer unless an alternative exists and the last dose is ≥7 days before pirtobrutinib.

Labs within 28 days: ANC ≥0.75 x 10^3/µL (≥0.50 with marrow involvement), platelets ≥50 x 10^3/µL (≥30 with marrow involvement), hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL (≥6 with marrow involvement), total bilirubin ≤1.5x ULN (≤3x with liver involvement or Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤3x ULN (≤5x with liver involvement), creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min.
LVEF ≥45% by echocardiogram or MUGA within 56 days; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.
No major bleeding event or grade ≥3 arrhythmia on prior BTK inhibitor therapy.
No major surgery within 28 days.
Able to swallow oral medication with no GI disorder likely to impair absorption.

HIV allowed with effective ART (no pirtobrutinib interactions) and undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No other prior or concurrent malignancy (beyond CLL/SLL and Richter transformation) that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Must agree to required blood and lymph node tissue submission for the integrated translational study.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

The NEO-RT Trial: A Phase 3 Randomized Trial of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy, Excision and Observation Versus ChemoRadioTherapy for Early Rectal Cancer

schema.label: Population
schema.text: International multicenter phase 3 randomized non-inferiority trial of induction FOLFOX or CAPOX followed by transanal endoscopic surgery, compared with chemoradiation followed by transanal endoscopic surgery, for cT1 to T3ab N0 mismatch-repair-proficient rectal adenocarcinoma. T3a is invasion less than 1 mm. T3b is invasion of 1 to 5 mm.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Centre. T stage (T1 vs T2/T3ab). Sex (male vs female).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The schema page does not print a randomization ratio. Planned sample size is 250 patients.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Six cycles of modified FOLFOX, or four cycles of CAPOX. Modified FOLFOX is leucovorin 400 mg/m2, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, optional bolus fluorouracil 400 mg, and infusional fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m2. CAPOX is capecitabine 1,000 mg/m2 twice daily for 14 days and oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Chemoradiation, 54 Gy in 27 to 30 fractions, with a standard dose of infusional 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine. The schema does not print that chemotherapy milligram dose.

schema.label: Restaging at 14 to 16 weeks
schema.text: MRI, endoscopy, and digital rectal examination, then response-directed surgery.

schema.label: Clinical complete response
schema.text: Transanal endoscopic surgery within 8 weeks, then shared decision-making about subsequent therapy (section 7.5) and follow-up until the earlier of 3 years from randomization or total mesorectal excision.

schema.label: Near complete response
schema.text: Near complete response (nCR): restage after 8 to 10 weeks. Section 7.5 says all nCR patients then follow the complete response or incomplete response strategy. Incomplete response (iCR on the schema; section 7.4 column heading is incomplete CR) proceeds to transanal endoscopic surgery within 8 weeks.

schema.label: Non-response or progression
schema.text: Recommend total mesorectal excision.

schema.label: If surgery is not done
schema.text: Document the reason and the date the decision was made.

schema.label: Survival follow-up
schema.text: Until 5 years from randomization.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed invasive, well to moderately differentiated rectal adenocarcinoma that is mismatch repair proficient.

MRI stage cT1 that is not eligible for transanal surgery alone under NCCN guidance, including T1 tumors larger than 2 cm, a positive margin, or SM3 invasion into the lower third of the submucosa, or MRI stage cT2 to T3ab. T3a is invasion less than 1 mm. T3b is invasion of 1 to 5 mm.
cN0 on pelvic MRI, with no radiographic mesorectal nodal metastasis, tumor deposits, or extramural venous invasion. M0, with no metastatic disease on CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.
Mid to low-lying tumor that the treating surgeon considers eligible for transanal excision, and medically fit for radical total mesorectal excision in that surgeon's judgment.
Age at least 18 years. ECOG performance status 2 or better, or Karnofsky performance status at least 60 percent.

No contraindications to protocol chemotherapy. Within 30 days before enrollment: absolute neutrophil count at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count at least 100 x 10^9/L, bilirubin less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal excluding Gilbert syndrome, and estimated creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min.

Able and willing to complete quality-of-life questionnaires in English, French, or Spanish, with the baseline assessment completed before enrollment. Lack of comprehension, cognitive issues, or lack of competency does not make the participant ineligible. Ability but unwillingness does.

Must be accessible for treatment and follow-up. People of reproductive potential must agree to highly effective contraception during chemotherapy and for 9 months after. A pregnancy test is part of the pre-study evaluation and may include ultrasound if a false positive is suspected.
HIV-infected patients on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible.
Not eligible: poorly differentiated histology, or mucinous or signet ring histology, on the diagnostic biopsy.
Not eligible: visible pelvic sidewall nodes on MRI, or unequivocal nodal disease that in the investigator's opinion would prohibit protocol therapy.

No previous pelvic radiation for any reason, including brachytherapy alone. No prior treatment for rectal cancer. A primary lesion already excised is not eligible. If there was a partial excision, gross residual disease must still be visible endoscopically.
A prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment is eligible. This sentence is printed inside the ineligibility section.
Known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency is excluded. Participants should have recovered from clinically significant adverse events of the most recent therapy before enrollment.
Patients with known cardiac history, current cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic agents must be New York Heart Association class 2B or better. Any contraindication to MRI is excluded.

Anterior lesions above or near the peritoneal reflection that make the patient unsuitable for transanal tumor excision are excluded. T3 tumors invading or abutting the internal sphincter are excluded.

Risk Adapted Treatment of Unilateral Favorable Histology Wilms Tumors (FHWT)

amendments.text: Amendment 1, the current version: safety correction of the RT risk insert in consent 4; GFR/creatinine clearance added before UH-3 carboplatin; clarified VIVA starts at Cycle 2 and M/MVI start at Cycle 3; removed fixed staging-imaging window at enrollment; patients with 4 cycles of DD-4A omit Cycle 11 of Regimen M; RT dosing table simplified for HR histology.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Enroll on APEC14B1 (Part A) and receive a qualifying Initial Stratum Assignment from central review (APEC14B1-REN) by Day 14 after nephrectomy or biopsy; enroll on AREN2231 by Day 14. Biology from a CLIA lab (LOH 1p and 16q, 1q gain; plus LOH 11p15 for potential mVLR) drives callbacks to the final regimen. Standard biology: no 1q gain and no combined LOH 1p/16q (Stage I: also no LOH 11p15; node-positive Stage III/IV: no single LOH 1p or 16q).

schema.label: Stage I
schema.text: Standard biology and either age under 4 (non-epithelial) or epithelial histology at any age: modified very low risk (mVLR), nephrectomy only. Adverse biology, or non-epithelial histology age 4 or older: EE-4A (vincristine, dactinomycin) cycles 1-7. mVLR relapse: DD-4A plus RT (flank/WAI, whole lung, or metastatic site) for FHWT, UH-3 for anaplasia.

schema.label: Stage II
schema.text: EE-4A cycle 1, then by biology: standard biology continues EE-4A cycles 2-7; adverse biology randomized.

schema.label: Randomize (Stage II adverse biology)
schema.text: Cycles 2-9

arms.label: DD-4A
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin.

arms.label: VIVA
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, irinotecan (EE-4A backbone plus vincristine/irinotecan cycles).

schema.label: Stage III
schema.text: Upfront nephrectomy: DD-4A cycle 1 with abdominal RT; standard biology moves to EE-4A from cycle 2 (doxorubicin omitted), adverse biology randomized M vs MVI. Biopsy/delayed nephrectomy: DD-4A cycles 1-2, delayed nephrectomy after cycle 2 (or after cycle 3-4), then by histology and biology: standard biology with low/intermediate-risk histology continues EE-4A or DD-4A, adverse biology randomized M vs MVI, high-risk blastemal-predominant histology goes to UH-3. Most Stage III patients receive RT.

schema.label: Stage IV
schema.text: DD-4A cycles 1-2, then central lung response assessment. Lung-only, standard biology, rapid complete response (RCR): continue DD-4A without lung RT. Lung-only with slow incomplete response (SIR) or adverse biology, and all extrapulmonary metastases: randomized M vs MVI with whole lung and/or metastatic site RT. High-risk histology at delayed nephrectomy: UH-3. Most Stage IV patients receive RT.

schema.label: Randomize (Stage III adverse biology; Stage IV SIR, adverse biology, or extrapulmonary metastases)

arms.label: Regimen M
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, etoposide (starts at Cycle 3).

arms.label: Regimen MVI
arms.text: Regimen M plus vincristine/irinotecan cycles (starts at Cycle 3).

schema.label: Radiation therapy
schema.text: Flank RT 10.8 Gy/6 fx (19.8 Gy/11 fx for high-risk histology at delayed nephrectomy); whole abdomen 10.5 Gy/7 fx for rupture, diffuse spill, or peritoneal seeding; whole lung 12 Gy/8 fx (10.5 Gy/7 fx age 12 months or younger); brain, liver, bone, node, and soft tissue metastasis doses per section 17.9.4. Abdominal RT begins by Day 14 after nephrectomy; lung RT after the cycle 2 response assessment. IROC pre-approval required for whole lung IMRT, liver RT, and proton flank or WAI.

schema.label: Primary aims
schema.text: EFS: maintain outcomes with treatment reduction (Stage I nephrectomy only, Stage III EE-4A non-inferiority); non-inferiority of VIVA vs DD-4A (Stage II adverse biology) and MVI vs M (Stage III/IV); superiority of UH-3 for blastemal-predominant Stage III/IV vs historical controls.

eligibility: Enrolled on APEC14B1 with consent to Part A eligibility screening before enrollment.
Age under 30 years at enrollment.
Newly diagnosed Stage I-IV favorable histology Wilms tumor confirmed by central review, with a qualifying Initial Stratum Assignment by Day 14 after the diagnostic procedure; enrollment by Day 14.
Tumor sent for CLIA molecular testing for LOH 1p and 16q and 1q gain (plus LOH 11p15 if potentially mVLR); results needed by arm-specific time points.
Upfront nephrectomy must include at least one centrally confirmed lymph node (also required at delayed nephrectomy).
Karnofsky 50 or higher (over 16 years) or Lansky 50 or higher (16 or younger).
Bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (or direct bilirubin 3 x ULN or less); AST or ALT 3 x ULN or less (5 x ULN with liver metastases).
Stage IV: shortening fraction 27% or higher or ejection fraction 50% or higher (Stage II/III assigned to doxorubicin must meet this before doxorubicin).
HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No bilateral (Stage V) Wilms tumor; no uncontrolled intercurrent illness.
No mVLR (nephrectomy only) assignment with a Wilms tumor predisposition syndrome, contralateral nephrogenic rests, unilateral multicentric tumor, or partial nephrectomy.
No lung-only metastatic disease with all radiologically evident nodules already completely resected.

No prior tumor-directed chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this diagnosis (except emergent therapy); no prior doxorubicin if doxorubicin may be required; no concurrent chemotherapy for another diagnosis.
No known Charcot-Marie-Tooth syndrome.
Not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

studies.title: PREcision DIagnostics in Prostate Cancer Treatment (PREDICT)

schema.label: Pre-registration
schema.text: Local CLIA sequencing and, when needed, Caris DNA and RNA testing are reviewed by the molecular tumor board. The board assigns the arm. There is no randomization. Protocol treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

schema.label: Actionable alteration
schema.text: At progression, one re-registration is allowed and the board may assign a new arm from Caris testing.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Valemetostat tosylate (DS-3201b) 200 mg by mouth once daily, continuously, each 28-day cycle, on an empty stomach, with no food for 2 hours before and 1 hour after the dose. Qualifying alterations on the schema: Rb loss (DNA); Rb functional loss signature (RNA); NEPC signature (RNA).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 4 IV over 30 minutes plus cabazitaxel 20 mg/m2 IV over 60 minutes every 3 weeks for up to 10 cycles (21-day cycles). Growth-factor support is required, and concurrent prednisone follows institutional standard. Qualifying alterations on the schema: 2/3 TSG, FANC, HRD (DNA); SLFN11 signature (RNA).

schema.label: No study-defined alteration
schema.text: Physician choice of one option below. A patient may not receive an agent already received.

arms.label: Arm C
arms.text: Cabazitaxel 20 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks for up to 10 cycles (21-day cycle), or abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily plus prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily with no food for at least 2 hours before or 1 hour after abiraterone (28-day cycle), or enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily (28-day cycle), or lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan 7.4 GBq (200 mCi) IV every 6 weeks for up to 6 doses (42-day cycle).

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 in each arm, among patients with measurable disease.

eligibility: Step 0 requires histologic or cytologic prostate cancer, including neuroendocrine, small-cell, and sarcomatoid variants, without central pathology review and without using histology to select the arm.

Measurable or non-measurable metastatic disease by RECIST 1.1 is required, and tissue from any time during mCRPC or within 12 months before pre-registration must be available, with metastasis preferred and no mandated repeat biopsy for a later pre-registration.

A CLIA next-generation sequencing report is required, the molecular tumor board assigns the arm, qualifying DNA may come from tumor at any time or ctDNA within 12 months, and RNA assignment requires Caris testing of tumor from the mCRPC period or within 12 months when no qualifying DNA alteration is found.
Age is 18 or older.
Step 1 requires progressive mCRPC with testosterone below 50 ng/dL plus PSA progression, RECIST 1.1 soft-tissue progression, or PCWG3 bone progression.

PSA progression is two consecutive rises at least 1 week apart, the most recent PSA at least 2.0 ng/mL when PSA is the only sign of progression, and antiandrogen withdrawal before counting PSA progression if an antiandrogen was used.

Patients assigned to lutetium must have investigator-assessed PSMA-positive mCRPC; the protocol cites the VISION reference of at least one lesion with uptake above liver and no PSMA-negative node of short axis at least 2.5 cm, solid-organ lesion of short axis at least 1.0 cm, or bone lesion with a soft-tissue component of short axis at least 1.0 cm.

A prior androgen-receptor signaling inhibitor in metastatic hormone-sensitive disease or mCRPC is required, a prior taxane in either setting is required unless the patient is taxane-ineligible or refuses, prior lutetium is allowed, and deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 requires a prior PARP inhibitor.
Prior toxicity must be grade 1 or less or at baseline, except alopecia, and stable grade 2 neuropathy, fatigue, and the listed endocrinopathies are allowed.

No cytotoxic, biologic, radiopharmaceutical, or other non-kinase investigational agent is allowed within 4 weeks, kinase inhibitors and abiraterone, apalutamide, or darolutamide must stop at least 2 weeks before registration, enzalutamide must stop at least 4 weeks before, radiotherapy must stop at least 2 weeks before, major surgery must stop at least 4 weeks before, and prior EZH-inhibitor treatment is excluded.
The registration checklist also prints a separate bullet, 'Prior treatment with cabazitaxel + carboplatin,' and does not say whether that treatment is required, allowed, or excluded.

Current moderate or strong CYP3A inducers and hypersensitivity to valemetostat tosylate (DS-3201b) are exclusions; HIV with an undetectable viral load on antiretroviral therapy within 6 months is allowed; hepatitis B must be undetectable on suppression if indicated; and hepatitis C must be cured or undetectable on treatment.

Imminent or established spinal cord compression is excluded, and brain metastases or cranial epidural disease must be treated and stable for at least 4 weeks after radiotherapy or surgery, with wound healing complete.

Myocardial infarction or uncontrolled angina within 6 months, NYHA class 3 or 4 heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension above 160 mmHg systolic or 100 mmHg diastolic, QTcF of 470 ms or higher within 42 days in a patient with cardiac history or a QT-prolonging medication, a clinically significant acute infection requiring systemic therapy, and Child-Pugh class B or C liver disease are exclusions.
ECOG performance status is 0-2, sperm cannot be frozen or donated within 14 days, and G-CSF, red-cell transfusion, platelet transfusion within 2 weeks, and a bleeding diathesis are exclusions.

Labs are WBC at least 2,500/mcL, ANC above 1,500/mcL, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (at most 3 x ULN in Gilbert disease), AST and ALT at most 3 x ULN, and albumin at least 2.8 g/dL, and registration waits for the tumor-board assignment.

One re-registration is allowed after progression on the assigned therapy, without reconsent, and requires testosterone below 50 ng/dL, radiographic progression on CT or MRI of chest, abdomen, and pelvis plus a bone scan within 42 days, the same performance status, transfusion, cardiac, and laboratory limits, with transfusions allowed for the hemoglobin threshold and QTcF below 470 ms when cardiac history or a QT-affecting condition is present, plus a new Caris-based tumor-board assignment.

schema.label: Randomization
schema.text: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma with light chain cast nephropathy and new-onset renal failure within 90 days, no prior anti-CD38 antibody. N = 74. Cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Severity of renal impairment: severe (MDRD eGFR <= 29 mL/min/1.73 m2 or hemodialysis) vs non-severe (eGFR > 29).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 4 cycles of protocol therapy.

arms.label: Arm A: CyBorD
arms.text: Cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m2 PO or IV days 1, 8, 15, 22; bortezomib 1.5 mg/m2 SQ days 1, 8, 15, 22; dexamethasone 40 mg days 1-4, 8, 15, 22 in cycle 1 and days 1, 8, 15, 22 in cycles 2-4. 4 cycles.

arms.label: Arm B: Dara-VD
arms.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg/30,000 units SQ days 1, 8, 15, 22 cycles 1-2 and days 1, 15 cycles 3-4; bortezomib 1.5 mg/m2 SQ days 1, 8, 15, 22; dexamethasone as in Arm A. 4 cycles.

schema.label: After 4 cycles
schema.text: All further treatment, including autologous transplant for patients with PR or better, at investigator discretion.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Renal response rate by IMWG renal response criteria over 4 cycles.

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG 0-2 (PS 3 allowed if due to pathologic fracture or bone pain).
Multiple myeloma by IMWG criteria within 90 days: marrow plasma cells >= 10% or biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, plus at least one myeloma-defining event. No smoldering myeloma or MGUS.
Newly diagnosed (within 90 days) light chain cast nephropathy: proteinuria > 1 g/dL with < 10% albuminuria and/or involved serum FLC > 150 mg/dL.
New-onset renal failure within 90 days: MDRD eGFR < 40 ml/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine > 2 mg/dL, or on dialysis (eGFR must be < 50 if qualifying by creatinine or dialysis).
Prior myeloma therapy limited to no more than one cycle of cyclophosphamide, bortezomib, and/or dexamethasone, with the last dose within 30 days. Plasma exchange for LCCN within 30 days allowed.
No prior or current anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody.
No focal radiation within 14 days before randomization, except palliative RT for symptoms not directed at a measurable extramedullary plasmacytoma.
SPEP, 24-hour UPEP, serum FLC, and bone marrow (or bone/extramedullary lesion biopsy) within 28 days.
Labs within 28 days: Hgb >= 7.5 g/dL (transfusion or erythropoietin allowed), ANC > 1000/mcL, platelets > 75,000/mcL (transfusion allowed), bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN.
No AL amyloidosis, plasma cell leukemia, or CNS involvement.
No grade 3-4 peripheral neuropathy.

Respiratory disease in the past 2 years (COPD, moderate or severe persistent asthma) requires FEV1 >= 50% predicted within 28 days; no uncontrolled asthma. NYHA class II or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic agents.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated and cured.
No allergy or intolerance to boron, mannitol, sorbitol, corticosteroids, monoclonal antibodies, or human proteins.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

eligibility: Multiple myeloma by IMWG criteria (amyloid deposits allowed) diagnosed within 28 days before registration, or before the first induction course if previously treated; no plasma cell leukemia.
Measurable disease: IgG serum M-protein >= 0.5 g/dL, IgA/IgM/IgD/IgE >= 0.2 g/dL, urine M-protein >= 200 mg/24 h, or involved FLC >= 10 mg/dL with abnormal ratio.

Frail or intermediate fit by the Myeloma Frailty Index within 28 days. Frail: any renal function, Hb >= 7 g/dL, platelets >= 50 x 10^9/L, ANC >= 0.75 x 10^9/L. Intermediate fit requires at least one of CrCl < 30 mL/min, Hb > 7 and < 8 g/dL, platelets > 50 and < 75 x 10^9/L, ANC > 0.75 and < 1 x 10^9/L, or R-ISS stage III.
No prior systemic myeloma therapy except up to one cycle of a non-anti-CD38 regimen; emergency corticosteroids (up to dexamethasone 160 mg equivalent) and localized palliative RT allowed.

Zubrod performance status 0-2 (PS 3 allowed if due to myeloma).
Bilirubin <= 2 x ULN (<= 5 x ULN with Gilbert's) and AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN within 28 days.

No uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c > 9% within 14 days).
No COPD with FEV1 < 50% predicted.
No grade >= 3 peripheral neuropathy.

No major surgery within 14 days; no live vaccine within 28 days.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant or nursing; pregnancy tests within 14 days of registration and within 24 hours before C1D1 per lenalidomide REMS.

schema.text: APEC14B1 is required for COG participation. Group 1 was patients >= 18 years with marrow with or without extramedullary relapse of any duration, or < 18 years with marrow with or without extramedullary relapse < 24 months after initial diagnosis. Patients with WBC >= 30,000 and/or CNS2/3 and/or testicular disease received mandatory pre-immunotherapy treatment before the randomized arm: chemotherapy for WBC >= 30,000, intrathecal chemotherapy for CNS2/3, and chemoradiation for testicular disease. After Group 1 randomization, two immunotherapy cycles with marrow MRD after each cycle, then HSCT off protocol therapy. MRD < 0.01% after Cycle 1: may stop at physician discretion or proceed to Cycle 2. MRD >= 0.01%: Cycle 2 on the assigned arm.

Group 2 (closed) was marrow relapse >= 24 to < 36 months with any MRD, IEM relapse < 18 months with any MRD, or marrow or IEM relapse of any duration with MRD >= 0.1%, in patients < 18 years with marrow with or without extramedullary relapse >= 24 months from diagnosis, or any IEM relapse age >= 1 to < 31 years. Group 3 on this page is marrow relapse >= 36 months with MRD < 0.1%, or IEM relapse >= 18 months with MRD < 0.1%. MRD < 0.01% after Cycle 1 immunotherapy: may come off without Cycle 2. arms.text: Blinatumomab/nivolumab immunotherapy, Continuation 1, blinatumomab/nivolumab, Continuation 2, blinatumomab/nivolumab, Maintenance.

schema.label: Groups 3 and 4 (post-Amendment #4E)
schema.text: APEC14B1 required. Age >= 1 to < 31 years with IEM, bone marrow, or IEM plus bone marrow relapse of any duration. Study entry, VXLD reinduction, bone marrow MRD. Bone marrow blasts >= 50% after VXLD: off protocol therapy. Callback details are in Section 3.1.7.

schema.label: Group 4 callback and randomization
schema.text: Group 4: >= 18 years with marrow relapse of any duration; < 18 years with marrow relapse < 36 months with any MRD; age 1-31 years with IEM relapse < 18 months with any MRD; < 18 years with marrow relapse >= 36 months with MRD >= 0.1%; age 1-31 years with IEM relapse >= 18 months with MRD >= 0.1%. Two immunotherapy cycles, marrow MRD after each, then off-protocol HSCT. MRD < 0.01% after Cycle 1: may come off at physician discretion without Cycle 2. MRD >= 0.01%: Cycle 2 on the assigned arm.

arms.label: Arm H
arms.text: Blinatumomab immunotherapy for both cycles, then off-protocol HSCT.

arms.label: Arm I
arms.text: Blinatumomab/nivolumab immunotherapy for both cycles, then off-protocol HSCT.

schema.label: Group 3 callback and randomization
schema.text: Group 3: < 18 years with marrow relapse >= 36 months and MRD < 0.1%, or age 1-31 years with IEM relapse >= 18 months and MRD < 0.1%. Sequence after randomization: assigned immunotherapy, Consolidation, Intensification 1, assigned immunotherapy, Intensification 2, assigned immunotherapy, Maintenance. Patients with CNS2 that does not resolve to CNS1 by Day 15 of VXLD reinduction, and patients with CNS3, receive chemoradiation before the first cycle of Maintenance.

arms.label: Arm E
arms.text: Blinatumomab immunotherapy at each immunotherapy block.

arms.label: Arm F
arms.text: Blinatumomab/nivolumab immunotherapy at each immunotherapy block.

schema.label: Down syndrome, Arm G
schema.text: APEC14B1 required, study entry on Arm G. Pre-immunotherapy callback only if pre-immunotherapy is required (Section 4.1.2.4). WBC >= 30,000 and/or CNS2/3 and/or testicular disease: mandatory pretreatment before blinatumomab/nivolumab (chemotherapy, intrathecal chemotherapy, or chemoradiation, respectively). DS callback is required for all Down syndrome patients, after pre-immunotherapy if applicable. Cycle 1 blinatumomab/nivolumab, marrow MRD, Cycle 2 blinatumomab/nivolumab, marrow MRD, end of protocol therapy. MRD < 0.01% after Cycle 1: may stop at physician discretion or proceed to Cycle 2. MRD >= 0.01%: Cycle 2.

eligibility: Age >= 1 and < 31 years at enrollment.

First relapse of CD19-positive B-ALL, and relapse blasts must express CD19: isolated bone marrow; isolated CNS (excluding known optic nerve, retinal, and CNS chloromas) and/or testicular relapse; or combined bone marrow with CNS (same exclusions) and/or testes.
Patients with Down syndrome are eligible for isolated bone marrow relapse, or combined bone marrow with CNS (excluding known optic nerve, retinal, and CNS chloromas) and/or testicular relapse.
ECOG 0, 1, or 2. Use Karnofsky if > 16 years and Lansky if <= 16 years. For developmental delay, including Down syndrome, Lansky may replace Karnofsky, but ECOG 0-2 is still required.
Eligibility laboratories within 7 calendar days before enrollment unless otherwise indicated.
Must have fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy.
Prior blinatumomab or CD19-positive chimeric antigen receptor therapy in the upfront setting is allowed if relapsed lymphoblasts retain CD19 expression. No prior hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
One intrathecal chemotherapy at relapse is allowed. If fewer than 7 days have elapsed before protocol therapy, Day 1 intrathecal methotrexate, cytarabine, or triple intrathecal may be omitted.
In the 28 days before enrollment, up to five days of post-relapse, pre-enrollment steroids and/or hydroxyurea is allowed. There is no washout for patients who relapse while receiving upfront therapy.

Down syndrome patients who received that pre-enrollment therapy and have WBC >= 30,000/µL at enrollment still receive protocol cytoreduction with vincristine and dexamethasone, and no washout is required. If WBC < 30,000/µL, a 24 hour washout is required before immunotherapy.

Renal: creatinine clearance or radioisotope GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 1 to < 2 years 0.6/0.6, 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4.
Cardiac: shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, or ejection fraction >= 50% by echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, or radionuclide angiogram.
Pulmonary: no dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry > 94% if there is a clinical indication to measure it.

No B-lymphoblastic lymphoma, Burkitt leukemia or lymphoma, mature B-cell leukemia, Philadelphia chromosome-positive B-ALL, or ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL (rearrangements of ABL1, ABL2, CSF1R, or PDGFRB predicted sensitive to imatinib or dasatinib).
No mixed phenotype acute leukemia, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, or MYC translocation associated with mature (Burkitt) B-cell ALL, regardless of blast immunophenotype.

No active uncontrolled infection: positive bacterial blood culture within 48 hours of enrollment; IV or oral antibiotics with continued signs or symptoms (a course may be finished if cultures have been negative for at least 48 hours and symptoms have resolved; C. difficile requires at least 72 hours of antibacterial therapy and stools at baseline); fever above 38.2°C within 48 hours with clinical signs of infection (fever attributed to tumor burden is allowed if cultures are negative for more than 48 hours); positive fungal culture within 30 days or active therapy for presumed invasive fungal infection; or active viral or protozoal infection requiring IV treatment.
No Bloom syndrome, ataxia-telangiectasia, Fanconi anemia, Kostmann syndrome, Shwachman syndrome, or any other known bone marrow failure syndrome.

No uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load for at least the prior 6 months is eligible. Treated hepatitis B or C with no detectable viral burden is eligible.

No significant CNS pathology that would preclude blinatumomab, including a severe neurologic disorder or autoimmune disease with CNS involvement. Seizures well controlled on stable anti-epileptic doses are eligible. Cerebrovascular ischemia or hemorrhage with residual deficits is not eligible; resolved deficits remain eligible.

No active known or suspected autoimmune disease, except type I diabetes, hypothyroidism requiring only hormone replacement, skin disorders such as vitiligo, psoriasis, or alopecia not needing systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur without an external trigger.

Down syndrome with known non-hematopoietic, non-CNS/testicular extramedullary (chloromatous) disease is not eligible. Group 3 and 4 patients with chloromatous disease are eligible if it is not the only site of relapse.
Females of childbearing potential need a negative pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment. Lactating females are not eligible unless they agree not to breastfeed.

schema.label: Registration and induction
schema.text: Diagnosis, enrollment on APEC14B1, rapid central review on APEC14B1-CNS (imaging and tumor markers), then study entry on ACNS2021. Protocol therapy must begin within 31 days of definitive surgery or clinical diagnosis, whichever is later. Induction cycles 1-4, 21 days per cycle: cycles 1 and 3 carboplatin/etoposide, cycles 2 and 4 ifosfamide/mesna/etoposide. Response assessments after cycles 2 and 4. Prepare for high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue if less than radiographic CR or PR and/or marker elevation on the institutional assessment after cycle 4. Induction cycles 5 and 6, 21 days per cycle: cycle 5 carboplatin/etoposide, cycle 6 ifosfamide/mesna/etoposide. Rapid central review after cycle 6. Progressive disease is off protocol therapy.

schema.label: Radiographic CR or PR with normalization of markers
schema.text: Whole ventricular and spinal canal irradiation, 30.6 Gy, plus involved-field boost to 54 Gy.

schema.label: Less than radiographic CR or PR with normalization of markers
schema.text: Second-look surgery performed: if it reveals mature teratoma or non-viable tumor, proceed to whole ventricular and spinal canal irradiation (30.6 Gy plus involved-field boost to 54 Gy). No second-look surgery, with the reason documented: off protocol therapy.

schema.label: Less than radiographic CR or PR without normalization of markers
schema.text: Second-look surgery performed unless contraindicated. Viable tumor at second-look surgery: off protocol therapy. This pathway also connects to consolidation with high-dose chemotherapy and stem cell rescue.

schema.label: Radiographic PR without normalization of markers
schema.text: Consolidation with high-dose chemotherapy and stem cell rescue: thiotepa/etoposide (28-day cycle), PBSC infusion, and craniospinal irradiation of 36 Gy plus involved-field boost to 54 Gy.

schema.label: Radiographic CR without normalization of markers
schema.text: Same high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue consolidation: thiotepa/etoposide (28-day cycle), PBSC infusion, and craniospinal irradiation of 36 Gy plus involved-field boost to 54 Gy.

eligibility: Age >= 3 years and < 30 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed localized primary CNS NGGCT of the suprasellar and/or pineal region, by pathology and/or serum or CSF AFP above the institutional normal or > 10 ng/mL, or hCGβ > 100 mIU/mL, confirmed by rapid central marker screening on APEC14B1-CNS. Suprasellar, pineal, and bifocal tumors are included.

Eligible pathologic elements: endodermal sinus (yolk sac), embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, malignant or immature teratoma, and mixed germ cell tumor if those malignant elements are present. Patients with only mature teratoma are excluded. Pure germinoma admixed with mature teratoma is excluded.

Eligibility must be confirmed by rapid central imaging review on APEC14B1-CNS. Cranial MRI with and without gadolinium is required; if resected, pre-operative and post-operative brain MRI are required, and the post-operative MRI should be within 72 hours of surgery (recommended but not required after biopsy only). Spine MRI with gadolinium is required. Imaging within 31 days before enrollment (the post-operative MRI, if surgery was done).
Lumbar CSF cytology before enrollment unless medically contraindicated. If not obtained at surgery, obtain it at least 10 days after surgery and before enrollment.
CSF tumor markers with rapid central tumor marker review before enrollment unless medically contraindicated. Ventricular CSF at a diversion procedure is acceptable; lumbar CSF is preferred.
Serum AFP and hCGβ within 7 days before enrollment and start of therapy. CSF tumor markers and cytology within 31 days. Eligibility labs within 7 days.
ANC >= 1000/µL, platelets >= 100,000/µL and transfusion independent, and hemoglobin >= 8.0 g/dL (RBC transfusion allowed).

Creatinine clearance or radioisotope GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 3 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4.
Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, and ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
Seizure disorder is allowed if the patient is on anticonvulsants and well controlled. Patients must not be in status epilepticus, coma, or assisted ventilation before enrollment.

Protocol therapy must begin within 31 days of definitive surgery or clinical diagnosis, whichever is later. If only a biopsy was done, the biopsy date is the definitive surgery date. If additional surgery follows a biopsy or incomplete resection, the date of the last resection is used.

No tumors outside the ventricles (basal ganglia or thalamus). No isolated mature teratoma with non-elevated markers at diagnosis. No prior tumor-directed therapy other than surgery and corticosteroids. No metastatic disease by MRI, lumbar CSF cytology, or intraoperative evidence of dissemination.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. Serum or urine pregnancy tests may be falsely positive because of hCGβ-secreting germ cell tumors; confirm the patient is not pregnant by institutional standards. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

studies.title: A Phase I/ II Study of the Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of Belantamab Mafodotin (GSK2857916) in Combination with Iberdomide (CC-220)/ Dexamethasone Versus Belantamab Mafodotin (GSK2857916)/ Dexamethasone in Relapsed Refractory Multiple Myeloma

amendments.text: Update #01 (resubmission), the current version: new study chair, iberdomide 1.3 mg dose level removed (no longer manufactured), revised iberdomide CAEPR with consent addendum for patients on iberdomide, updated CTSU language and expedited reporting table.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: All patients pre-register to submit bone marrow and blood to the Alliance HEME Biorepository. Phase I enrollment uses slot reservation.

schema.label: Phase I (3+3 de-escalation)
schema.text: 56-day cycles: iberdomide (dose level 1: 1.0 mg starting; level -1: 0.75 mg) days 1-21 and 29-49, belantamab mafodotin 1.9 mg/kg IV day 1, dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg if age 75 or older) days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43, 50. Aspirin or anticoagulation required with iberdomide. Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Primary endpoint: DLTs in cycle 1.

schema.label: Phase II: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified by ISS stage (1-2 vs 3) and cytogenetic risk (high risk: 1q gain/amplification, t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p)). 56-day cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Belantamab mafodotin 1.9 mg/kg IV day 1 plus dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg if 75 or older) days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43, 50.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Iberdomide at the phase II recommended dose days 1-21 and 29-49, plus belantamab mafodotin and dexamethasone as in Arm 1.

schema.label: Step 2: Crossover re-registration
schema.text: Arm 1 patients with IMWG progression may add iberdomide (belantamab/iberdomide/dexamethasone) if labs and toxicity allow.

schema.label: Primary endpoint (phase II)
schema.text: PFS from randomization. Patients stopping for toxicity before progression are followed every 6 months up to 3 years from registration.

eligibility: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma by IMWG criteria, with measurable disease: serum M-protein 0.5 g/dL or more, urine M-protein 200 mg/24 h or more, or involved FLC 10 mg/dL or more with abnormal ratio.
Two or more prior lines of therapy, or triple-class exposed (exposed or refractory to an IMiD and/or PI and/or daratumumab or other anti-CD38 antibody).
No prior iberdomide, belantamab mafodotin, or other BCMA-directed therapy; no monoclonal antibody within 2 weeks; no targeted (non-antibody) or investigational agent within 2 weeks without recovery.
No severe allergic reaction (including erythema nodosum) to lenalidomide, pomalidomide, or another IMiD; no hypersensitivity to belantamab mafodotin or its components.
No prior allogeneic transplant (syngeneic allowed only without current or prior GvHD); no live vaccine within 30 days; no plasmapheresis within 7 days; no major surgery within 2 weeks.
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 1,000/mm3 or more; platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more in phase II if marrow plasma cells >50%); CrCl 30 mL/min or more (Cockcroft-Gault); spot urine albumin/creatinine <500 mg/g; bilirubin 2 x ULN or less; AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less; alkaline phosphatase 3 x ULN or less.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment; treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression.

No uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months. HCV allowed only after successful antiviral treatment with negative RNA after at least 4 weeks washout. HBcAb-positive/HBsAg-negative allowed with undetectable HBV DNA; HBsAg-positive allowed only with undetectable DNA on antivirals started at least 4 weeks before registration and no cirrhosis.

No unacceptable cardiac risk: uncontrolled arrhythmia or Mobitz II/third-degree AV block; MI, acute coronary syndrome, angioplasty, stenting, or bypass within 3 months; NYHA class III-IV heart failure; uncontrolled hypertension; congenital long QT or QTcF >480 msec; any VF or torsades; symptomatic bradycardia (HR <50); LVEF <30%.

No Child-Pugh score above 1 or cirrhosis (stable non-cirrhotic liver disease or hepatobiliary myeloma involvement allowed); no active renal condition or dialysis (isolated myeloma proteinuria allowed); no active mucosal or internal bleeding; no active infection.
No symptomatic amyloidosis, active POEMS syndrome, or active plasma cell leukemia.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (stop 14 days before registration); able to swallow oral agents.

Step 2 (Arm 1 crossover): IMWG progression on belantamab/dexamethasone with measurable disease (including PET/CT or MRI progression), ANC 1,000/mm3 or more, platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 if marrow plasma cells >50%), CrCl 30 mL/min or more, bilirubin 2 x ULN or less, AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less.

studies.title: A Phase II Study of Cabozantinib in Combination with Cemiplimab (REGN2810) (Cabo-Cemiplimab (REGN-2810)) Versus Cabozantinib Alone in Adolescents and Adults with Advanced Adrenocortical Cancer

schema.label: Step 1: Registration/Randomization
schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma, age ≥ 12. Treatment begins ≤ 28 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior systemic therapy (treatment naive vs ≥ 1 prior line); corticosteroid-producing tumor (yes vs no). Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO once daily, continuous, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cemiplimab 350 mg IV day 1 every 21 days + cabozantinib 40 mg PO once daily. Cemiplimab maximum 2 years; cabozantinib alone may continue afterward until progression or toxicity.

schema.label: Step 2: Crossover (Arm C)
schema.text: Arm A patients with RECIST progression may re-register within 4 weeks (± 1 week) to cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 21 days + cabozantinib daily (no re-escalation of a previously reduced cabozantinib dose); cemiplimab maximum 2 years.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 4 years from registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1, cabozantinib-cemiplimab vs cabozantinib alone.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically confirmed adrenocortical carcinoma, locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic, with disease evaluable by RECIST 1.1.
Up to 3 prior systemic lines in the unresectable/recurrent/metastatic setting (EDP-M counts as 1 line); treatment-naive patients allowed.
No prior cabozantinib or other cMET inhibitor, anti-CTLA-4, or anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy.

Prior RT, cytotoxic chemotherapy, or targeted therapy allowed if completed ≥ 14 days before registration with toxicity recovered to grade ≤ 1; lesions irradiated within 1 month cannot be index lesions.
Mitotane within 6 months: must be stopped ≥ 28 days before registration with a mitotane level < 2 mg/L.
Age ≥ 12 years and BSA ≥ 1.2 m2. ECOG 0-2 (age ≥ 18), Lansky ≥ 50 (age 12-15), or Karnofsky ≥ 50 (age 16-17).

ANC ≥ 1,000/mcL without growth factor within 2 weeks, platelets ≥ 100,000/mcL, hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert ≤ 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, UPCR ≤ 1 mg/mg, CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min.
Adrenal steroid production assessed (random ACTH and cortisol) within 3 months before registration, for stratification.

Cardiac: NYHA class II or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; no congenital long QT, no myocarditis, no MI or unstable angina within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypertension (sustained ≥ 150/90 mmHg) within 14 days.

No GI conditions with bleeding or perforation risk within 6 months (active ulcer, bleeding endoluminal metastasis, IBD), no GI perforation within 6 months, no tumor invading the GI tract within 28 days, and no pancreatitis.
No endobronchial lesions of main or lobar bronchi, no tumor infiltrating major pulmonary vessels or encasing any major blood vessel, and no hemoptysis > 2.5 mL within 3 months.
No history of pneumonitis.

No brain metastases or cranial epidural disease unless treated with RT and/or surgery (including radiosurgery), stable ≥ 4 weeks, neurologically asymptomatic, and off corticosteroids at treatment start.
No major surgery within 2 weeks or minor surgery within 10 days; no fracture or non-healing wound within 28 days.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that may recur and affect vital organs or require immunosuppression; vitiligo and replaced endocrinopathies allowed. No steroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent.

No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (stop 14 days before), and no warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors within 5 days; low-dose aspirin, LMWH, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban allowed.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with assessment.
Able to swallow tablets. Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before registration).

Step 2 (crossover to Arm C): RECIST progression on Arm A cabozantinib, re-registration within 4 weeks (± 1 week) of progression, all Step 1 criteria met, not discontinued from (or meeting discontinuation criteria for) cabozantinib due to toxicity, pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before re-registration.

A Phase III Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy of the Addition of Inotuzumab Ozogamicin (a Conjugated Anti-CD22 Monoclonal Antibody) to Frontline Therapy in Young Adults (Ages 18-39 Years) with Newly Diagnosed Precursor B-Cell ALL

amendments.text: Update #10, the current version. Updated inotuzumab CAEPR (version 2.1) with new risks and matching consent changes, per NCI Action Letter; consent addendum required for patients on or awaiting inotuzumab. Phase III enrollment was closed earlier, in Update 08, when the Pilot Cohort became the only enrolling arm.

schema.label: Enrollment status
schema.text: As of Update 08 the phase III randomization is permanently closed to new patients, and all new patients enroll on the single-arm Pilot Cohort (planned 24 patients). The confirmation of tolerability phase was completed in 2018 at inotuzumab 0.5 mg/m2 on Days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Baseline bone marrow (or peripheral blood if inaspirable) sent centrally. For the closed phase III this included the LDA assay used for stratification.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration, Course I induction
schema.text: C10403 pediatric-inspired induction starting within 5 days of registration: IT cytarabine Day 1; dexamethasone Days 1-7 and 15-21; vincristine and daunorubicin 25 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15, 22; pegaspargase (age over 21.5) or calaspargase (age under 21.5) once Day 4-6; IT methotrexate Days 8 and 29 (also Days 15 and 22 for CNS3). Day 29 bone marrow. M3 or M4 marrow (more than 25% blasts) ends protocol treatment, with survival follow-up every 6 months.

schema.label: Pilot Cohort (current)

schema.text: Phase III: event-free survival without censoring for transplant. Pilot: safety and tolerability of one inotuzumab cycle plus two blinatumomab cycles added to C10403.

eligibility: Newly diagnosed CD22-positive precursor B-cell ALL (WHO). CD22 and CD20 positivity means expression on more than 20% of blasts by local flow cytometry.

HIV is allowed if no AIDS-related complications other than prior low CD4 count, HIV viral load under 200 copies/mm3 on combination antiretroviral therapy compatible with protocol therapy (no cobicistat, stavudine, or zidovudine).

schema.text: Dara-VCD x 3 cycles (28 days): bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 SC, cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m2 PO/IV (cap 500 mg), dexamethasone 20 mg, all days 1, 8, 15, 22; daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg SC weekly Cycles 1-2, days 1 and 15 Cycle 3. Start within 14 days

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG performance status 0-2 (3 allowed if due to neuropathy).
Biopsy-proven systemic AL amyloidosis (Congo red with green birefringence or characteristic EM) with confirmatory typing by mass spectrometry or immunofluorescence.

Measurable disease (monoclonal serum or urine immunofixation or clonal marrow plasma cells) plus dFLC >= 2 mg/dL, assessed within 28 days before therapy (56 days if treatment started before registration).
Up to one cycle (28 days) of any plasma cell-directed therapy before enrollment; no MOD-PFS event if prior Dara-VCD counts toward induction.

Transplant eligible for melphalan 140-200 mg/m2 and willing to undergo ASCT: supine SBP >= 90 mmHg; NT-proBNP < 5000 pg/mL (or BNP < 400); cTnT < 0.06 ng/mL (or hsTnT < 75 ng/L or TnI < 0.1 ng/mL); NYHA I-II; LVEF >= 40%.

Within 56 days: Hb > 8.0 g/dL, WBC >= 2,000/uL, ANC >= 1,000/uL, platelets >= 50,000/uL, bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, direct bilirubin <= 2.0 mg/dL, AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN, alkaline phosphatase <= 750 U/L (hepatic involvement excepted), creatinine <= ULN or CrCl >= 30 mL/min.
Peripheral neuropathy grade <= 2.
No concurrent multiple myeloma (lytic lesions, plasmacytoma, >= 60% marrow plasma cells, or hypercalcemia).
No HBsAg positivity or detectable HBV DNA; HCV treated and cured or undetectable within 6 months; HIV on ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No COPD with FEV1 < 50% predicted; no moderate or severe persistent asthma within 2 years or uncontrolled asthma.
No uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension, or infection; no major surgery within 14 days; no live vaccine within 28 days.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant or nursing.

Step 2: At least PR after 3 cycles, no MOD-PFS event, still receiving daratumumab plus at least one other study drug; cardiac criteria rechecked within 14 days and labs within 28 days; ASCT arm must collect >= 2.0 x 10^6 CD34+/kg.
Step 3: Daratumumab not permanently discontinued; registered within 28 days of completing Arm 1 consolidation or within 180 days of ASCT; no MOD-PFS event.
