schema.label: Step 1: Registration and induction
schema.text: Zanubrutinib 160 mg PO BID days 1-28 plus rituximab (or biosimilar) 375 mg/m2 IV day 1, every 28 days for 6 cycles (subcutaneous rituximab/hyaluronidase allowed after one full IV dose). Zanubrutinib continues until randomization. Treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

schema.label: Response after cycle 6
schema.text: CR proceeds to randomization within 28 days after C6D28. PR, SD, or PD: off protocol treatment.

schema.label: Step 2: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: CR patients only. Stratified by age (60-69 vs 70 or older) and MIPI (low, intermediate, high). Maintenance cycles are 84 days.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Continuous zanubrutinib at the end-of-induction dose, days 1-84 of each cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Observation until first progression (PD #1), then zanubrutinib restarted within 21 days of documented PD #1 and continued until second progression (PD #2) or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: PFS from randomization: PFS1 (first progression or death) on Arm A vs PFS2 (second progression or death) on Arm B. Follow-up 10 years from registration.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed mantle cell lymphoma with cyclin D1 expression and/or CCND1 rearrangement or t(11;14); cyclin D1/t(11;14)-negative MCL with an MCL expression profile (such as SOX11) is also eligible. Any stage (I-IV).
Measurable disease by PET or CT (liver disease must be measurable if liver is the only site), or bone marrow involvement by MCL.

No prior systemic treatment for MCL (steroids up to prednisone 100 mg/day or equivalent for up to 7 days before registration allowed), no prior radiation for stage I MCL, no prior BTK inhibitor or anti-CD20 antibody, and no prior stem cell transplant.

Age 70 or older, or age 60 to <70 with comorbidity precluding autologous transplant: EF <45%, DLCO <60% predicted, CrCl <70 but >30 mL/min, ECOG 2, or CIRS total score >6. Not a transplant candidate or declined transplant.
ECOG performance status 0-2.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 750/mm3 or more and platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more if due to lymphoma), without growth factor or transfusion within 7 days; CrCl 30 mL/min or more; total bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (unless Gilbert's); AST/ALT 3 x ULN or less.

No clinically significant cardiovascular disease: unstable angina within 3 months, NYHA class III-IV heart failure, clinically significant arrhythmia (sustained VT, VF, torsades), QTcF >480 msec (unless pacemaker), or Mobitz II or third-degree block without a pacemaker.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. No active hepatitis B or C: prior HBV exposure allowed with undetectable viral load on prophylactic antivirals; prior HCV allowed with undetectable viral load.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

No severe bleeding disorder (hemophilia A/B, von Willebrand disease, or spontaneous bleeding requiring transfusion or intervention); no stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 6 months before registration.

No disease significantly affecting GI absorption (malabsorption, gastric or small bowel resection, bariatric surgery, symptomatic IBD, bowel obstruction); must swallow pills. Recovered from major surgery.
No live vaccine within 35 days before registration; no hypersensitivity to zanubrutinib or rituximab.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers stopped 14 days before registration.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: EBV-associated recurrent and/or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, no prior palliative systemic therapy.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration and induction
schema.text: Baseline plasma EBV DNA collected. Induction within 7 days: nivolumab 360 mg IV Day 1 + cisplatin 80 mg/m2 (or carboplatin AUC 5) Day 1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8, every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Response by RECIST 1.1 after cycles 3 and 6.

schema.label: Step 3: Registration
schema.text: Patients without progression (CR, PR, SD) after 3-6 induction cycles completed within 20 weeks, with post-induction plasma EBV DNA collected. Patients with progression go off study.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Age (≤ 50 vs > 50); number of disease sites before induction (1 vs > 1).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Maintenance starts within 7 days of randomization; maximum 2 years counted from start of induction, or until progression or intolerance.

arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks.

arms.label: Arm 2 (experimental)
arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg + relatlimab (BMS-986016) 480 mg as a single IV infusion every 4 weeks.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival by RECIST 1.1 (signal of improvement with relatlimab added to nivolumab maintenance).

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically proven NPC with locoregional recurrence not amenable to curative surgery or re-irradiation, and/or distant metastases (de novo metastatic allowed).
EBV associated: EBER-positive tumor, or a history of detectable plasma EBV DNA by PCR at any time since diagnosis.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 (previously irradiated lesions count only with documented progression after RT); contrast CT chest, and contrast CT or MRI of nasopharynx and neck if locoregional disease is known.

Treated brain or leptomeningeal metastases or cord compression allowed if clinically stable ≥ 2 months and off steroids (> 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent) > 4 weeks; skull base involvement allowed unless directly invading brain with symptoms or significant edema.
Age ≥ 18; ECOG 0-2.
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 8.0 g/dL (transfusion allowed, not EPO dependent).
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN or direct bilirubin ≤ ULN (≤ 3 x ULN with Gilbert's); ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases); corrected calcium ≤ 1.5 x ULN.
Creatinine ≤ 1.5 x ULN or CrCl > 30 mL/min; CrCl must be > 50 mL/min for cisplatin (carboplatin if 30-50).

No prior palliative systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic NPC (prior curative-intent therapy, including systemic therapy before curative re-irradiation or surgery, allowed); > 6 months from last curative-intent treatment to recurrence.
No prior PD-L1, PD-L2, LAG-3, or other checkpoint/co-stimulation agents; prior PD-1 or CTLA-4 inhibitor allowed only as adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy for non-metastatic NPC.
Prior therapy toxicity resolved to grade 0-1 (except alopecia, dry mouth, dysgeusia, dysphagia, fatigue; cisplatin neuropathy must be grade 0-2; any hearing loss allowed).
No palliative RT within 30 days unless the irradiated sites are not target lesions and not the only measurable disease; no major surgery within 30 days.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization or MI within 6 months; NYHA II or better; no prior myocarditis.
No history of pneumonitis requiring steroids, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or organizing pneumonia; no active or MDR TB (treated TB > 2 years ago allowed); no active infection requiring IV therapy.

No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 2 years (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hormone-replaced endocrinopathy, alopecia, and psoriasis not requiring systemic therapy allowed); no immunosuppressive steroids (> 10 mg prednisone) or immunosuppressants within 14 days; no prior solid organ or bone marrow transplant.
No live vaccine within 30 days; no grade 3-4 allergy to cisplatin, carboplatin, or gemcitabine, or grade 4 reaction to any monoclonal antibody.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months at an experienced site; chronic HBV requires undetectable HBV DNA; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

Step 3: no progression after a minimum of 3 and up to 6 induction cycles completed within 20 weeks of Cycle 1 Day 1 (fewer than 6 only for toxicity delays or intercurrent illness), CT within 30 days, no criteria for permanent discontinuation or nivolumab-related autoimmune toxicity requiring discontinuation, and post-induction plasma EBV DNA collected.

studies.title: Randomized Phase 2 Study of Nivolumab and Ipilimumab with or Without Cabozantinib in Patients with Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma That Have Progressed After Platinum Treatment and Immunotherapy

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Recurrent or metastatic incurable nasopharyngeal carcinoma after platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: EBV positive vs negative (local pathology); ECOG 0-1 vs 2. Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 28-day cycles. Safety lead-in in the first 6 patients per arm (12 total), with accrual paused until all complete 8 weeks.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily + nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Nivolumab and ipilimumab for a maximum of 2 years; cabozantinib may continue beyond 2 years per investigator.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 2 years after treatment discontinuation or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival, cabozantinib-nivolumab-ipilimumab vs nivolumab-ipilimumab.

eligibility: Histologically documented nasopharyngeal carcinoma, any WHO type (keratinizing, non-keratinizing, basaloid squamous), regardless of EBV, HPV, p16, or PD-L1 status.
Recurrent, metastatic, incurable disease previously treated with platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade (first or second line), with immunotherapy part of the most recent line.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 with at least one measurable lesion not previously irradiated.
No more than 2 prior lines of systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic NPC; no prior VEGFR-targeted therapy.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS 0-2.

ANC ≥ 1,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, creatinine ≤ 1.5 mg/dL or CrCl ≥ 30 (MDRD), total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert < 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).

No chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 3 weeks (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C) before registration; palliative limited-field RT allowed if repeat imaging shows no new bone metastases and the irradiated lesion is not a target lesion.

Recovered from prior therapy toxicity to grade ≤ 1 (except alopecia); no prior life-threatening immune-related events likely to recur (severe pneumonitis, grade 4 bullous dermatitis/DRESS, autoimmune encephalitis, transverse myelitis, myocarditis).

amendments.text: Revision #7: Stage II accrual extended through September 30, 2027 or 220 screened; cohorts simplified to TIS high or low within melanoma and HNSCC (TMB no longer used for assignment); TIS replaces GEP throughout; ORR analyzed by TIS subgroup with new secondary objectives for ORR by TIS and TMB and TMB as a continuous variable; Stage II futility analysis consolidated across cohorts; CD8 and PD-L1 translational analysis added.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II immunoMATCH pilot (BiCaZO) of cabozantinib plus nivolumab in PD-1 refractory melanoma or HNSCC. Two disease cohorts (melanoma, HNSCC), each stratified by tumor inflammation score (TIS): TIS high is 6 or more for melanoma and 7 or more for HNSCC. TMB is measured but no longer used for cohort assignment.

schema.label: Step 1: Specimen submission
schema.text: Order kits one week before registration. Submit fresh biopsy or archival tissue plus blood within 3 days after Step 1 registration for central TMB and TIS testing.

schema.label: Step 2: Treatment registration
schema.text: Stage I: registered and treated before biomarker results, assigned to biomarker cohort retrospectively. Stage II (opened with Revision #5): registered only if a slot is open in the participant's biomarker cohort; otherwise off study. Treatment starts within 7 days of Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV day 1 every 28 days plus cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily, fasting (no food 2 hours before and 1 hour after). Up to 24 months or 26 cycles. Treatment beyond initial RECIST progression allowed during the first 24 weeks if clinically stable and benefiting.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Accrual
schema.text: Through September 30, 2027 or until 220 participants are screened, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Feasibility: proportion with biomarker turnaround of 21 days or less (Stage I TMB; Stage II TMB and TIS), with at least 75% considered feasible. Efficacy: ORR in each disease cohort by TIS subgroup.

eligibility: Step 1: Histologically confirmed unresectable stage III or IV, recurrent, or metastatic non-uveal melanoma; or HNSCC of the oropharynx, oral cavity, hypopharynx, or larynx that is metastatic or locally recurrent and not amenable to curative therapy. No nasopharynx primary or unknown primary. HPV or p16 status known for oropharynx.
Step 1: Disease consistent with measurable disease.

Step 1: Documented progression during or within 12 weeks after the last dose of PD-1 based therapy, after at least 6 weeks of checkpoint inhibitor. Recurrence during or within 12 weeks of adjuvant anti-PD-1 qualifies if measurable and unresectable.
Step 1: Recovered to baseline or grade 1 or less from prior treatment toxicity (unless clinically nonsignificant or stable on supportive therapy).

Step 1: No more than one prior curative or adjuvant RT course to head and neck mucosal surfaces, completed at least 16 weeks before (chemoradiation) or 8 weeks before (RT alone). Palliative RT allowed if not to previously irradiated tissue (CNS excepted) and finished at least 4 weeks before. Treated areas healed with no RT sequelae predisposing to fistula.
Step 1: No prior anti-VEGF therapy.
Step 1: Age 18 or older; Zubrod 0-1; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; able to swallow capsules whole; no malabsorption.
Step 1: No MI or thromboembolic event requiring anticoagulation within 90 days unless stable on management. No uncontrolled hypertension (systolic over 150 or diastolic over 90 mmHg) within 28 days.

Step 1: No hemoptysis (1/2 teaspoon or more of bright red blood) or tumor bleeding within 90 days. No prior carotid bleeding, tumor invading major vessels, cavitary central lung metastases (within 2 cm of hilum), or bleeding from the current head and neck cancer.

Step 1: No warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors such as clopidogrel. Low-dose aspirin and prophylactic LMWH allowed; therapeutic LMWH, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban allowed if no known brain metastases and stable dose for at least 1 week.

Step 1: No active autoimmune disease requiring more than 10 mg prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression (type 1 diabetes, replaced endocrinopathy, and non-systemically treated skin disorders allowed). No organ allograft. No active infection requiring systemic therapy.

Step 1: HIV allowed with undetectable viral load within 6 months on ART. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load within 28 days; prior HCV allowed with undetectable viral load within 28 days.
Step 1: Adequate archival tissue obtained after resistance to anti-PD-1/L1, or fresh biopsy with under 2% expected risk of severe complications; whole blood for germline analysis.
Step 1: Not pregnant and not nursing.

Step 2: Measurable disease assessed within 28 days (non-measurable within 42 days). Melanoma: CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis. HNSCC: CT neck and chest.
Step 2: Treated brain metastases without progression after CNS-directed therapy and off steroids at least 14 days.

Step 2: No surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, biologic agents, or steroids within 14 days; no investigational agents or monoclonal antibodies within 28 days; no live vaccine within 30 days; no strong CYP3A4 inducers within 14 days or strong inhibitors within 5 half-lives.

Step 2: H&P within 28 days. Within 28 days: leukocytes at least 3,000/uL, ANC at least 1,500/uL, platelets at least 100,000/uL, total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (3 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN, creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault), baseline urinalysis.

amendments.text: Update #10, the current version. Updated blinatumomab CAEPR (version 2.8) with new risks and matching consent changes, per NCI Action Letter; consent addendum required for patients on or awaiting blinatumomab.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory first-pull bone marrow aspirate and peripheral blood to the HEME Biobank for MRD. Protocol treatment starts within 7 days of registration.

schema.label: Cohort 1
schema.text: Newly diagnosed Ph-negative CD22-positive B-ALL, age 60 or older, not planned for HCT. Induction Course IA: inotuzumab ozogamicin 0.8 mg/m2 Day 1 and 0.5 mg/m2 Days 8 and 15 (21 days), marrow Day 18-21. CR/CRi: Course IB, inotuzumab 0.5 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15 (28 days). Adequate cytoreduction without CR (50% or greater blast reduction or marrow cellularity 20% or less): Course IC, 0.8/0.5/0.5 mg/m2 (28 days). Inadequate cytoreduction goes straight to Course II. Then Course II blinatumomab (84 days), then Course IIIA (two 42-day blinatumomab cycles) after CR/CRi to induction, or Course IIIB (three 42-day cycles) if induction did not produce CR/CRi.

schema.label: Cohort 2
schema.text: Relapsed or refractory Ph-negative CD22-positive B-ALL in salvage 1 or 2, age 18 or older. Same inotuzumab induction (Courses IA, IB, or IC) and Course II blinatumomab, then Course IIIB blinatumomab (126 days) if in CR/CRi. Allogeneic HCT is allowed any time after CR/CRi.

schema.label: Cohort 3 (feasibility)
schema.text: Newly diagnosed Ph/BCR-ABL1-positive CD22-positive B-ALL, age 75 or older, or 18 or older and HyperCVAD-ineligible. Course I (35 days): ponatinib 45 mg daily, dexamethasone 20 mg/m2 Days 1-7 and 15-21, IT methotrexate Days 1, 15, 29. Course IIA (21 days): ponatinib 15 mg (if CMR) or 30 mg with inotuzumab 0.3 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15 if in CR/CRi, or 0.6/0.3/0.3 mg/m2 if not. Course IIB (CR/CRi after IIA) or IIC (no CR/CRi): one more 28-day inotuzumab cycle with ponatinib. Courses III and IV: two 42-day blinatumomab cycles each with ponatinib. Maintenance: ponatinib 15 mg daily (CMR) or 30 mg daily (no CMR) for 24 months. Ponatinib continues without breaks through maintenance.

schema.label: Blinatumomab dosing
schema.text: Continuous infusion 9 mcg/day Days 1-7 of the first cycle, then 28 mcg/day for 28 days of each 42-day cycle (BSA-based doses if weight under 45 kg). Hospital admission recommended for initiation and cycle restarts.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cohorts 1 and 2: 1-year event-free survival. Cohort 3: feasibility of the regimen. The confirmation of tolerability lead-in for Cohorts 1 and 2 was completed as of Update #03.

eligibility: Morphologic precursor B-cell ALL (WHO), CD22 on 20% or more of lymphoblasts by local hematopathology. Ph/BCR-ABL1 status by cytogenetics, FISH, or PCR determines cohort (negative for Cohorts 1 and 2, positive for Cohort 3). No Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia.

No active CNS leukemia: only CNS-1 allowed. No CNS-directed treatment for active disease or symptomatic CNS leukemia within 28 days, and no parenchymal CNS mass. Prophylactic IT therapy alone is allowed.
Known or suspected testicular involvement is allowed only with concomitant scrotal/testicular radiotherapy (section 3.3.1); the schema summary instead lists testicular involvement as an exclusion.
ECOG performance status 0-2. Not pregnant and not nursing; pregnancy test within 7 days before registration.

No unstable cardiac disease (MI, angina, uncontrolled heart failure or arrhythmia) within 6 months. No LVEF under 45% or NYHA class III-IV heart failure. No clinically significant ventricular arrhythmia, unexplained non-vasovagal syncope, or chronic bradycardic states unless a permanent pacemaker is in place. QTcF 470 msec or less.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. HBV allowed only on suppressive therapy with no active virus or liver damage. HCV allowed only after eradication with undetectable viral load and no liver damage.

No clinically relevant neurologic disorder (epilepsy, seizure, aphasia, stroke, severe brain injury, structural brain abnormality, benign brain tumor, dementia, Parkinson disease, movement or cerebellar disorder).
No other malignancy except treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, cervical carcinoma in situ, stage I-II cancer in complete remission, or any cancer disease-free for 2 years or more.
No chronic liver disease or cirrhosis, and no history of SOS/VOD. No uncontrolled infection, and no deep tissue infection (fasciitis, osteomyelitis) within 4 months.
Total bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (2 x ULN or less for Gilbert disease or leukemic infiltration), AST and ALT 2.5 x ULN or less, creatinine clearance 40 mL/min or higher.

Cohort 1: age 60 or older, Ph-negative, no plan for allogeneic or autologous HCT, and no prior ALL therapy except single-dose IT chemotherapy, corticosteroids, hydroxyurea, or leukapheresis for no more than 14 days, completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy.

Cohort 2: age 18 or older, Ph-negative, relapsed or refractory in salvage 1 or 2, no isolated extramedullary relapse. Prior allogeneic HCT allowed if 4 months or more before registration, no GVHD, and off immunosuppression for 30 days or more. No prior inotuzumab, blinatumomab, or other CD22- or CD19-directed therapy. Rituximab completed 7 days or more and other monoclonal antibodies 6 weeks or more before registration.

Cohort 2: other prior ALL therapy completed 14 days or more before registration, except IT chemotherapy, hydroxyurea, corticosteroids, 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, or leukapheresis (completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy). Prior non-hematologic toxicity resolved to grade 1 or less. Peripheral blast count 10,000/uL or less.

Cohort 3: age 75 or older, or 18 or older and ineligible for HyperCVAD; Ph/BCR-ABL1-positive; no prior ALL therapy except single-dose IT chemotherapy, corticosteroids, hydroxyurea, a BCR-ABL1 TKI, or leukapheresis for no more than 14 days, completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy. No chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers.

amendments.text: Update #10, the current version. Cabozantinib CAEPR updated to version 2.6 (arterial thromboembolism added; MI and wound dehiscence raised to rare but serious) and nivolumab CAEPR to version 2.6; consent and consent addendum revised accordingly; 'gender' changed to 'sex'.

schema.label: Registration by histology cohort
schema.text: Single-arm phase II with parallel cohorts: A small cell/neuroendocrine bladder; B bladder, urachal, or bladder/urethra clear cell adenocarcinoma; C squamous cell bladder; D plasmacytoid urothelial; E any penile cancer; F sarcomatoid RCC; G miscellaneous GU variants; H sarcomatoid urothelial; I renal medullary; J bone-only non-prostate GU (exploratory); K collecting duct; L urethral. Expansion cohorts (checkpoint-inhibitor naive only) added for A, C, and L in Update #07.

schema.label: Cycles 1-4: triplet (21-day cycles)
schema.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily, nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Day 1, ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Day 1, every 3 weeks for 4 doses. Treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

schema.label: Cycle 5 onward: doublet (28-day cycles)
schema.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily plus nivolumab 480 mg IV Day 1 every 4 weeks, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: With confirmed CR or PR, treatment continues 2 years from response; with stable disease beyond 9 months, total therapy is 33 months. Then surveillance off treatment.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 5 years from registration or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Objective response rate per cohort. Simon two-stage design: 9 then up to 17 evaluable patients (null 5%, target 30%); expansion of 30 patients if 3 or more responses in 17.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. Karnofsky 80% or higher. Able to swallow tablets.

Histologically confirmed metastatic disease (new or progressive lesions) in one of cohorts A-L, with at least one RECIST 1.1 measurable lesion, or at least one bone lesion for the bone-only cohort J. Pure histology required for adenocarcinoma and squamous cohorts; about 50% or more variant histology for plasmacytoid, sarcomatoid, and micropapillary types.

Treatment-naive or up to 2 prior systemic therapies. Small cell carcinoma must have had a platinum-based combination (neoadjuvant, adjuvant, or first line). Urothelial bone-only patients must have had cisplatin-based chemotherapy if cisplatin-eligible.

No prior PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 therapy, except urothelial histology cohorts (D, H, J, L). Expansion cohorts enroll checkpoint-naive patients only. No prior cabozantinib; prior MET or VEGFR inhibitor allowed, but not both MET/VEGF and checkpoint therapy.

ANC at least 1,000/mcL, platelets at least 75,000/mcL, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed), albumin at least 3.2 g/dL, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert's up to 3.0 mg/dL), AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN (5 x ULN with liver metastases or Gilbert's), creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or CrCl at least 40 mL/min/1.73 m2, lipase and amylase at most 2 x ULN with no pancreatitis.

Washouts: no cytotoxic or biologic therapy within 2 weeks; no small-molecule kinase inhibitor or hormonal therapy within 14 days or 5 half-lives (GnRH agonists/antagonists allowed); no investigational agent within 14 days; no radionuclide within 6 weeks. Prior toxicity recovered to grade 1 or less.
No RT to lungs, mediastinum, or abdomen within 4 weeks (or ongoing complications); no WBRT within 3 weeks or SRS within 2 weeks; no RT to other sites within 2 weeks before first dose.
No active brain metastases or epidural disease. Treated brain metastases allowed if asymptomatic and off steroids for at least 2 weeks; resection or biopsy at least 3 months before treatment.
No tumor invading major blood vessels, the GI tract, or the airway (endotracheal or endobronchial) within 28 days. No rectal tumor masses.

No clinically significant GI bleeding within 6 months, hemoptysis of 2.5 mL or more within 1 month, or pulmonary hemorrhage within 3 months. No GI or GU fistula, perforation, obstruction, or intra-abdominal abscess within 2 years; no active diverticulitis, abscess, or GI obstruction within 12 months.

Cardiac: no NYHA class III-IV heart failure; no uncontrolled hypertension (above 150/90 despite treatment); QTcF 500 ms or less; no congenital long QT; no unstable angina, significant arrhythmia (atrial fibrillation allowed), stroke or TIA, MI, or cardiomyopathy within 6 months.
No major surgery within 3 months (6 weeks if healed in aggressive cancers) or minor surgery within 1 month; wounds fully healed. No serious non-healing wound or fracture.
No full-dose warfarin (low-dose warfarin up to 1 mg/day, aspirin up to 325 mg/day, LMWH, and thrombin or factor Xa inhibitors allowed). No chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors.

No active autoimmune disease or history that may recur and threaten organ function or need immunosuppression (for example, MS, Guillain-Barre, myasthenia, SLE, IBD, TEN/SJS). Vitiligo, replaced endocrinopathies, and topically controlled psoriasis or arthropathies allowed.
No positive HBsAg (unless PCR negative) or active HCV. HIV allowed on stable HAART with CD4 above 350 and undetectable viral load.
No organ or allogeneic stem cell transplant. No severe hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies. No active malignancy requiring systemic therapy within 2 years.
No severe infection needing IV treatment within 14 days and no uncompensated thyroid dysfunction within 7 days.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before registration).

amendments.text: Revision #1, the current version. Expanded tissue collection window before Step 1 from 12 to 36 months; allowed bone or soft tissue biopsy; added washout examples and >3-day AR-agent washout; treatment start within 7 days of randomization; updated primary objective and statistics, AE reporting, and study calendar.

schema.label: Step 1: Screening registration
schema.text: mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel (castrate-sensitive and/or castrate-resistant setting). Tumor tissue sent to the MD Anderson Clinical Pathology Laboratory for central AVPC-MS (aggressive variant molecular signature) IHC of TP53, RB1, and PTEN. Inconclusive results allow tissue resubmission.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: AVPC-MS-IHC status (positive vs negative), planned cabazitaxel starting dose (20 vs 25 mg/m²), Zubrod PS (0 vs 1-2), prior PARP inhibitor (yes vs no).

schema.label: Step 2: Randomization 1:1
schema.text: Within 70 days of Step 1, after AVPC-MS result is available. 21-day cycles, up to 10 cycles; primary G-CSF prophylaxis after every cycle; continued LHRH agonist/antagonist.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Cabazitaxel 20 or 25 mg/m² IV day 1 plus prednisone 5 mg PO twice daily (or 10 mg daily) days 1-21.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Cabazitaxel 20 or 25 mg/m² IV day 1 plus carboplatin AUC 4 IV day 1 (cabazitaxel first; max 900 mg), plus prednisone 5 mg PO twice daily (or 10 mg daily) days 1-21.

schema.label: Treatment duration
schema.text: Up to 10 cycles; physician may stop earlier after at least 2 cycles for CR/PR/SD (optimal cytoreduction) or cumulative toxicity. Imaging continues until protocol-defined progression.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Radiographic PFS (RECIST 1.1 or PCWG2 bone progression) in AVPC-MS-positive participants; if positive, then tested in AVPC-MS-negative participants.

eligibility: Step 1: Age ≥18 with histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma; treatment-related neuroendocrine carcinoma is eligible, de novo treatment-naive small cell prostate cancer is not.
Step 1: Metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer to bone and/or RECIST-measurable soft tissue, visceral, or nodal disease on bone scan and/or CT, PET-CT, or MRI of chest, abdomen, and pelvis.
Step 1: Any prior therapy allowed, but must include docetaxel (castrate-sensitive and/or castrate-resistant setting).

Step 1: FFPE bone or soft tissue biopsy material (blocks or 10 unstained slides) collected within 36 months before Step 1, submitted for central AVPC-MS IHC even if tested locally; metastatic CRPC-state samples preferred.
Step 2: Randomized within 70 days of Step 1 with AVPC-MS result in hand; protocol therapy planned to start within 7 days of randomization (Section 5.2 note says 14).

Step 2: Castrate testosterone <50 ng/dL within 28 days; metastatic disease on bone scan and/or chest/abdomen/pelvis imaging within 28 days (measurable visceral/soft tissue lesions ≥1.0 cm, nodes >1.5 cm short axis).
Step 2: Progressive disease by RECIST 1.1, bone progression (≥2 new bone scan lesions, or new or enlarging lytic lesion on CT/MRI), PCWG2 PSA rise, or unequivocal clinical progression.
Step 2: No prior cabazitaxel or carboplatin, and not on another therapeutic trial.

Step 2 washouts: chemotherapy, radium-223, sipuleucel-T, radioligands (e.g., Lu-177), and trial agents ≥21 days; abiraterone and second-generation antiandrogens >3 days; stereotactic RT ≥3 days; no other RT or kyphoplasty/vertebroplasty within 14 days; no major surgery within 28 days.
Step 2: No untreated fractures or cord compression. No symptomatic uncontrolled brain metastases (brain metastases properly treated, e.g., with stereotactic RT, are allowed).
Step 2: Zubrod PS 0-2 within 28 days.

Step 2 labs within 28 days: ANC ≥1.5 x 10^3/uL; platelets ≥100 x 10^3/uL (>75 x 10^3/uL if marrow infiltration); total bilirubin ≤ULN (Gilbert's, liver metastases, or acute tumor-associated illness <4x ULN); AST/ALT ≤3x ULN (≤4x with liver metastases); Cockcroft-Gault CrCl ≥30 mL/min.
Step 2: Peripheral neuropathy ≤ grade 2.
Step 2: No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Step 2: HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months.

amendments.text: Amendment #6D, the current version. Interim analyses made event-driven rather than time-driven per DSMC, and end-of-therapy and follow-up imaging footnotes revised to support the body-composition radiomics aim.

schema.label: Low Risk (all ages): active surveillance
schema.text: Stage I extracranial GCT after surgery, no chemotherapy. Strata: ovarian immature teratoma (any stage or grade, AFP ≤ 1,000 ng/mL, normal β-HCG); stage I testicular seminoma; stage I non-seminoma MGCT at any site (yolk sac, embryonal, or choriocarcinoma). Post-op markers must be falling. Tumor markers and imaging surveillance; patients with rising markers or recurrence may transfer to a Standard Risk arm by late randomization (not seminoma).

schema.label: Standard Risk 1 (age < 11): Randomize
schema.text: COG stage II-IV extracranial MGCT, any site (IGCCC does not apply). 21-day cycles.

arms.label: CEb x 4
arms.text: Carboplatin 600 mg/m2 day 1 (max 1200 mg), etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 day 1 (max 30 units); BSA-banded doses below 0.6 m2.

arms.label: PEb x 4
arms.text: Cisplatin 20 mg/m2 days 1-5, etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 day 1.

schema.label: Standard Risk 2 (age 11 to < 25): Randomize
schema.text: Ovarian COG stage II-III (FIGO IC-III) or testicular COG stage II-IV and IGCCC good risk. 21-day cycles.

arms.label: BEC x 3
arms.text: Carboplatin 600 mg/m2 day 1 (max 1200 mg), etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 days 1, 8, 15.

arms.label: BEP x 3
arms.text: Cisplatin 20 mg/m2 days 1-5, etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 days 1, 8, 15.

schema.label: Post-chemotherapy evaluation
schema.text: Markers and imaging within 6 weeks of day 21 of the last cycle; second-look resection of residual masses ≥ 1 cm within 6 weeks of imaging. Routine consolidation cycles are not recommended; further therapy for viable tumor is at physician discretion. Myeloid growth factor after each cycle.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Low Risk: 2-year OS of at least 95.7% for stage I MGCT and at least 88% for ovarian immature teratoma with surgery plus surveillance. Standard Risk: EFS with carboplatin- vs cisplatin-based therapy (CEb vs PEb in SR1, BEC vs BEP in SR2).

eligibility: Low Risk: no age limit. SR1: age < 11 years. SR2: age ≥ 11 and < 25 years.

Newly diagnosed extracranial GCT: stage I for Low Risk strata, malignant GCT stage II or higher for Standard Risk, with histology and stage as defined per stratum (yolk sac component must be more than microscopic when it is the only malignant element).

Histologic confirmation required, except recurrence of resected non-seminoma with markers > 5 x ULN on 2 measurements at least 1 week apart, or markers AFP ≥ 500 ng/mL or HCG ≥ 500 IU/L with typical imaging when biopsy or upfront resection is not appropriate.
SR2 testicular: IGCCC good risk using post-op markers (AFP < 1,000 ng/mL, β-HCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, LDH < 3.0 x normal).
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16).

Standard Risk only: CrCl or GFR ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum; total bilirubin ≤ 2 x ULN and AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (unless Gilbert's, liver involvement, or vanishing bile duct syndrome); ANC ≥ 750/mm3 and platelets ≥ 75,000/mm3.
No pure ovarian or extragonadal dysgerminoma/seminoma, pure mature teratoma, primary CNS GCT, or GCT with somatic malignant transformation.
No poor-risk GCT (age ≥ 11 with COG stage IV ovarian, stage II-IV extragonadal, or IGCCC intermediate/poor risk testicular).
No prior radiation therapy, except CNS irradiation of brain metastases in SR1 patients.
Standard Risk: no significant pre-existing respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin.
Standard Risk: not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

amendments.text: Revision #1, the current version. Revised amivantamab-hyaluronidase drug information and administration; broadened the immunocompromised definition (added MDS, polycythemia vera, myelofibrosis); clarified CT or MRI for disease assessment; updated premedication tables and cetuximab dosing; lab window changed to 72 hours; added safety run-in section.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Immunocompromised adults with locoregionally incurable (recurrent inoperable) or metastatic cutaneous SCC.

schema.label: Cohort A: Safety run-in
schema.text: Non-randomized; amivantamab-hyaluronidase as in Arm 1. Randomization opens if run-in safety criteria are met.

schema.label: Cohort B stratification
schema.text: Prior solid organ transplant (yes vs no), current systemic steroids or other immunosuppression (yes vs no), prior immune checkpoint inhibitor (yes vs no).

schema.label: Cohort B: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 28-day cycles, up to 24 cycles. Treatment starts within 14 days.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Amivantamab-hyaluronidase SC (abdomen): 1600 mg if <80 kg or 2240 mg if ≥80 kg, weekly days 1, 8, 15, 22 of cycle 1, then day 1 every 4 weeks (3520 mg or 4640 mg).

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Cetuximab 500 mg/m² IV days 1 and 15 of each cycle.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cohort A: safety and preliminary efficacy. Cohort B: progression-free survival.

eligibility: Age ≥18, Zubrod PS 0-2.

Pathologically proven cutaneous SCC (original or recurrent/metastatic lesion), measurable or non-measurable by RECIST 1.1 on CT or MRI chest/abdomen/pelvis within 28 days (42 days if non-measurable only); disease only in a prior RT field must show clear progression to count as measurable.
Exclusively locally recurrent disease only if surgery is contraindicated or not beneficial, or the patient has refused surgery or radiation.

Immunocompromised: CLL, acute leukemia, MDS, polycythemia vera, or myelofibrosis (any treatment status); lymphoma or myeloma on therapy or within 6 months after; organ transplant recipient (not corneal or lung) with stable allograft documented within 180 days; or autoimmune disease on active immunosuppression (prednisone >10 mg/day for 30 days, oral/SC immunosuppressant ≥90 days, or ≥2 IV doses within 90 days).
Vitiligo, psoriasis, type 1 diabetes, hypothyroidism, and resolved childhood asthma/atopy do not qualify as autoimmune indications.

Treated brain metastases must show no progression after CNS-directed therapy; active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease allowed only if no immediate CNS treatment is needed or anticipated in cycle 1.
No cetuximab or other EGFR inhibitor within 365 days.

Labs within 14 days: leukocytes ≥3 x 10^3/uL, ANC ≥1.5 x 10^3/uL, platelets ≥100 x 10^3/uL, total bilirubin ≤1.5x ULN (≤5x with Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤3x ULN (≤5x with liver metastases), creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min.
No current or past ILD/pneumonitis (including drug- or radiation-induced), no lung transplant, and no pulmonary GVHD.
NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history.
No active infection (antibiotics completed 1 week before treatment), active bleeding diathesis, or unstable ophthalmologic condition.

HIV allowed with effective ART and undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (negative pregnancy test within 72 hours before registration).

A Randomized Phase II Study of Tepotinib with or Without Ramucirumab in Participants with MET Exon 14 Skipping Positive Stage IV or Recurrent Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (LUNG-MAP SUB-STUDY)

amendments.text: Revision #3, the current version. Treatment-naive participants allowed (any number of prior lines, including zero); stage IV or recurrent NSCLC requirement and biomarker documentation clarified; recovery-from-toxicity criterion limited to prior NSCLC therapy; specimen sections updated to the current SWOG template.

schema.label: Step 1: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: On-study biomarker testing on LUNGMAP, or submission of documentation of previously completed testing (MET exon 14 skipping found outside Lung-MAP requires documentation). SWOG SDMC assigns MET exon 14 skipping-positive participants to S1900K.

schema.label: Step 2: S1900K randomization
schema.text: No stratification factors. About 25 eligible participants per arm. Treatment starts within 10 calendar days of sub-study randomization. 21-day cycles until progression or other removal criteria. Safety run-in with weekly toxicity monitoring in Cycle 1.

arms.label: Arm A (investigational)
arms.text: Ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV day 1 every 21 days plus tepotinib 450 mg PO daily, days 1-21 (taken at least 1 hour after the ramucirumab infusion ends).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Tepotinib 450 mg PO daily, days 1-21.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after sub-study randomization, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Response rate (confirmed or unconfirmed, complete or partial). Key secondary: all-grade treatment-related peripheral edema.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900K by the SWOG SDMC through the LUNGMAP screening protocol.
Stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation by tissue- or blood-based (ctDNA) NGS in a CLIA, ISO/IEC, CAP, or similarly certified laboratory.
No other known actionable oncogenic alteration (EGFR sensitizing or T790M, ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK, HER2 mutation, KRAS activating mutations, BRAF V600E, among others).

Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before sub-study randomization (non-measurable sites within 42 days). Effusions, ascites, or labs alone do not qualify. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts as measurable only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before sub-study randomization. No leptomeningeal disease, cord compression, or brain metastases unless locally treated and controlled and asymptomatic for at least 3 days after stereotactic radiation or 14 days after whole brain radiation, with no residual neurologic dysfunction and off corticosteroids for at least 24 hours.
Any number of prior lines for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC, including none (treatment-naive allowed); previously treated participants must have progressed on the most recent line.
No prior MET inhibitor (crizotinib, tivantinib, savolitinib, tepotinib, cabozantinib, foretinib, etc.) and no prior angiogenesis inhibitor (bevacizumab, ramucirumab, etc.).

No systemic therapy (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, investigational drug) within 21 days. No radiation therapy within 7 days before sub-study randomization, except CNS stereotactic radiation completed at least 3 days before and palliative bone RT completed at least 1 day before. No major surgery within 14 days. No planned concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior NSCLC therapy toxicity (except alopecia and vitiligo).
No history of interstitial lung disease that required steroids.
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before sub-study randomization.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 2.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); serum creatinine at or below ULN or creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault); baseline cystatin C.

No peripheral edema (grade above 0) within 28 days. No arterial thromboembolic event (including TIA or stroke) within 6 months. No uncontrolled hypertension (SBP above 150 or DBP above 90 mmHg) within 28 days.
No cirrhosis Child-Pugh B or worse, and no cirrhosis of any degree with hepatic encephalopathy or clinically meaningful ascites.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better.

Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load within 6 months if on treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.text: Single-arm phase II. Advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion, at least 1 prior line of therapy.

schema.text: Osimertinib 160 mg PO once daily, days 1-21 of 21-day cycles, until RECIST 1.1 progression or discontinuation criteria; treatment beyond progression allowed with continued clinical benefit.

schema.label: Sample size
schema.text: Simon two-stage design, 20 patients (18 evaluable); possible third stage if promising.

schema.text: Best objective response rate by RECIST 1.1.

eligibility: Age >= 18 years; ECOG performance status <= 1.
Pathologically confirmed NSCLC, stage IV, stage IIIB not amenable to definitive multimodality therapy, or recurrent after stage I-III (AJCC 7th edition).
EGFR exon 20 insertion detected in tumor tissue by any CLIA-certified tissue assay.
Measurable disease, with baseline imaging of all sites within 4 weeks before registration.
At least one prior line of therapy for advanced disease; no maximum.
No prior osimertinib; no PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 therapy within 6 months (180 days) before registration.

Labs within 4 weeks: Hgb >= 9.0 g/dL, WBC >= 3,000/mcL, ANC >= 1,500/mcL, platelets >= 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN (<= 3 x ULN with Gilbert's or liver metastases), AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN (<= 5 x ULN with liver metastases), creatinine <= 1.5 x ULN.
No active or symptomatic ILD or pneumonitis and no history of clinically significant ILD or radiation pneumonitis.

Radiation washouts before starting treatment: 4 weeks for RT to the lung fields, 2 weeks for palliative RT with fields including lung, 7 days for palliative RT to other sites, 6 months for curative-intent RT.
No symptomatic brain metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or cord compression; stable corticosteroid dose for 14 days allowed if asymptomatic.
LVEF >= institutional LLN (or >= 50% if LLN undefined) by ECHO or MUGA within 28 days.

No mean resting QTc >= 470 ms, prior drug-related QTc prolongation requiring discontinuation, Torsades-associated medications, clinically important ECG abnormalities or QT risk factors, or symptomatic NYHA II-IV heart failure.
No potent CYP3A4 inducers within 3 weeks; no St John's wort.
No clinically active second cancer; no other investigational agents (washout at least 2 weeks or 5 half-lives).
No uncontrolled intercurrent illness, unresolved prior toxicity > grade 1 (except alopecia and grade 2 platinum neuropathy), or GI conditions precluding oral absorption.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 2 weeks before registration).

studies.title: A Phase II Study of Daratumumab-Hyaluronidase for Chemotherapy-Relapsed/ Refractory Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) in T Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia/ Lymphoma (T-ALL/ T-LBL)

schema.label: Step 0: Preregistration
schema.text: T-ALL/T-LBL in morphologic CR, CRh, or CRi. Bone marrow aspirate (or peripheral blood in adults) sent for central MRD by flow cytometry at CHLA; clonoSEQ per institutional standard. Accrual 20.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Persistent or recurrent MRD >= 10^-4 by central flow cytometry, or MRD positive by clonoSEQ.

schema.label: Course 1
schema.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1,800 mg/30,000 units SC weekly x 4 (days 1, 8, 15, 22). Day 29 bone marrow MRD assessment.

schema.label: Course 1B (Day 29 MRD negative)
schema.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase weekly x 4 (days 36, 43, 50, 57), or allogeneic stem cell transplant at physician discretion.

schema.label: Course 1A (Day 29 MRD positive)
schema.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase weekly x 4 (days 36, 43, 50, 57) plus physician's choice of chemotherapy: Option 1, high-dose cytarabine 3,000 mg/m2 q12h x 4 (days 37-38) and methotrexate 1,000 mg/m2 over 24 hours day 36 (reduced doses for age >= 65 or GFR < 60) with IT methotrexate/cytarabine; Option 2, Capizzi escalating methotrexate (starting 100 mg/m2 days 36, 46, 56) with vincristine, pegaspargase or calaspargase pegol, and IT methotrexate; Option 3, nelarabine (adults 1,500 mg/m2 days 36, 38, 40). Day 64 (or count recovery) bone marrow MRD.

schema.label: Course 2 (MRD negative after Course 1A or 1B)
schema.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase every 2 weeks x 8 doses (days 1-99), or allogeneic transplant. MRD positive at Day 64: off treatment to follow-up. Maximum 16 daratumumab doses; no daratumumab after transplant.

schema.label: Off treatment
schema.text: Morphologic or flow evidence of disease with >= 5% marrow blasts. Intrathecal CNS prophylaxis or treatment allowed at investigator discretion.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Rate of complete MRD response by flow cytometry at Day 29 after 4 weekly doses of daratumumab-hyaluronidase.

eligibility: Age >= 12 and weight >= 40 kg.

T cell ALL or lymphoblastic lymphoma in first or later morphologic CR, CRh, or CRi after at least 2 blocks of intensive chemotherapy (age >= 65 unfit for intensive therapy may enroll after 1 cycle if in CR/CRh/CRi at least 28 days after starting therapy).
Step 1: persistent or recurrent MRD >= 10^-4 by central flow cytometry (CHLA), or >= 1 residual clonal cell per million by clonoSEQ.
Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant allowed, but no GVHD requiring ongoing immunosuppression (prednisone <= 10 mg/day allowed).
ECOG 0-2 for adults; Lansky >= 50 for patients < 18.
Labs within 7 days: ANC >= 750/uL, platelets >= 75,000/uL, total or direct bilirubin <= 2 mg/dL, AST/ALT <= 3.0 x ULN.
Adults: creatinine <= 1.5 x ULN or CrCl > 30 ml/min. Patients < 18: CrCl or radioisotope GFR >= 60 ml/min/1.73 m2, or creatinine <= 1.5 x ULN, or age/sex-based creatinine maximum.
No active CNS involvement at Step 1 (prior CNS disease allowed). Extramedullary disease outside the CNS allowed if asymptomatic.
Adults with cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic agents must be NYHA class 2B or better; patients < 18 need LVEF >= 50% or shortening fraction >= 27% within 6 months.

Adults with suspected or proven COPD need FEV1 >= 50% predicted within 6 months; controlled intermittent or mild persistent asthma allowed. Patients < 18: no uncontrolled asthma (no dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, room-air oximetry > 92%).

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

amendments.text: Initial protocol. The document history lists no later amendment.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Primary tumor site (oropharynx or oral cavity vs larynx or hypopharynx). Stage (rT4a or rN3a vs other). Prior use of PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors in the definitive setting (yes vs no).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1:1
schema.text: Salvage surgery is part of every arm. Schema version date October 10, 2025.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Salvage surgery.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Carboplatin plus paclitaxel, then salvage surgery.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Carboplatin plus paclitaxel plus cemiplimab (REGN2810), then salvage surgery.

schema.label: Postoperative therapy if indicated
schema.text: Only for patients with high-risk pathologic features: standard postoperative radiation therapy plus cisplatin. Drug doses are not printed on the schema page.

eligibility: Pathologically proven locally recurrent or persistent squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck arising in the oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx.
PD-L1 combined positive score at least 1, from a CLIA-certified laboratory.
Insurance or other payment coverage for neoadjuvant chemotherapy must be verified.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1, and the patient must be a candidate for salvage surgery and deemed surgically resectable without gross residual disease.
p16-positive oropharynx: T2, T3, or T4 and N0, N1, or N2. All other eligible patients: T2, T3, or T4a and N0, N1, N2a, N2b, N2c, or N3a, using AJCC 8th edition.

Oral cavity disease is eligible only when it is recurrent or persistent after prior surgery. Candidates for salvage laryngectomy for recurrent laryngeal cancer, done with curative intent, are eligible. Resectable lymph node-only recurrence is eligible.

No major vascular involvement, defined as more than 180 degrees of the common carotid or internal carotid artery, and no jugular foramen or prevertebral or paraspinous muscle involvement that precludes a curative resection. No distant metastatic disease.
Minimum workup: general history and physical examination, plus diagnostic-quality neck CT and PET/CT of the neck (PET with attenuation-correction CT of the neck, chest, and abdomen).
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2. Not pregnant and not nursing. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 30 days before registration for persons of childbearing potential.
Labs: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,500 cells/mm3, platelets at least 100,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention is allowed).

Creatinine clearance greater than 50 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault. Total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal (this limit does not apply to known Gilbert syndrome). AST and ALT at or below 3 times the institutional upper limit of normal.

Only one prior course of radiation, definitive or postoperative, is allowed. It must have been completed at least 6 months before registration, and the majority of the index persistent or recurrent volume (more than 50 percent) must have received at least 40 Gy.

Prior systemic therapy, including anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, in the definitive setting (neoadjuvant or adjuvant) is permitted if completed at least 4 months before registration. Prior systemic therapy, including immunotherapy, for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is not permitted.

No investigational anticancer agent within 4 weeks before registration. No New York Heart Association class III or IV. No active infection requiring intravenous antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals. No grade 3 or 4 peripheral neuropathy.
No history of allergic reaction to the study agent, to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition, or to immune checkpoint inhibitors, including excipients.

On-study guidance: HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. Persistent grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormalities must be reversible with replacement. Highly effective contraception is required during therapy and for 4 months after.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Newly diagnosed IDH wild-type glioblastoma within 7 weeks of diagnostic surgery, with pre-op MRI and post-op MRI within 3 weeks of surgery; MGMT status ordered. Must register before starting temozolomide/RT.

schema.label: Chemoradiation (standard of care, protocol-specified parameters)
schema.text: Photon 3DCRT or IMRT, 1.8-2.0 Gy daily to 59.4-60 Gy: cone-down plan (PTV1 46 Gy/23 fx including FLAIR, then PTV2 boost 14 Gy/7 fx to enhancing tumor and cavity; or 45 Gy + 14.4 Gy at 1.8 Gy) or single-volume plan (enhancing tumor/cavity plus FLAIR believed to be tumor, CTV 1.5-2.0 cm). Concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m2/day or per institution, Optune allowed. Protons, SRS, hypofractionation, and whole brain RT make the patient unevaluable.

schema.label: Maintenance
schema.text: Temozolomide alone for 24 weeks starting about 4 weeks after RT.

schema.label: Post-RT MRI
schema.text: DSC-MRI time point 1 at 4 (+/- 2) weeks and time point 2 at 12 (+/- 2) weeks after RT, plus any MRI within 12 (+/- 2) weeks, read centrally for progressive enhancement. NANO assessment at each.

schema.label: Progressive enhancement pathway (about 50%)
schema.text: Centrally confirmed progressive enhancement within 12 (+/- 2) weeks after RT: one research imaging biomarker within 3 weeks of central review (cohort 1, 18F-fluciclovine PET; cohort 2, MR spectroscopy), then time point 3 MRI at 12-22 weeks and NANO at every visit.

schema.label: No progressive enhancement (about 50%)
schema.text: Time point 3 MRI at 12-22 weeks after RT, then follow-up for outcomes.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: At least 12 months after the last enrollment per biomarker cohort, maximum 6 years. Up to about 440 enrolled (about 220 per biomarker to reach 100 with progressive enhancement).

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: For each biomarker (DSC-MRI, 18F-fluciclovine PET, MR spectroscopy), whether it stratifies patients with progressive enhancement within 12 weeks after RT into overall survival risk groups.

eligibility: Newly diagnosed IDH wild-type glioblastoma with pathologic proof by WHO 2021 criteria.
Planning standard chemoradiation per Section 5.1; not planning proton therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery, or abbreviated hypofractionated RT.
Diagnostic surgery within 7 weeks before registration, with no further GBM surgery planned before RT/temozolomide.
Pre-operative MRI with and without contrast and post-operative MRI with and without contrast within 3 weeks of surgery, both available for TRIAD upload.
MGMT methylation status ordered at registration.
No contraindication to MRI or gadolinium contrast, and demonstrated tolerance of pre-surgical MRI. No allergy to 18F-fluciclovine or MR contrast.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: mCSPC on ADT for 6-12 months plus an ARPI for at least 4 months, with suboptimal PSA response (PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL).

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: PSA 0.2-4 vs > 4 ng/mL; ARPI type (CYP17 inhibitor abiraterone vs AR antagonist apalutamide, enzalutamide, or darolutamide); liver metastasis on screening CT vs none; de novo vs recurrent mCSPC; time from ADT start ≥ 6 to < 9 months vs ≥ 9 to 12 months.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: N = 830. Treatment starts within 10 working days of enrollment.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Continue standard ADT + ARPI until protocol-defined progression or intolerable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 21 days for up to 6 cycles, plus continued standard ADT + ARPI until protocol-defined progression or intolerable toxicity.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Disease status and survival. PSA progression alone does not end treatment; clinical progression is also required.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival.

eligibility: Male, age ≥ 18 years.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma, or no histology but PSA > 100 ng/mL with radiographic metastatic disease at diagnosis.
Metastatic disease on conventional imaging (bone scan, CT, or MRI) or PSMA-PET at ADT initiation. PSA ≥ 2.0 ng/mL before starting ADT (for histologically confirmed cases).
ADT for mCSPC for at least 6 and no more than 12 months (± 3 weeks) at enrollment, and an ARPI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, or darolutamide) for at least 4 months (± 2 weeks).
Prior radiotherapy to the prostate bed and/or metastatic sites allowed, with recovery to grade ≤ 1. Persistent stable ADT toxicities (hot flushes, fatigue) of any grade allowed.
Serum testosterone < 1.7 nmol/L (50 ng/dL) and PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL within 28 days of enrollment.
Candidate for docetaxel. ECOG performance status 0-2.

Within 28 days: hemoglobin ≥ 80 g/L, ANC ≥ 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets ≥ 100 x 10^9/L, total bilirubin ≤ 1.0 x ULN (≤ 2.0 x ULN if Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤ 1.5 x ULN with alkaline phosphatase ≤ 2.5 x ULN, creatinine clearance ≥ 30 mL/min.
No confirmed PSA progression on ADT (25% rise above nadir and an absolute rise of 2.0 ng/mL, confirmed by a further 25% rise at least 3 weeks later).
No confirmed radiographic or clinical progression since starting ADT (new bone lesions judged to be flare are allowed).
No prior taxane chemotherapy, no grade ≥ 2 peripheral neuropathy, and no severe hypersensitivity to polysorbate 80 formulations.
No unstable angina, symptomatic pericarditis, or MI within 6 months, and no NYHA class III-IV heart failure.
No concurrent anticancer systemic therapy other than ADT and ARPI. No live vaccine within 30 days.
No high-grade neuroendocrine or small cell features (except patients enrolled without histology on the PSA > 100 ng/mL criterion).
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV must have undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must be treated and cured, or viral load undetectable if on treatment.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory bone marrow or peripheral blood submission to Adaptive (clonoSEQ) for real-time identification of a trackable clone for MRD testing. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration and randomization 1:2
schema.text: Stratified by age (65-74 vs 75 or older), 17p deletion (present if 6.5% or greater by FISH), and IGHV mutation status (>2% vs 2% or less). Treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

arms.label: Arm 1 (Regimen A, control)
arms.text: Zanubrutinib 160 mg PO BID continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity, up to 10 years. Restaging at C15D1; patients with response continue zanubrutinib.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Zanubrutinib 160 mg PO BID for cycles 1-3; TLS risk restaging at C3D15; sonrotoclax weekly ramp-up from C4D1 (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160 mg) to 320 mg daily from C6D1, with zanubrutinib continued, through C15D28. Restaging with peripheral blood MRD at C15D1.

schema.label: Arm 2A
schema.text: Undetectable MRD (<10 residual clonal cells per million nucleated cells), or detectable MRD with response other than PR, PR-L, CR, CCR, or CRi: stop therapy at C15D28.

schema.label: Step 2: Re-randomization 1:1
schema.text: Arm 2 patients with detectable MRD (10 or more residual clonal cells per million) and PR, PR-L, CR, CCR, or CRi.

arms.label: Arm 2B
arms.text: Continue zanubrutinib plus sonrotoclax C16D1 to C27D28 (12 additional cycles), then stop.

arms.label: Arm 2C
arms.text: Stop therapy at C15D28.

schema.label: Co-primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS from initial randomization: (1) MRD-guided Regimen C (Arms 2A+2B) vs continuous zanubrutinib (Arm 1); (2) fixed-duration Regimen B (Arms 2A+2C) vs continuous zanubrutinib. Follow-up up to 10 years.

eligibility: CLL/SLL by IWCLL 2018 criteria: 5 x 10^9/L or more clonal B lymphocytes in blood (CLL) or lymph node biopsy showing SLL; CD19/CD20/CD5-positive clonal B cells; if bright surface immunoglobulin or CD23 absent in >10% of cells, t(11;14) must be absent by FISH.

Meets IWCLL 2018 indication for treatment (progressive marrow failure with Hb <10 g/dL or platelets <100,000/mm3, massive/progressive/symptomatic splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy, poorly responsive autoimmune cytopenia, or constitutional symptoms).

No prior therapy for CLL, except palliative steroids or rituximab/steroids for autoimmune complications, which must be completed before enrollment; palliative steroids no more than 20 mg/day prednisone equivalent at registration.
Age 65 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must be treated and cured, or undetectable viral load if currently on treatment.
No active systemic anticoagulation with warfarin (off warfarin for at least 5 half-lives with normal INR before enrollment).
Patients with known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better; acute cardiac events within 6 months need careful evaluation.
No history of severe bleeding disorder, hemorrhagic stroke, or intracranial hemorrhage.
No known active progressive CNS disease.
No known condition preventing swallowing of oral agents.

Step 2 (Arm 2 only): detectable MRD (10 or more residual clonal cells per million nucleated cells) in peripheral blood by clonoSEQ at C15 restaging, and response of PR, PR-L, CR, CCR, or CRi.

amendments.text: Revision #5, the current version. Documents permanent closure of Arm 2 (platinum/etoposide plus atezolizumab followed by observation) effective July 9, 2026; randomization now to Arms 1 and 3 only. ECOG-ACRIN champion updated and specimen kit link revised.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Advanced or metastatic poorly differentiated extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma. Treatment starts within 7 calendar days of registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Zubrod 0-1 vs 2; tumor origin: prostate vs GI vs other (non-prostate, non-GI, or unknown).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1:1
schema.text: Induction is 4 cycles of 21 days. Platinum is physician's choice: carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 IV day 1, with etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3. A single pre-registration cycle of platinum/etoposide does not count toward the 4.

arms.label: Arm 1 (experimental)
arms.text: Atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV day 1 plus platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles; if no progression, maintenance atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV every 21 days for up to 17 cycles (maximum 1 year).

arms.label: Arm 2 (experimental, closed)
arms.text: Atezolizumab plus platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles, then observation for 1 year. Permanently closed to accrual effective July 9, 2026; new participants are randomized to Arm 1 or Arm 3 only.

arms.label: Arm 3 (control)
arms.text: Platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles, then observation for 1 year.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 5 years after registration, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival from randomization, tested in fixed sequence: Arm 1 vs Arm 3, then Arm 2 vs Arm 3, then Arm 1 vs Arm 2.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed extrapulmonary poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma by WHO criteria, with Ki-67 of 55% or higher (Ki-67 not required for genitourinary origin); local pathology confirmation is sufficient.

Unresectable or metastatic disease not eligible for definitive therapy, with RECIST-evaluable (measurable or non-measurable) disease on contrast CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (or CT chest plus MRI abdomen/pelvis) within 28 days before registration. PET or bone scan alone is not acceptable.

Brain MRI (or contrast head CT) within 28 days only if clinically indicated. No symptomatic CNS metastases and no known or suspected leptomeningeal disease. Treated brain metastases need no progression within 28 days and steroids stopped at least 14 days; untreated lesions must be 2.0 cm or smaller, without mass effect, edema, or progression, and need no more than dexamethasone 2 mg/day (or prednisone 10 mg).

No prior therapy for advanced or metastatic NEC except one cycle of platinum plus etoposide. Prior platinum-based therapy with or without radiation or surgery for localized or locally advanced NEC allowed if completed at least 6 months before registration. Prostate or urothelial NEC: prior chemotherapy for the non-NEC component allowed if completed at least 24 weeks before registration.

No prior immune checkpoint inhibitor (anti-PD-1, PD-L1, PD-L2, CTLA-4, CD137 agonist, or other) for any neuroendocrine neoplasm; checkpoint inhibitors for other cancers allowed if the last dose was at least 12 months before registration. No systemic immunostimulatory agents (interferon, IL-2) within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives.

No active systemic therapy for another cancer except hormonal therapy (ADT may continue; enzalutamide or apalutamide only after chemotherapy; darolutamide allowed during chemotherapy; no abiraterone or other glucocorticoid-containing regimens). Denosumab must be stopped and replaced with a bisphosphonate.
Age 18 or older; Zubrod performance status 0-2 within 28 days.

Within 14 days (at least 21 days after day 1 of any pre-registration chemotherapy cycle): ANC at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, AST and ALT up to 2.5 x ULN, total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN, creatinine clearance above 50 mL/min. No uncontrolled or symptomatic hypercalcemia.
No immunodeficiency and no systemic steroids above hydrocortisone 20 mg/day equivalent or other immunosuppression within 14 days.
No active or prior autoimmune disease, except hypothyroidism on replacement, controlled type 1 diabetes on insulin, and limited skin-only eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo.

No idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced or idiopathic pneumonitis, or active pneumonitis on screening CT (radiation pneumonitis confined to the radiation field is allowed).
No NYHA class II or higher heart disease, MI within 3 months, unstable arrhythmia, or unstable angina.
No major surgery (other than diagnostic) within 28 days or planned during treatment. No grade 2 or higher infection at registration and no known active tuberculosis.
Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment; known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant. No live attenuated vaccine within 28 days before treatment, during atezolizumab, or for 5 months after.
No severe hypersensitivity to chimeric or humanized antibodies, CHO cell products, atezolizumab, cisplatin, carboplatin, or etoposide.
Not pregnant.

studies.title: Multimodality Therapy with Immunotherapy in Stage I-IIIA Pleural Mesothelioma

amendments.text: Update #04: staging scans reduced from every 3 months for 3 years to every 3 months for 2 years; pre-registration TSH only when clinically indicated; surgery must be within 90 days of last immunotherapy dose with re-registration; patients stopping immunotherapy for adverse events may still be considered for surgery; commercial-agent CAEPRs removed; editorial changes.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Stage I-IIIA pleural mesothelioma (UICC 8th edition), untreated. 1 cycle = 6 weeks.

schema.label: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy
schema.text: Nivolumab 360 mg IV on days 1 and 22 plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV on day 1 of each 6-week cycle, for 2 cycles. Then assessed for surgery.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration and surgery
schema.text: Register 21-90 days after the last immunotherapy dose. Extended pleurectomy/decortication or extrapleural pneumonectomy per surgeon, aiming for macroscopic cytoreduction, within 90 days of the last immunotherapy dose. Patients not eligible for surgery are observed and treated at physician discretion.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 5 years from registration or until death. Co-primary endpoints: surgery rate after ipilimumab/nivolumab and 12-month PFS rate.

eligibility: Step 1: Pleural mesothelioma of any histology, stage I-IIIA (UICC TNM 8th edition), measurable or non-measurable disease.

Step 1: No chest wall invasion, peritoneal spread, contralateral pleural involvement, mediastinal organ involvement, vertebral involvement, contralateral intrathoracic nodal metastases, or any supraclavicular nodes.
Step 1: No prior treatment for mesothelioma and no prior hormones or chemotherapy (hormones for non-disease conditions allowed).
Step 1: Age 18 or older; ECOG PS 0-2 or Karnofsky 60% or higher.

Step 1: ANC at least 1,000/mm3, leukocytes at least 2,000/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, creatinine up to 1.5 x ULN or creatinine clearance at least 40 mL/min, total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert below 3.0 mg/dL), AST/ALT and alkaline phosphatase up to 3.0 x ULN.

Step 1: No active, known, or suspected autoimmune disease (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hypothyroidism on replacement, psoriasis not needing systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur without a trigger are allowed).
Step 1: No history of symptomatic interstitial lung disease.

Step 1: No active systemic infection requiring therapy and no positive hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C antibody. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.
