A Phase 3 Study of Dinutuximab Added to Intensive Multimodal Therapy for Children with Newly Diagnosed High-Risk Neuroblastoma

schema.label: Induction cycle 1
schema.text: All patients start with topotecan and cyclophosphamide. Three callbacks follow: treatment-arm randomization, end of induction, and end of extended induction.

schema.label: ALK branch
schema.text: A qualifying somatic ALK aberration found by APEC14B1 before induction cycle 1, day 24, removes the patient from ANBL2131 so the patient can enroll on ANBL1531 Arm E when that arm is open and the patient is eligible (section 4.1 limits this path to patients at least 1 year old). If Arm E is unavailable or the patient is not eligible, the patient stays on ANBL2131 and is randomized. An ALK result that is still unknown on day 24 does not delay randomization, and the assigned arm continues even if an ALK aberration is found later. An ALK inhibitor cannot be added on study.

schema.label: Randomization
schema.text: Randomization is after induction cycle 1, once ALK status is known or day 24 has passed. It is stratified by INRG stage (M or MS vs L2), ALK status (aberrant vs wild type vs unknown or pending), and MYCN status (amplified vs non-amplified vs unknown or pending), using APEC14B1 results. Surgery is planned after induction cycle 4 and may be after cycle 5. Dinutuximab given during induction or extended induction is investigational supply. Post-consolidation dinutuximab is commercial supply.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Induction cycle 2 is topotecan and cyclophosphamide, followed by stem-cell harvest. Cycle 3 is cisplatin and etoposide. Cycle 4 is vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide, then surgery. Cycle 5 is cisplatin and etoposide. After the end-of-induction evaluation and callback, a good end-of-induction response goes to COG standard consolidation with tandem stem-cell transplant and radiotherapy, then post-consolidation GM-CSF, dinutuximab, and isotretinoin for cycles 1-5 and isotretinoin alone for cycle 6. Progressive disease during induction cycles 3-5, or a poor end-of-induction response, goes to extended induction or off-protocol therapy at the treating team's discretion, after disease evaluation and the callback.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Same induction backbone, surgery, response branches, consolidation, and post-consolidation as Arm A, with dinutuximab and GM-CSF added on induction cycles 2-5. The schema recommends GM-CSF in cycle 2 together with G-CSF for apheresis. The treatment plan gives dinutuximab on days 2-5 of cycles 2-5, and sargramostim during cycles 3-5, strongly encouraged in cycle 2.

schema.label: Extended induction
schema.text: Irinotecan and temozolomide on days 1-5, dinutuximab on days 2-5, and GM-CSF, given as 2-cycle blocks with disease evaluation after each block. Poor end-of-induction response can continue to a maximum of 6 cycles. Progression during extended induction is off-protocol therapy. A good response proceeds to standard consolidation and the same post-consolidation immunotherapy. An end-of-extended-induction callback is required. For BSA at least 0.6 m2, temozolomide is 100 mg/m2 per dose. These patients are not eligible for primary-site CTV dose reduction.

schema.label: Primary-site radiotherapy
schema.text: Adjuvant radiotherapy to the primary site is required. The standard dose is 21.6 Gy in 12 fractions of 1.8 Gy (GyRBE where applicable). Patients with a good end-of-induction response and a primary-site complete response may receive 18 Gy to the CTV or PTV while the GTV still receives 21.6 Gy. Extended induction excludes that CTV reduction even after a primary-site complete response.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Event-free survival, comparing early chemoimmunotherapy during induction with induction that does not include it.

eligibility: Patients must enroll on APEC14B1 and consent to eligibility screening and the Molecular Characterization Initiative before ANBL2131.
Age is 30 years or younger at the initial high-risk diagnosis, and body surface area is at least 0.25 m2.
Diagnosis is neuroblastoma or nodular ganglioneuroblastoma, verified by tumor pathology or by clumps of tumor cells in the bone marrow with elevated urinary catecholamines.

High-risk disease is any age with INRG stage L2, MS, or M and MYCN amplification; age at least 547 days with INRG stage M regardless of biology; any age with initial INRG stage L1 MYCN-amplified disease that progresses to stage M without systemic chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis; or age at least 547 days with initial INRG stage L1, L2, or MS disease that progresses to stage M without systemic chemotherapy within 6 months.
Patients aged 365 to 546 days with INRG stage M and MYCN-non-amplified disease are excluded, as are patients at least 547 days old with INRG stage L2 and MYCN-non-amplified disease.

No prior anticancer therapy is allowed except emergency topotecan and cyclophosphamide within the permitted timing, one cycle of low- or intermediate-risk chemotherapy for disease later found to be high risk, or localized emergency radiation to a life-threatening or function-threatening site.

Known HIV infection is allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months, and there must be no known contraindication to peripheral-blood stem-cell collection.

Eligibility laboratories are within 7 days before enrollment: total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN for age, ALT at most 10 x ULN with the study ULN set at 45 U/L, and either shortening fraction at least 27% or ejection fraction at least 50%.
Renal eligibility is the age- and sex-specific maximum serum creatinine, or a 24-hour creatinine clearance or directly measured GFR of at least 70 mL/min/1.73 m2; estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Creatinine maxima in mg/dL are 0.4 under 6 months, 0.5 from 6 months to under 1 year, 0.6 from 1 to under 2 years, 0.8 from 2 to under 6 years, 1 from 6 to under 10 years, and 1.2 from 10 to under 13 years for both sexes; from 13 to under 16 years they are 1.5 for males and 1.4 for females, and at 16 years or older they are 1.7 for males and 1.4 for females.

Bone marrow failure syndromes, chronic immunosuppression other than allergy prevention or treatment and adrenal replacement, and primary immunodeficiency requiring ongoing immune globulin are exclusions; topical and inhaled corticosteroids are allowed.

Pregnancy, planned breastfeeding, and sexual activity without agreement to use effective contraception are exclusions, and a pregnancy test is required before enrollment for female patients of childbearing potential.

Staging imaging and marrow studies are obtained within 14 days before enrollment, except baseline MIBG or PET, which may be done within 14 days after cycle 1 starts without affecting eligibility; after one cycle of intermediate-risk therapy, those studies must be within 21 days before ANBL2131 therapy.

HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months of registration.
No allogeneic tissue or organ transplant. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

schema.label: Study entry and randomization
schema.text: Project EveryChild APEC14B1 is strongly encouraged, then study entry and randomization. VAC2200 is vincristine, dactinomycin, and cyclophosphamide (dose = 2,220 mg/m2). VAC1200/VI is vincristine, dactinomycin, and cyclophosphamide (dose = 1,200 mg/m2) with vincristine and irinotecan. VINO-CPO is vinorelbine and oral cyclophosphamide. DPE is delayed primary excision. Progressive disease is off protocol therapy. If distant metastatic-site radiotherapy is required, additional imaging is obtained after cycle 13 (week 39) for radiotherapy planning.

arms.label: Regimen A, VAC2200
arms.text: Cycles 1-4 of VAC2200, disease evaluation after cycle 3, delayed primary excision if applicable, cycles 5-8 of VAC2200, disease evaluation after cycle 8, cycles 9-14 of VAC2200, then end of therapy. Primary-site radiotherapy, if applicable, during cycle 5 and cycle 6. Metastatic-site radiotherapy, if applicable, during cycle 14.

arms.label: Regimen B, VAC1200/VI
arms.text: Cycles 1-4 of VAC1200/VI, disease evaluation after cycle 3, delayed primary excision if applicable, cycles 5-8, disease evaluation after cycle 8, cycles 9-14, disease evaluation after cycle 14, then maintenance VINO-CPO cycles 1-6, then end of therapy. Same primary-site radiotherapy window (cycles 5 and 6) and metastatic-site radiotherapy window (cycle 14).

eligibility: Age <= 50 years at enrollment. No lower age bound is printed.
Newly diagnosed soft tissue rhabdomyosarcoma of any subtype except adult-type pleomorphic, based on institutional histopathologic classification. FOXO1 fusion status must be known before enrollment.
FOXO1 fusion-negative: stage 2 or 3, Group III; or stage 4, Group IV, and < 10 years old. FOXO1 fusion-positive: stages 1-3, Groups I-III.
The protocol includes as embryonal RMS the 2020 WHO embryonal RMS variants (typical, dense, and botryoid) and spindle cell/sclerosing RMS. Alveolar RMS includes classic and solid variants.

FOXO1 status may be confirmed by cytogenetics, FISH, or next-generation sequencing and must be available to enroll and uploaded for randomization. Institutional PAX3 versus PAX7 testing is not required. Patients < 10 years old with stage 4 disease who are institutional fusion-negative but later fusion-positive by MCI or other testing are considered metastatic fusion-positive and come off study.
Appropriate lymph node sampling based on the primary site is required.
Lansky >= 50 if <= 16 years, or Karnofsky >= 50 if > 16 years.

Enroll before treatment begins. Protocol therapy is projected to start no later than 5 calendar days after enrollment. Eligibility labs within 7 days. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, and serum creatinine before therapy if more than 7 days have elapsed. Clinical studies and disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 21 days.
ANC >= 750/µL and platelets >= 75,000/µL.

Pediatric renal function (age < 18 years): serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 1 month to < 6 months 0.4/0.4, 6 months to < 1 year 0.5/0.5, 1 to < 2 years 0.6/0.6, 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable. Elevated creatinine from obstructive hydronephrosis secondary to tumor is still eligible if unimpeded flow is established by diversion (percutaneous nephrostomies or ureteric stents).

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection, based on actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, multiplied by 0.85 if female.

Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, or < 3 times the upper limit of normal for age if there is biliary obstruction by tumor. ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.
No uncontrolled infection. No previous or concurrent cancer treated with chemotherapy and/or radiation. Surgical resection alone of a previous or concurrent cancer is allowed.

No CNS rhabdomyosarcoma: malignant cells in cerebrospinal fluid, intra-parenchymal brain metastases separate and distinct from the primary tumor (direct extension from a parameningeal primary is allowed), or diffuse leptomeningeal disease. No known Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

No chemotherapy, excluding steroids, and no radiation for rhabdomyosarcoma before enrollment, except emergency radiation for life-threatening tumor complications if the patient is consented to ARST2531 before that radiation. Chemotherapy or radiation for a non-malignant condition is allowed, but chemotherapy for the non-malignant condition must stop before protocol therapy.
Pregnant patients are not eligible (pregnancy test required for females of childbearing potential). Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

eligibility: Pathologically proven stage IIB or III node-positive non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 8th edition, with known PD-L1 status before registration. A primary tumor and at least one nodal metastasis are required.
Up to 4 cycles of systemic therapy for this cancer before registration are allowed. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed.
Patients who refuse surgery, and patients who are unresectable or medically inoperable, are eligible. Separate nodules in the same lobe as the primary are eligible.
No distant metastases on FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor 7 cm or smaller. Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.
Blood counts must be adequate for chemotherapy and radiotherapy, at the treating physician's discretion. Creatinine clearance at least 25 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault.
A non-malignant pleural effusion is allowed if it is not a known exudate. A visible effusion needs a negative cytology. A minimal effusion that cannot be tapped safely is allowed.

A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it is not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment. A negative pregnancy test within 14 days is required when relevant, and consent is required.
No prior radiotherapy to this cancer, and no prior radiotherapy to the region that would overlap fields and impede treatment.
Patients without an identifiable primary and at least one node are not eligible. T3-4 N0 and T0 N1-3 are not eligible.

A central primary under 2 cm from involved nodal disease that would make the SBRT and nodal fields overlap the proximal bronchial tree or esophagus is not eligible, with the exception stated for segmental nodes.
Pregnant participants, and participants unwilling to stop breastfeeding or to use highly effective contraception for the labeled interval after the chosen systemic therapy, are not eligible.

studies.title: Radioligand Efficacy Comparison by Initial PSA-Response Outcome in Metastatic CRPC with Lutetium 177Lu PSMA RLT (RECIPROCAL)

schema.label: Step 0
schema.text: Two doses of lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy. Patients whose PSA falls by at least 50% after those two cycles continue to randomization. Patients without that decline, and any other patient who does not move to Step 1, are treated at investigator discretion and are not followed.

schema.label: Step 1 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Each lutetium dose in the treatment plan is 7.4 GBq plus or minus 10% (200 mCi). Treatment continues until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients are followed for 5 years or until death. A trigger for the adaptive arm is an absolute PSA rise of at least 4 ng/dL, a PSA rise of at least 25% above nadir, radiographic progression by PCWG3, or clinical progression. The schema prints the absolute rise as ng/dL.

arms.label: Arm 1: standard dosing
arms.text: The next lutetium dose is scheduled in 3 weeks, then doses 3 through 6 are given every 6 weeks, plus or minus 1 week.

arms.label: Arm 2: adaptive dosing
arms.text: PSA is checked every 3 weeks starting on cycle 2, day 42, plus or minus 7 days. If no trigger is met, PSA checks continue every 3 weeks. If a PSA rise or clinical progression is met, the next dose is scheduled for 3 weeks later, plus or minus 1 week, and PSA monitoring resumes after that dose. This continues until doses 3 through 6 are given or disease progresses.

schema.label: Co-primary endpoints
schema.text: Overall survival for PSA-adaptive lutetium dosing compared with standard dosing every 6 weeks, and quality of life by FACT-P total score averaged over the first 30 months.

eligibility: Step 0 requires prostate adenocarcinoma confirmed by histology, pathology, or cytology, and progressive metastatic castration-resistant disease.
PSMA PET/CT with 68Ga-PSMA-11, 18F-DCFPyL, or 18F-rhPSMA-7.3 must show uptake greater than liver and no PSMA-negative measurable soft-tissue disease, and PSA must be greater than 2.0 ng/mL.

Progression is two consecutive PSA rises over a reference value from at least 1 week earlier, with a minimum start value of 2.0 ng/mL, or soft-tissue growth of at least 20% in the sum of diameters from the nadir sum or a new lesion, or bone progression by 2+2 PCWG3 criteria.

Prior orchiectomy or ongoing androgen deprivation is required, with testosterone below 50 ng/dL or below 1.7 nmol/L, and at least one of apalutamide, darolutamide, enzalutamide, or abiraterone is required and must stop at least 4 weeks before pre-registration.

Taxane chemotherapy for mCRPC is excluded, docetaxel for metastatic hormone-sensitive disease or neoadjuvant or adjuvant use is allowed if completed at least 12 months before pre-registration, and clinically significant prior toxicity must have recovered to grade 2 or less.

A stable bisphosphonate or denosumab regimen for at least 30 days is allowed, and strontium-89, samarium-153, rhenium-186, rhenium-188, radium-223, hemi-body irradiation within 6 months, and any prior PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy are excluded.

Systemic anticancer therapy and investigational agents within 28 days, and transfusion within 30 days before pre-registration, are excluded, and there is no concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radioligand therapy, or investigational therapy.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 2 or better, there is no acute biliary or urinary obstruction and no symptomatic or impending cord compression, and the patient can read and comprehend English or Spanish.

Treated brain metastases are allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression, the patient is neurologically stable and asymptomatic, and corticosteroids are not used to maintain neurologic function; treated stable epidural or canal disease without deficit is allowed, and parenchymal CNS disease requires brain MRI or contrast CT.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is allowed, hepatitis B must be undetectable on suppression if indicated, hepatitis C must be cured or undetectable on treatment, and there is no known hypersensitivity to the study therapy or its analogs.
Patients with known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy should be NYHA class II or better, and myocardial infarction, CABG, or angina within 6 months before pre-registration is excluded.

Step 0 labs are ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, total bilirubin below 1.5 x ULN or below 3 x ULN in Gilbert syndrome, eGFR at least 40 mL/min/1.73 m2 by MDRD, and ALT or AST at most 3.0 x ULN without liver metastases or at most 5.0 x ULN with liver metastases.

Step 1 requires two completed doses of lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy, a PSA decline of at least 50% from cycle 1 day 1 to cycle 2 day 22 plus or minus 3 days, ECOG 2 or better, and repeat ANC, platelet, eGFR, and ALT or AST thresholds, with hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL and transfusions allowed; Step 1 does not restate a bilirubin limit.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Metastatic (resected/ablated liver oligometastases) vs non-metastatic; Recurrence Risk Score (Zaidi) >= 6 vs < 6

schema.text: Dynamic balancing; treatment starts within 15 days of registration

arms.text: Capecitabine 750 mg/m2 PO twice daily days 1-14 plus temozolomide 200 mg/m2 PO once daily days 10-14 (capped at 400 mg/day), 28-day cycles x 4

arms.text: Surveillance, no adjuvant therapy

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Recurrence-free survival

eligibility: Age >= 18; Zubrod performance status 0-2.
Histologically confirmed well-differentiated pancreatic NET resected 14-120 days before registration, with R0 or R1 resection.
Ki-67 from the surgical specimen >= 3% and <= 55% (use the highest value if more than one is reported).

Localized disease must have a Recurrence Risk Score (Zaidi) >= 3: symptomatic tumor (GI bleed, jaundice, obstruction, pain, pancreatitis) 1 point; primary >= 2 cm 2 points; Ki-67 3-20% 1 point or 21-55% 6 points; node positive 1 point. Score is not required for resected liver-only metastatic disease.
Resection or ablation of up to 5 liver oligometastases at the time of pNET resection is allowed; no unresected or unablated metastatic disease.
Multiphase CT or contrast MRI of the abdomen within 90 days before registration showing no metastatic disease (other than resected/ablated liver oligometastases).
No clinically apparent CNS metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
No prior neoadjuvant therapy for pNET (preoperative somatostatin analogs allowed).
No postoperative somatostatin analogs for tumor control; a short course for surgical complications (e.g., fistula prevention) is allowed if stopped by registration.
Recovered from surgery.

Within 28 days: WBC >= 3,000/uL, ANC >= 1,500/uL, platelets >= 100,000/uL, total bilirubin <= ULN (<= 5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN, creatinine <= 1.5 x ULN and calculated CrCl >= 50 mL/min.
Able to swallow pills; no known absorption problems; no allergy to temozolomide or capecitabine analogs.
No planned warfarin during protocol treatment (other anticoagulants allowed).
No arterial thromboembolic event, unstable angina, or MI within 90 days before registration.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No active or uncontrolled infection; no serious medical or psychiatric illness affecting participation.
Not pregnant.

Randomized Phase II Trial of Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate Versus Everolimus in Somatostatin Receptor Positive Bronchial Neuroendocrine Tumors

schema.label: Central SSTR review
schema.text: Patients with somatostatin-receptor-positive bronchial neuroendocrine tumor have SSTR positivity confirmed by the Alliance ICL at IROC Ohio. Arm 1 cycles are 56 days and Arm 2 cycles are 28 days. P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers must be stopped 7 days before registration.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Arm 1 is given at a CTEP-authorized targeted radiopharmaceutical facility. Arm 2 is given at the registering institution. Follow-up may be done at a non-registering institution. Patients are followed for 5 years or until death.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate, 7400 MBq (7.4 GBq, 200 mCi) plus or minus 10%, every 8 weeks for 4 doses, or until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Everolimus 10 mg orally once daily on days 1-28 of each cycle, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent.

schema.label: Crossover re-registration
schema.text: Arm 2 patients with RECIST progression confirmed in real time by IROC Ohio may re-register and cross over to up to 4 cycles of lutetium Lu 177 dotatate.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival, comparing lutetium Lu 177 dotatate with everolimus in bronchial neuroendocrine tumor.

eligibility: Step 0 requires a well- or moderately differentiated bronchial neuroendocrine tumor, reported as well- or moderately differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, low- or intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumor, or typical or atypical carcinoid, from the primary or a metastasis.

Functional and nonfunctional tumors are allowed, and poorly differentiated or high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, including large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and small-cell lung cancer, and mixed tumors such as adenocarcinoid, are excluded.
Disease is recurrent, locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic, with radiologic progression in the 12 months before pre-registration.

SSTR PET, preferably 68Ga-DOTATATE, must be positive in the 12 months before pre-registration, with uptake greater than background liver in every measurable lesion, and documentation within 6 months is preferred.
Step 1 requires central confirmation of that SSTR positivity by the Alliance ICL at IROC Ohio.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 on CT or MRI is required, at least 1 cm, or at least 1.5 cm in short axis for nodes, and a lesion treated with percutaneous therapy or radiotherapy counts only if it has clearly progressed.

Treatment-naive and previously treated patients are allowed, previously treated disease must have progressed on that therapy, and prior peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy and prior mTOR inhibitors are excluded.

Prior hepatic-artery embolization or ablation is allowed if measurable disease remains outside the treated area or a treated site has progressed, liver-directed therapy must finish at least 28 days before registration, and yttrium-90 radioembolization must finish at least 6 weeks before.

Lung or mediastinal stereotactic radiotherapy must finish at least 14 days before registration and conventional radiotherapy at least 28 days before, systemic anticancer therapy and major surgery must finish at least 28 days before with wound healing complete, and prior toxicity should be grade 1 or less except alopecia, fatigue, and irreversible effects such as cisplatin neuropathy.

A somatostatin analog may continue only for a functional tumor that already progressed radiographically on a somatostatin analog, and P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers must stop 7 days before registration.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 0-2, and patients are not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative pregnancy test within 28 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

Labs are hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL, platelets at least 75,000/mm3, ANC at least 1,500/mm3, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or Cockcroft-Gault clearance at least 40 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 2.0 x ULN, albumin at least 2.8 g/dL, and AST or ALT at most 3.0 x ULN.
If Gilbert syndrome and total bilirubin is above 2.0 x ULN, direct bilirubin must be at most 2.0 x ULN.

CNS metastases must be treated and clinically stable for at least 14 days, with weaning steroids if steroids are used, and no other active malignancy is expected to need therapy during the study except non-melanoma skin cancer and in situ carcinoma such as breast or cervical.

Known active hepatitis B is excluded unless the viral load is undetectable on suppression, known active hepatitis C with detectable HCV RNA is excluded, and HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months of registration is allowed.

Active infection requiring antifungals or antibiotics in the prior 3 days, a live attenuated vaccine in the prior 7 days, decompensated cirrhosis, prior symptomatic or treated drug-induced pneumonitis, inability to swallow, impaired absorption of an oral agent, and hypersensitivity to everolimus or another rapamycin analog are exclusions.

Re-registration for crossover requires centrally confirmed RECIST progression, ECOG 0-2, the same laboratory thresholds, and a negative pregnancy test within 28 days for women of childbearing potential.

schema.text: First 6-12 evaluable participants (adult and pediatric run-ins) non-randomly assigned to Arm 1 with revumenib dose de-escalation (rolling-6), DLT assessment through cycle 1.

schema.label: Cohort A stratification
schema.text: Age (<18 vs ≥18) and end-of-induction flow MRD (≥0.01% vs <0.01% vs unknown).

schema.label: Cohort A: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Two 28-day cycles; IT methotrexate days 1 and 15 each cycle; dexamethasone 20 mg before blinatumomab on day 1. Treatment starts within 14 days.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Blinatumomab continuous IV (28 mcg/day adults; 15 mcg/m²/day if <18, max 28) days 1-28 plus revumenib PO every 12 hours (270 mg if >40 kg, 160 mg/m² if <40 kg) days 4-28 of cycle 1 and days 1-28 of cycle 2.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Blinatumomab alone, same schedule, 2 cycles.

schema.label: Cohort A after protocol cycles
schema.text: Children stay on protocol through COG-style consolidation, interim maintenance, and delayed intensification (removed if flow MRD ≥5% after consolidation or ≥0.01% after blinatumomab cycle 2); maintenance is off study. Adults: allogeneic HCT allowed; non-transplant adults 18-54 recommended CALGB 10403, ≥55 low-intensity chemotherapy plus blinatumomab, per physician.

schema.label: Cohort B (single arm, age ≥55)
schema.text: Newly diagnosed untreated Ph-negative KMT2A-rearranged B- or T-ALL or ALAL. Feasibility run-in with revumenib de-escalation, then expansion. Induction (35 days): vincristine 1.5 mg/m² (max 2 mg; 1 mg/m² if ≥70) days 1, 8, 15, 22, dexamethasone 5 mg/m² twice daily days 1-7 and 15-21, daunorubicin 25 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15, IT cytarabine and IT methotrexate, revumenib days 8-28. If CR, CD19+ B-lineage, and no grade ≥3 revumenib toxicity: 2 cycles of blinatumomab 28 mcg/day plus revumenib (42-day cycles). T-ALL comes off after induction.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 10 years after registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cohort A: safety in run-in; MRD-negative CR by clonoSEQ after one cycle in MRD-positive participants, then MRD event-free survival (hierarchical). Cohort B: feasibility of revumenib with reduced-intensity chemotherapy.

eligibility: Cohort A: B-ALL or ALAL with KMT2A translocation documented locally (cytogenetics, FISH, or NGS); CD19 expression at any level at diagnosis; Ph-negative; no lymphoid blast crisis of CML or prior TKI for CML.

Cohort A: Morphological CR1 (marrow blasts <5%) after induction; trackable clonoSEQ clone or banked diagnostic sample available; not already known MRD-negative by clonoSEQ and not known to lack a trackable clone.
Cohort A: Age ≥1 (no upper limit); Zubrod/ECOG 0-2 or Lansky/Karnofsky 50-100. Adults may have had 1-3 cycles of induction/consolidation; children must enroll after induction.

Cohort A: No prior blinatumomab, menin inhibitor, CAR-T, or anti-CD19 antibody; no prior allogeneic HSCT; no systemic immunosuppressants other than leukemia chemotherapy (prednisone ≤10 mg/day allowed).
Cohort A: No relapsed or refractory marrow disease (≥5% blasts) or extramedullary involvement; no active CNS2 or CNS3 (prior CNS disease allowed if now CNS1).

Cohort A labs within 14 days: GFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73 m² (adults CrCl ≥50 mL/min), ANC ≥1 x 10^3/uL, platelets ≥100 x 10^3/uL, direct bilirubin ≤2.0 mg/dL (≤5x ULN with Gilbert's), ALT ≤5x ULN. LVEF ≥50% or shortening fraction ≥27% within 90 days.
Cohort B: Age ≥55, Zubrod/ECOG 0-2, newly diagnosed Ph-negative B- or T-ALL or ALAL with locally documented KMT2A translocation; no CML blast crisis or prior CML TKI.

Cohort B: No prior systemic therapy except hydroxyurea, steroids, retinoic acid, IT chemotherapy, or study-backbone induction already started if revumenib can begin by induction day 8; no prior allogeneic HSCT.

Cohort B labs within 14 days: CrCl ≥50 mL/min, direct bilirubin ≤2.0 mg/dL (≤5x ULN if Gilbert's or leukemia-related), ALT ≤5x ULN unless leukemia-related. LVEF ≥50% within 28 days. Lumbar puncture within 14 days; no bulky CNS involvement (CNS3c: facial palsy, brain or eye involvement, hypothalamic syndrome).
All: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and strong or moderate inducers (except corticosteroids) stopped 14 days before registration; recovered from major surgery ≥14 days.
All: QTcF ≤450 msec on screening ECG; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.

All: No uncontrolled infection; no oxygen >2 L/min, mechanical ventilation, or vasopressors (Cohort A); no clinically significant autoimmune disease (Cohort A). Able to take oral medication (NG/G-tube oral solution allowed).

HIV allowed with effective ART and undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment (Cohort A adults and all Cohort B).
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (negative pregnancy test within 7 days before treatment).

schema.label: Primary question
schema.text: Non-inferiority of ultra-hypofractionation versus hypofractionation for 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. The margin is 10% (50% to 40%), corresponding to a hazard ratio below 1.32.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T3N0M0 urothelial carcinoma. Mixed urothelial carcinoma is allowed. Small cell carcinoma is not.
One TURBT before randomization. Maximal resection is attempted. Complete or partial resection are both allowed. A repeat TURBT after the initial TURBT is not required.
The window from TURBT pathology to randomization is 180 days. It extends to 240 days only when the patient has completed at least 3 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

Staging of chest, abdomen, and pelvis with CT or MRI, or FDG PET, before randomization. No T4, node-positive, or metastatic disease. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis requires a biopsy showing no tumor.
No diffuse CIS on cystoscopy and biopsy. No prior pelvic radiation. No urothelial carcinoma outside the bladder within 24 months, except upper-tract Ta, T1, or CIS after complete nephroureterectomy.
Age 18 or older. Zubrod performance status 0-2.

submission.text: TRIAD is the NRG image exchange. It anonymizes and validates DICOM and other objects as they transfer.

submission.label: Arm 1, non-adaptive
submission.text: Submit the DICOM CT, planning MR when used, RT structure, RT dose for all initial plans, and RT plan for all initial plans. The first Arm 1 case from each site needs pre-treatment review before RT starts, unless that case uses adaptive planning, in which case the adaptive tables apply. After the site completes the required pre-treatment reviews, later Arm 1 submissions are due within 7 days of RT start.

submission.label: Plan library
submission.text: Required for Arm 2 and optional for Arm 1. The first Arm 2 plan-library case from each site needs pre-treatment review before RT, and a second pre-treatment review of delivered adapted fraction 1 before fraction 2. After those reviews, later cases are due within 7 days of the RT end date. The initial submission is the planning CT (three sets if differential bladder filling is used), planning MR when used, RT structures, three RT plans, and three RT doses. The delivered-fraction submission adds the selected plan and dose, daily volumetric images with alignment, a post-adaptation pre-delivery image, and a post-delivery image.

submission.label: Online adaptive

After the site completes the required pre-treatment reviews, adaptive data for later Arm 2 cases are due within 14 days of the RT end date.

schema.text: Age >= 70, advanced NSCLC, ECOG 0-2, PD-L1 TPS 1-49%, EGFR/ALK negative. Investigator declares intended Arm B chemotherapy (doublet vs single agent) at registration.

schema.text: Baseline GA completed after Step 1 and before Step 2; Step 2 within 5 calendar days of Step 1. GA results reviewed before final Arm B chemotherapy choice.

schema.text: Stratified by age < 80 vs >= 80. Accrual 304 (152 per arm).

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for cycles 1-4, then 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks, up to 2 years.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks plus investigator-choice chemotherapy for cycles 1-4 (carboplatin AUC 5 with pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 [non-squamous], nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15, or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 day 1 or 80 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15; or single-agent nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or pemetrexed), then pembrolizumab maintenance up to 2 years with optional pemetrexed maintenance.

schema.label: Follow-up

schema.text: Overall survival, chemo-immunotherapy vs pembrolizumab alone.

eligibility: Step 1: Age >= 70 years; ECOG performance status 0-2.
Step 1: Histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS 1-49%.
Step 1: Stage IIIB, IIIC, or IV and not a candidate for combined chemoradiation; recurrence after prior chemo-RT for stage III allowed.
Step 1: Negative for EGFR mutation, ALK translocation, or other actionable alterations treated with first-line oral TKIs.

Step 1: No prior cytotoxic chemotherapy for metastatic disease (completed adjuvant or locally advanced chemotherapy allowed); no prior immunotherapy for metastatic disease (adjuvant or locally advanced immunotherapy allowed if completed > 6 months before registration).
Step 1: No symptomatic CNS metastases; treated CNS metastases or cord compression allowed if stable for 14 days and off steroids for 24 hours; asymptomatic CNS metastases allowed.

Step 1: No uncontrolled autoimmune disease (alopecia, vitiligo, RA, psoriasis/psoriatic arthritis, Hashimoto's, lupus, and IBD allowed); no immunosuppressants or steroids > prednisone 10 mg daily equivalent (short courses stopped before randomization and inhaled/topical steroids allowed).
Step 1: Labs within 14 days: ANC >= 1,500/uL, platelets >= 75,000/uL, Hgb >= 8.0 g/dL, total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3.0 x ULN, CrCl >= 45 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, actual body weight).
Step 1: Baseline imaging of all disease sites within 45 days before registration.

Step 1: Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it does not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

schema.label: Enrollment
schema.text: Any child, adolescent, or young adult with a known or suspected eligible neoplasm, independent of therapeutic trial participation. Participants consent to one or more optional components. Some COG therapeutic trials require APEC14B1 enrollment first.

schema.label: Project:EveryChild components (COG sites)
schema.text: Six components: eligibility screening (clinical, pathology, imaging, surgical, and biologic data, with optional central review, for COG trial eligibility or risk stratification); biobanking of tumor, normal host, and parental germline specimens at diagnosis, progression, relapse, or post-mortem; tracking outcome; childhood cancer registry (formerly ACCRN07); contact for future research; and the Molecular Characterization Initiative.

schema.label: Project:AYA components (non-COG NCTN sites)
schema.text: Added in 2025 for adults potentially eligible for COG-led NCTN trials. Limited to eligibility screening, biobanking, future contact, and molecular characterization.

schema.label: Molecular Characterization Initiative
schema.text: NCI CCDI-sponsored testing for selected and rare cancer types at the Institute for Genomic Medicine: enhanced whole exome sequencing (tumor and germline), RNA fusion testing, and DNA methylation array. Results returned to the treating physician in about 3 weeks for clinical management and trial eligibility.

schema.label: Specimens
schema.text: Tumor only from clinically indicated procedures, never research-only procedures; research blood limited to 3 mL/kg or less (saliva or buccal swab in rare cases).

eligibility: Enrollment within 6 months of initial presentation, or within 6 months of refractory disease, progression, recurrence, second or secondary malignancy, or post-mortem.
Prior ACCRN07 patients may enroll in the tracking outcome, registry, and future contact components any time after reaching the age of majority.
Known or suspected neoplasm of the pediatric, adolescent, or young adult population: any ICD-O behavior code 1 (borderline), 2 (in situ), or 3 (malignant).
Any CNS or kidney neoplasm regardless of behavior.

Selected benign or borderline conditions: mesoblastic nephroma, teratomas (mature and immature), myeloproliferative disease including transient myeloproliferative disease, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, lymphoproliferative disease, desmoid tumors, gonadal stromal tumors, neuroendocrine tumors including pheochromocytoma, melanocytic tumors other than clearly benign nevi, and ganglioneuromas.
Age 25 years or younger at original diagnosis, except patients being screened for a specific COG (or COG-participating NCTN) therapeutic trial with a higher age limit.
Must agree to at least one study component; parents consent separately for their own specimens.

eligibility: Histologic soft tissue sarcoma on core or incisional biopsy, primary or locally recurrent, stage II-IIIB by AJCC 8th edition. No prior partial excision or partial excisional biopsy, even with gross residual disease. No prior procedure that removed the tumor completely with no gross residual disease.

Primary site in the extremity, including the shoulder girdle and hip girdle, excluding the hands and feet. Trunk, head, neck, intra-abdominal, intrapelvic, and retroperitoneal primaries are excluded. Extension from an eligible primary into an adjacent region such as the torso, hands, or feet is allowed.
MRI of the primary site within 90 days before randomization. The field of view contains the whole tumor and includes axial T1 with fat suppression and a T1 sequence with gadolinium.

Pulmonary nodules 5 mm or smaller without histology are not exclusionary. Nodules of 6-10 mm are allowed if stable for at least 6 months or if FDG-PET makes metastasis unlikely. Nodules larger than 10 mm are treated as metastatic unless biopsy, resection, or 6 months of stability shows otherwise.
No fungating tumor. No myxoid liposarcoma, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, osteosarcoma, or NTRK-rearranged spindle cell sarcoma.

A surgeon has judged, within 35 days before randomization, that limb-salvage resection with an expectation of negative margins is appropriate. Anticipated positive margins on fixed critical structures are allowed. No prior treatment of this tumor with systemic therapy, radiation, or complete resection, and no prior radiation to the anatomic site.
Age 18 or older, Zubrod 0-2, and a history and physical within 28 days before randomization that describes the tumor site, laterality, and extremity.
People of reproductive potential use effective contraception. No uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would limit compliance or safety.
Sites in the United States offer optional specimen banking. Informed consent is required. A legally authorized representative may consent when decision-making is impaired.

schema.label: Registration/randomization
schema.text: High grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma (biopsy, or high grade cytology with a mass on cross-sectional imaging or seen at ureteroscopy). Assignment by cisplatin eligibility: cisplatin-eligible (CrCl > 50, ECOG 0-1, hearing loss grade 0-2, neuropathy grade 0-1) are randomized to Arm A or B; cisplatin-ineligible are registered to Arm C.

schema.text: Sessile architecture (present vs absent vs unknown/both); tumor location (ureter vs renal pelvis vs multifocal); regional lymph node short axis (< 1.0 cm vs >= 1.0 cm and < 1.5 cm).

schema.text: Neoadjuvant therapy for 4 cycles if tolerated.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: aMVAC (methotrexate 30 mg/m2, vinblastine 3 mg/m2, doxorubicin 30 mg/m2, cisplatin 70 mg/m2 or 35 mg/m2 days 1 and 2, all day 1 every 14 days, with G-CSF per investigator) x 4 cycles plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 28 days (cycles 1 and 3).

arms.text: aMVAC alone, every 14 days x 4 cycles.

schema.text: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1, every 21 days x 4 cycles. Cisplatin-ineligible means any of: CrCl > 15 and <= 50 ml/min, hearing loss >= grade 3, neuropathy >= grade 2, or ECOG PS 2.

schema.label: Surgery (all arms)
schema.text: Radical nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff and template regional lymph node dissection 21-60 days after the last dose of neoadjuvant therapy, if no metastatic or unresectable disease.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Every 3-6 months for 5 years from study entry or from surgery.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cisplatin-eligible cohort: event-free survival (aMVAC with vs without durvalumab). Cisplatin-ineligible cohort: pathologic complete response (ypT0N0/Nx) at nephroureterectomy.

eligibility: High grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma diagnosed within 14 weeks (98 days) before registration by either biopsy plus a mass on cross-sectional imaging or tumor seen at ureteroscopy, or high grade cytology plus a clinically invasive mass on imaging (for example tumor-related hydronephrosis) or tumor seen at ureteroscopy.
No small cell/neuroendocrine component; other variant histology allowed if conventional urothelial carcinoma is >= 50%.

No metastatic disease and no clinically enlarged regional lymph nodes (>= 1.5 cm short axis) on imaging within 28 days before registration (non-regional findings >= 1.5 cm judged not concerning by the investigator are allowed).
Labs within 14 days: leukocytes >= 3,000/mcL, platelets >= 100,000/mcL, Hgb >= 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed), total bilirubin <= 1.2 mg/dL (<= 2 mg/dL for Gilbert's), AST and ALT <= 2 x ULN.
CrCl (Cockcroft-Gault) or GFR > 15 ml/min within 28 days; body weight > 30 kg; life expectancy >= 12 weeks.

Cisplatin-eligible cohort (Arms A/B) requires all of: CrCl or GFR > 50, ECOG 0-1, hearing loss grade 0-2, neuropathy grade 0-1, ANC >= 1,500/mcL within 14 days, and LVEF >= 50% by MUGA or echo within 28 days.
Cisplatin-ineligible cohort (Arm C) requires any of: CrCl or GFR > 15 and <= 50, hearing loss >= grade 3, neuropathy >= grade 2, or ECOG PS 2, plus ANC >= 1,000/mcL within 14 days.

No other active malignancy within 2 years, except resected non-melanoma skin cancer, resected in situ carcinoma, and low-risk prostate cancer on surveillance or previously treated prostate cancer with no rising PSA.

Prior urothelial cancer allowed only if T0, Ta, or Tis at any time, or T1-4a N0 with no evidence of disease for more than 2 years after last therapy; no prior pT4b, N+, or M1 urothelial cancer; no prior systemic immune checkpoint inhibitor.
No prior systemic anthracycline (prior intravesical therapy for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer allowed). No prior radiation to >= 25% of bone marrow.

No autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppression within 2 years, and no history of inflammatory bowel disease, neuromuscular autoimmune disease, immune-related pneumonitis, or interstitial lung disease (controlled thyroid disease, diet-controlled celiac, type I diabetes, vitiligo, alopecia, psoriasis, eczema allowed).

No immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first durvalumab dose (topical, inhaled, intranasal, local injection steroids, prednisone <= 10 mg/day equivalent, and steroid premedication allowed).

No uncontrolled illness, including active infection or tuberculosis, symptomatic CHF, MI or unstable angina, significant uncontrolled arrhythmia, clinically relevant cirrhosis, or interstitial lung disease in the prior 3 months. Patients with cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic agents must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load and CD4 > 250 cells/mcL; chronic HBV allowed if viral load undetectable on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated with undetectable viral load.

No live attenuated vaccine within 30 days before the first durvalumab dose. No major surgery within 28 days (cystoscopy, ureteroscopy, TURBT, stent, or nephrostomy not counted). No prior allogeneic organ transplant.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

studies.title: A Phase II Trial of Durvalumab with Gemcitabine and Cisplatin as Neoadjuvant Therapy for High-Risk Resectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
Phase II Randomized Trial of Radiotherapy with or Without Cisplatin for Surgically Resected Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN) with TP53 Sequencing

schema.label: Step 0
schema.text: Pre-register as soon as possible after surgery and submit resected tumor to Foundation Medicine for FoundationOne CDx and p53 mutation status. The schema accrual goal for Step 0 is 320-345. Step 1 registration must occur within 8 weeks of resection. Full assay turnaround is at least 14 days.

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Randomize only after the site is notified that central p53 testing is complete. Stratify by disruptive p53 mutation, non-disruptive p53 mutation, or p53 wild type. No randomization ratio is printed.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Postoperative RT, 60 Gy IMRT, standard fractionation at 2 Gy per day.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: The same 60 Gy IMRT at 2 Gy per day, plus cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV weekly for 6 doses during radiation.

eligibility: Step 0: Age 18 or older with pathologically proven squamous cell carcinoma, including verrucous carcinoma, spindle cell carcinoma, or carcinoma NOS, of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Pathologic stage III or IVA by AJCC 8: T3-T4a N0-3 M0, or T1-T2 N1-3 M0. The primary tumor must have been totally resected with curative intent.

An oropharynx primary must be HPV negative by p16 immunohistochemistry. Positive margins that are not superseded by an additional tumor-negative tissue margin, nodal extracapsular extension, or gross residual disease make the patient ineligible. Paraffin-embedded surgical tumor must be available to ship to Foundation Medicine.

A prior curatively treated malignancy must be disease free for at least 2 years, except carcinoma in situ of the cervix and non-melanoma skin cancer. No chemotherapy or investigational therapy within 2 years of resection of the primary. No prior head and neck irradiation that would overlap current fields. Recurrent disease or multiple primaries are ineligible.

Step 1: All Step 0 criteria must still be met, and randomization waits for notice that central p53 assay of the surgical tumor is complete. Gross total resection must have been completed within 8 weeks before randomization.

Within 8 weeks before randomization: examination by a head and neck surgeon, or by the treating medical or radiation oncologist, and chest x-ray, chest CT, chest CT/PET, or chest MRI to rule out distant metastasis. ECOG performance status 0-1 within 2 weeks before randomization.
Women must not be pregnant or breast-feeding. A woman of childbearing potential needs a blood or urine pregnancy test within 2 weeks before randomization.

Within 4 weeks before randomization: ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin at or under the ULN, and Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance over 60 mL/min, with the result multiplied by 0.85 for women. No intercurrent illness likely to interfere with protocol therapy.

studies.title: A Phase III Trial of Stereotactic Radiosurgery Compared with Hippocampal-Avoidant Whole Brain Radiotherapy (HA-WBRT) plus Memantine for 5-15 Brain Metastases

schema.label: Population
schema.text: International multicenter open-label randomized phase III trial of stereotactic radiosurgery vs hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy plus memantine, for patients with 5 or more brain metastases. Planned sample size is 206.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: DS-GPA predicted median overall survival (less than 6 months vs at least 6 months). Use of targeted therapy or immunotherapy within 4 weeks of the original brain-metastasis diagnosis, or planned within 4 weeks of radiation (yes or no). Histology: radio-resistant vs other. Radio-resistant means sarcoma, melanoma, or renal cell carcinoma. Metastasis within 5 mm of one hippocampus (yes or no).

schema.label: Step 1 registration
schema.text: Consenting patients believed to be eligible are registered in OPEN with an abbreviated eligibility checklist. After registration, neurocognitive assessments, quality-of-life questionnaires, and health economics assessments may be administered.

schema.label: Step 2 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Randomize after baseline assessments and before treatment. Stratification factors are collected at registration. Protocol treatment begins within 14 days of enrolment.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy, 30 Gy in 10 fractions, plus memantine. Memantine starts the same day as whole brain radiotherapy and must start no later than before the fourth fraction. The target dose is 20 mg (10 mg twice daily), escalated by 5 mg per week.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Stereotactic radiosurgery in a single fraction: 22 Gy for lesions under 4 cc, and 18 to 20 Gy for lesions of 4 to 10 cc. The schema footnote says further details are in the treatment section.

schema.label: Observation
schema.text: Both arms then enter observation and event monitoring. If brain metastases or systemic disease progress, the patient remains under observation.

eligibility: Five or more brain metastases, counted on a contrast-enhanced T1 MRI obtained within 30 days of randomization. Pathologic diagnosis, cytology or histology, of a non-hematopoietic malignancy.

The largest brain metastasis must be smaller than 2.5 cm in maximal diameter. Total tumor volume must be 30 cm3 or less, estimated as the product of three perpendicular diameters divided by 2, or by direct slice-by-slice contouring.

The centre must be able to treat with Gamma Knife, Cyberknife, or a linear accelerator radiosurgery system, or must have access to an open centre that can. The enrolling facility must be IROC-credentialed for stereotactic radiosurgery and hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy, or have access to a credentialed centre where the study is open. The treating centre must have completed credentialing for the specific radiosurgery system and for the IMRT system used for hippocampal avoidance.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0, 1, or 2.

Able and willing to complete quality-of-life questionnaires in English or French, alone or with assistance, before randomization. Also able and willing to complete neurocognitive testing without help from family or companions, and fluent and fully testable in English or French. A patient who is able but unwilling to complete the questionnaires is ineligible.
Creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min within 28 days before registration. Section 4 does not list other numeric hematology or chemistry floors.

The neurocognitive testing examiner must have credentialing that confirms completion of the neurocognitive testing training. Patients must be accessible for treatment and follow-up. Protocol treatment starts within 14 days of enrolment.

Women and men of childbearing potential must agree to highly effective contraception. A pregnancy test is part of the pre-study evaluation. An ultrasound may be used if a false-positive pregnancy test is suspected, and a negative ultrasound makes the patient eligible.
Pregnant or nursing women are excluded. Men or women of childbearing potential who will not use adequate contraception are excluded.

Inability to complete a brain MRI, and known allergy to gadolinium, are exclusions. Prior cranial radiation is excluded. Planned cytotoxic chemotherapy within 48 hours before or after stereotactic radiosurgery or hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy is excluded.

Primary germ cell tumor, small cell carcinoma, and lymphoma are excluded. Widespread definitive leptomeningeal metastasis is excluded, including cranial nerve palsy, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, ependymal involvement, cranial nerve involvement on imaging, suspicious linear meningeal enhancement, or cerebrospinal fluid positive for tumor cells.
A brain metastasis within 5 mm of the optic chiasm or either optic nerve is excluded. Prior surgical resection of a brain metastasis is excluded. Stereotactic biopsies are allowed.

Prior allergic reaction to memantine, or hypersensitivity to any memantine excipient, is excluded. Current alcohol or drug abuse is excluded. Current use of NMDA antagonists such as amantadine, ketamine, or dextromethorphan is excluded.

Chronic liver disease or cirrhosis, for example Child-Pugh class B or C, is excluded. Clinically significant untreated or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions, and symptomatic cardiac dysfunction, are excluded, including unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous year, ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication, second or third degree atrioventricular block, and uncontrolled hypertension.
Current active or uncontrolled urinary tract infection is excluded. A history of epilepsy or seizures in a patient not currently taking anti-epileptic medication is excluded.

Any other serious illness that the local investigator judges would compromise safety, preclude the planned treatment, or prevent protocol management is excluded. Architectural distortion of the lateral ventricles that, in the local investigator's opinion, makes hippocampal delineation challenging is excluded.

studies.title: Phase III Trial of Neoadjuvant Durvalumab (NSC 778709) Plus Chemotherapy Versus Chemotherapy Alone for Adults with MammaPrint High 2 Risk (MP2) Hormone Receptor (HR) Positive /  Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (HER2) Negative Stage II-III Breast Cancer

amendments.text: Revision 3, the current version. Request for Amendment: updated durvalumab CAEPR to version 2.6 (adds diabetic ketoacidosis), removed commercial drug information per CTEP policy, clarified slide type and storage.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: HR-positive, HER2-negative clinical stage II-III breast cancer, untreated

schema.label: Step 1: Registration (screening)
schema.text: Tumor tissue sent for MammaPrint, or a known MammaPrint result within 12 weeks. MP1/low risk (index above -0.57) is ineligible

schema.label: Step 2: Randomization
schema.text: MammaPrint High 2 (index -1.0 to -0.57 inclusive); randomize within 84 days of the MP2 result (same day as Step 1 if already known)

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Age < 50 vs >= 50; node positive (clinical or pathologic) vs negative; intended adjuvant targeted therapy yes vs no

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Start within 7 days; 14-day cycles, 10 cycles total

arms.label: Arm 1: Chemotherapy
arms.text: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 weekly x 12 (Cycles 1-6), then dose-dense doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 every 14 days x 4 (Cycles 7-10) with G-CSF

arms.label: Arm 2: Chemotherapy + durvalumab
arms.text: Same chemotherapy plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 28 days (Cycles 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; 5 doses)

schema.label: Surgery
schema.text: Standard-of-care breast and axillary surgery, then standard-of-care radiation and adjuvant endocrine with or without targeted therapy as indicated

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 10 years from randomization

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Breast cancer event-free survival

eligibility: Age >= 18; body weight > 30 kg; Zubrod performance status 0-2.
Histologically confirmed ER- and/or PR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer per ASCO/CAP (HER2-low or equivocal allowed if no HER2-directed therapy).
Clinical stage II or III, including inflammatory breast cancer; no occult primary with axillary nodes only.
No metastatic disease (cM0 or Mx); no locally recurrent breast cancer.
Multifocal or synchronous bilateral tumors allowed if all biopsied tumors are HR+/HER2- and at least one is MammaPrint High 2.
At least 10 unstained FFPE slides from the diagnostic biopsy for MammaPrint, or a known MP2 result from the last 12 weeks (any known non-MP2 result is ineligible).
Step 2: MammaPrint High 2 (index -1.0 to -0.57 inclusive).
No prior treatment for this breast cancer (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal) and a candidate for doxorubicin, paclitaxel, and durvalumab.
No non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids or active pneumonitis within 2 years; no autoimmune disease requiring systemic therapy within 2 years (replacement therapy allowed).
No live vaccine within 28 days before randomization.
Within 28 days of Step 2: WBC >= 3,000/uL, ANC >= 1,500/uL, platelets >= 100,000/uL, total bilirubin <= ULN (<= 5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN, CrCl >= 50 mL/min.
NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history, symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy.
No uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >= 9.0% within 28 days).
HIV on effective ART with undetectable viral load, chronic HBV with undetectable load on suppression, and HCV treated and cured or undetectable, each within 6 months.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed only if it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant or nursing.

studies.title: A Phase 2 Study of Nivolumab and Ipilimumab in Combination with Sirolimus and Prednisone in Kidney Transplant Recipients with Selected Unresectable or Metastatic Cutaneous Cancers
Phase III Trial of Immunotherapy-Based Combination Therapy with or Without Cytoreductive Nephrectomy for Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma (PROBE Trial)

amendments.text: Revision #10, the current version. Decentralized trial activities and international site guidance added; standard-of-care therapy may be given by local providers, nephrectomy must be at the NCTN site; eligibility clarified (brain imaging only if clinically indicated, no progression in metastatic sites or primary at Step 2); calendar footnotes updated.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Newly diagnosed metastatic RCC with primary tumor in place. Enter either immunotherapy-naive (start pre-randomization treatment within 7 days) or after completing the protocol-specified pre-randomization regimen off protocol (Step 1 and Step 2 the same day).

schema.label: Pre-randomization immunotherapy (choose one, about 12 weeks)
schema.text: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q3 weeks (up to 4 doses), then nivolumab 240 mg q2 weeks or 480 mg q4 weeks; nivolumab (240 mg q2 weeks or 480 mg q4 weeks) plus cabozantinib 40 mg daily; pembrolizumab (200 mg q3 weeks or 400 mg q6 weeks) plus axitinib 5 mg BID; pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib 20 mg daily; or avelumab (800 mg or 10 mg/kg q2 weeks) plus axitinib 5 mg BID.

schema.label: Week 12 assessment
schema.text: Disease assessment at 12 weeks (plus or minus 2 weeks). Participants without progression (stable disease, partial response, or investigator-judged clinical benefit; suspected pseudoprogression allowed) proceed to randomization; those not randomized are not followed.

schema.label: Stratification at Step 2
schema.text: Zubrod 0 vs 1; immunotherapy combination vs TKI plus immunotherapy; week 12 response PR vs less than PR.

schema.label: Step 2: Randomization 1:1
schema.text: Between week 11 day 1 and week 14 day 7 of pre-randomization treatment.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Continued systemic immunotherapy-based regimen (same combination as pre-randomization) until progression.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Cytoreductive nephrectomy (radical or partial; laparoscopic, open, or robotic) planned within 42 days of randomization (no later than 56 days) at an NCTN site, plus continued systemic immunotherapy; systemic therapy may be held up to 42 days perioperatively, axitinib stopped at least 24 hours before surgery.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Randomized participants followed until death or 7 years after randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival.

eligibility: Step 1: Histologically proven clear cell or non-clear cell RCC (collecting duct carcinoma excluded; multifocal or bilateral tumors allowed), with primary tumor in place.

Step 1: Measurable or non-measurable metastatic disease on CT chest and CT (with contrast) or MRI abdomen/pelvis within 90 days before registration (immunotherapy-naive) or within 90 days before the first immunotherapy dose (pre-randomization completed).
Step 1: Brain metastases allowed if any post-treatment imaging shows no progression after CNS-directed therapy; brain imaging not required unless clinically indicated.

Step 1: No prior systemic immunotherapy for metastatic RCC beyond the single protocol-specified pre-randomization regimen (if given off protocol), and no immunotherapy for any cancer within 6 months before registration or before starting the pre-randomization regimen. Pre-randomization completed participants must not exceed regimen-specific maximum dose counts (for example 4 ipilimumab infusions, 5 pembrolizumab 200 mg infusions).
Step 1: Palliative radiotherapy for symptomatic metastases is allowed before or after registration.
Step 1: Age 18 or older; no clear contraindication to nephrectomy or immune-based combination therapy; no solitary or transplanted kidney.

No other prior malignancy except adequately treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, in situ (Step 1 also T1) cancer, adequately treated stage I or II cancer in complete remission, or other cancer disease-free for at least 2 years.

Step 2: Restaging CT chest and CT or MRI abdomen/pelvis 12 weeks (plus or minus 2 weeks) after starting pre-randomization therapy and within 28 days before randomization, showing stable disease, partial response, or investigator-judged clinical benefit with Zubrod 0-1. Complete response in all metastatic sites is not eligible.
Step 2: No progression in metastatic sites or primary tumor (pseudoprogression allowed); plans to continue the same immune-based regimen.

Step 2: Randomized between week 11 day 1 and week 14 day 7 of pre-randomization treatment, after at least the minimum immunotherapy (for example 2 nivolumab plus 1 ipilimumab infusion, 2 pembrolizumab 200 mg or 1 pembrolizumab 400 mg, or 2 avelumab infusions).
Step 2: Urology consultation within 42 days confirming surgical candidacy, with planned surgery date within 42 days of randomization.
Step 2: Zubrod performance status 0-1 and history and physical within 28 days before randomization.
Step 2: Within 28 days: total bilirubin up to 2 x ULN; AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); serum creatinine up to 1.5 x ULN or creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min.

studies.title: Molecular Analysis for Combination Therapy Choice (ComboMATCH)

schema.label: Molecular testing
schema.text: Tumor tissue or ctDNA sequencing at an NCI-designated CLIA laboratory (the treatment-determining assay).

schema.label: Registration (EAY191, non-treatment)
schema.text: Enroll on the ComboMATCH registration trial in OPEN with clinical data, optional physician choice, and the CLIA sequencing and pathology reports. No research biopsy or biospecimens under this protocol.

schema.label: Assignment
schema.text: MATCHBox rules engine assigns one ComboMATCH treatment trial. Tie-breakers include required dual targets, histology priority, gene/variant priority, level of evidence, variant allele frequency, and accrual balance; physician choice is the default when eligible. Ineligibility triggers reassignment until options are exhausted.

schema.label: Treatment trial enrollment
schema.text: Register to the assigned treatment trial within 5 weeks of assignment after meeting its eligibility and consent (otherwise re-register). Treatment, research biopsy, and specimens are governed by the treatment trial. After progression, crossover or a second treatment trial assignment is possible; a third requires new registration.

schema.label: Primary objective
schema.text: To register, allocate, and assign patients to ComboMATCH treatment trials.

eligibility: Measurable disease.
ECOG 0-2, or Lansky or Karnofsky >= 50%.

Locally advanced or advanced histologically documented solid tumor requiring therapy, with progression on at least one line of standard systemic therapy or no standard treatment shown to prolong overall survival.
Sequencing results from ctDNA or tumor tissue from an NCI-credentialed designated laboratory (submit both reports if both exist).
Judged potentially eligible for a ComboMATCH treatment trial by the enrolling provider.
Age >= 18 with a minimal-risk biopsy site: willing to undergo a research biopsy if assigned (waived for ctDNA enrollment without collectable tissue, with archival tissue within 1 year requested).
Age >= 18 without a minimal-risk biopsy site: archival FFPE tumor tissue collected within 12 months before registration must be available.
Age < 18: willing to submit archival FFPE tumor tissue, if available.

followup.window: Until off follow-up on the assigned treatment trial, or 6 months after registration if never enrolled on a treatment trial
followup.note: Assessments and AE reporting are under the treatment trial.

studies.title: Phase 2 Randomized Trial of Neoadjuvant or Palliative Chemotherapy with or Without Immunotherapy for Peritoneal Mesothelioma

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Untreated peritoneal mesothelioma with measurable disease. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Surgical candidate at study entry (yes vs no); histologic subtype (epithelioid vs non-epithelioid). Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles, 4 cycles of induction

arms.label: Regimen 1
arms.text: Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 IV + carboplatin AUC 5 IV, day 1 every 3 weeks x 4 cycles.

arms.label: Regimen 2
arms.text: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 IV + carboplatin AUC 5 IV, day 1 every 3 weeks x 4 cycles.

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: Imaging before cycle 3 and 21-28 days after cycle 4 (surgical candidates) or before cycle 5 (non-surgical).

schema.label: Surgical candidates
schema.text: Cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC 4-8 weeks after chemotherapy, then observation with imaging every 84 days for 2 years. If surgery is insufficient, aborted, or lacks cytoreductive intent, maintenance therapy may be given.

schema.label: Non-surgical candidates
schema.text: Maintenance bevacizumab 15 mg/kg ± atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks regardless of randomization (atezolizumab added at investigator discretion in Regimen 2), until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 3 years from registration.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 2 years post treatment or 3 years from registration, whichever comes first, or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Best response rate by RECIST, Regimen 1 vs Regimen 2.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically confirmed malignant peritoneal mesothelioma, previously untreated; well-differentiated papillary and multicystic mesothelioma are excluded.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS 0-1.

Leukocytes ≥ 2,500/mm3, ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, CrCl ≥ 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 if creatinine above normal, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT ≤ 3.0 x ULN, UPC ratio < 1 or urine protein ≤ 1+.
No prior systemic therapy for peritoneal mesothelioma; no concurrent radiotherapy.

No active or prior autoimmune disease or immune deficiency (exceptions: autoimmune hypothyroidism on replacement, controlled type 1 diabetes on insulin, limited skin-only eczema/psoriasis/vitiligo < 10% BSA on low-potency topical steroids).
No history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced or idiopathic pneumonitis, and no active pneumonitis on screening chest CT.
No prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant.
CNS metastases allowed only if treated with local therapy (surgery, radiation, ablation) and steroids tapered to ≤ 10 mg prednisone equivalent.
No inadequately controlled hypertension (> 150/100 mmHg), hypertensive crisis, or hypertensive encephalopathy.
No stroke or MI within 12 months, unstable angina, NYHA class II or greater CHF, or uncontrolled arrhythmia; no significant vascular disease within 6 months; no grade 4 venous thromboembolism.

No abdominal fistula, GI perforation, intra-abdominal abscess, or active GI bleeding within 6 months; no non-healing wound, active ulcer, or untreated fracture.

No major surgery or significant trauma within 28 days of treatment (diagnostic laparoscopy allowed); no core biopsy or minor procedure within 7 days; vascular access device at least 2 days before treatment.
No active infection requiring IV antibiotics at start of treatment.

No immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks before treatment (exceptions: brief or one-time steroid pulse, mineralocorticoids, steroids for COPD/asthma, low-dose steroids for orthostatic hypotension or adrenal insufficiency).

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No other malignancy within 5 years except localized in situ cancer such as basal or squamous cell skin cancer.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 28 days before registration).

studies.title: NET RETREAT: A Phase II Study of 177 Lutetium-DOTATATE Retreatment vs. Everolimus or Sunitinib or Cabozantinib in Metastatic/ Unresectable Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumours

schema.label: Population
schema.text: International multicenter open-label randomized phase II trial of limited-dose 177Lu-DOTATATE compared with everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only) in metastatic or unresectable well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with a prior durable response to 177Lu-DOTATATE. Planned sample size is 100 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Longer responders (at least 24 months) vs standard responders (less than 24 months) to initial PRRT. A responder is stable disease, partial response, or complete response per RECIST 1.1. Pancreatic vs extrapancreatic site of origin. Intervening therapy vs no intervening therapy.

schema.label: Randomize 2:1
schema.text: Treatment on either arm continues until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: 177Lu-DOTATATE 7400 MBq (200 mCi) every 8 weeks for 2 cycles.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Everolimus 10 mg daily, or sunitinib 37.5 mg daily, or cabozantinib 60 mg daily. Pancreatic NET may receive everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only). Midgut NET may receive only everolimus or cabozantinib (US patients only).

schema.label: Crossover
schema.text: At objective progression per RECIST 1.1, Arm 2 may cross over to Arm 1. The schema prints the Arm 1 regimen a second time at that step, again 7400 MBq (200 mCi) every 8 weeks for 2 cycles. Crossover is also available to patients who stop everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib for toxicity and later have objective progression, if they stayed in protocol follow-up after stopping the Arm 2 agent chosen at the start of protocol therapy.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Disease status every 12 weeks until objective progression, then telephone, virtual, or clinic survival follow-up every 6 months until death.

eligibility: The study population is metastatic or unresectable well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that progressed no sooner than 12 months after prior peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

Age at least 18. Metastatic, histologically confirmed grade 1 or 2 well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, including an unknown primary thought to be gastroenteropancreatic, using the 7th edition TNM classification.

A positive gallium-68 DOTATATE, copper-64 DOTATATE, or octreotide scan within 12 months is recommended and within 36 months is allowed. A target lesion is positive if its SUVmax is greater than the SUV mean of normal liver.

Prior PRRT must have been 3 or 4 cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE, or a cumulative exposure of 22,200 MBq (600 mCi) or 29,600 MBq (800 mCi), within plus or minus 10 percent, given within a 52-week period. No previous targeted alpha therapy.

Radiologic progression per RECIST 1.1 after prior PRRT, and no sooner than 12 months from the last scan after initial PRRT, during which stable disease, partial response, or complete response was maintained.

Intervening systemic anticancer therapy is allowed if the patient benefited from initial PRRT for at least 12 months and then progressed per RECIST 1.1 on that intervening therapy. A somatostatin analogue given for functional control is not intervening systemic therapy.

If intervening therapy included a VEGF inhibitor, sunitinib cannot be the Arm 2 standard of care. If it included an mTOR inhibitor, everolimus cannot be the Arm 2 standard of care. If the intervening therapy is an alkylating agent, alkylator exposure cannot exceed 12 months. That 12-month limit also applies to alkylator use before PRRT.

Prior ablative liver therapy or bland embolization is allowed if not within 12 weeks of randomization. Prior chemoembolization and radioembolization are not permitted. A lesion treated with ablation, and lesions in a liver lobe treated with embolization, are not target lesions unless they have since progressed.
No ongoing toxicity from prior PRRT that is grade 3 or higher by CTCAE 5.0. ECOG performance status 2 or better.

Organ and marrow function within 28 days before enrollment: hemoglobin at least 80 g/L (8.0 g/dL), absolute neutrophil count at least 1.0 x 10^9/L (1,000/mm3), platelets at least 80 x 10^9/L (80,000/mm3), total bilirubin less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (Gilbert syndrome may be eligible at or below 3.0 times that limit), and creatinine clearance greater than 50 mL/min by 24-hour urine or Cockcroft-Gault.

Prior or current somatostatin analogues are allowed for carcinoid syndrome control and in the Arm 1 retreatment population. Patients randomized to Arm 2 who receive everolimus, sunitinib (pancreatic NET only), or cabozantinib (US patients only) may not continue somatostatin analogues unless they have a functional syndrome.

The patient must have access to everolimus, or to sunitinib for pancreatic NET, or to cabozantinib for US patients. If the site cannot provide that access, the patient is not eligible. Patients must be treated and followed at the participating centre.

People of reproductive potential must use highly effective contraception during protocol treatment and for 7 months after the last dose for females and 4 months after the last dose for males. Men should avoid fathering a child for 4 months after the last 177Lu-DOTATATE dose. A pregnancy test is part of the pre-study evaluation.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. A prior or concurrent malignancy is eligible when its natural history or treatment would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Exclusions: major surgery within 6 weeks of randomization. Known brain metastases, unless treated, stabilized, and off steroids for at least 4 weeks, with a contrast head CT and/or MRI documenting stable disease before enrollment.

The ineligibility list includes uncontrolled congestive heart failure no worse than NYHA class IIB, as defined in Appendix XIII. Inability to swallow oral medications, or gastrointestinal disease that limits absorption of oral agents, is excluded. Any other significant medical or surgical condition that is uncontrolled and may interfere with completing the study is excluded.

Pregnant women are excluded. Breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only), and for 2.5 months after the last 177Lu-DOTATATE treatment.
