amendments.text: Revision #4, the current version. Sample size lowered from 60 to 40 and accrual extended from 33 to 44 months; secondary objectives added for grade 2 or higher edema and weight change; blood pressure eligibility left to investigator judgment; pancreatitis criterion broadened (asymptomatic amylase or lipase elevation allowed); more MET amplification assays accepted; archival tissue collection added.

schema.label: Step 1: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Screened on the LUNGMAP master protocol at radiographic or clinical progression on osimertinib; tissue for biomarker profiling, or tissue or blood (ctDNA) NGS results from an accepted CLIA laboratory, obtained after progression on osimertinib. SWOG SDMC assigns eligible EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified participants to S1900G.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Brain metastases (yes vs no); prior lines of therapy for advanced, recurrent, or metastatic disease (1 vs 2 or more).

schema.label: Step 2: S1900G randomization 1:1

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Capmatinib 400 mg PO twice daily, days 1-28, plus osimertinib 80 mg PO daily, days 1-28, plus ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Capmatinib 400 mg PO twice daily, days 1-28, plus osimertinib 80 mg PO daily, days 1-28.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after sub-study randomization, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Key secondary: Cycle 1 toxicity rate, grade 2 or higher edema, weight change from baseline.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900G by the SWOG SDMC through the LUNGMAP screening protocol.
NSCLC with a sensitizing EGFR mutation, with radiologic or clinical progression on osimertinib (alone or in combination) as the most recent line of therapy; any number of prior lines allowed.
MET amplification by tissue- or blood-based (ctDNA) NGS in a CLIA, ISO/IEC, CAP, or similarly certified laboratory, on tissue or blood obtained after progression on osimertinib.

Measurable disease (assessed within 28 days) or non-measurable disease (within 42 days) by CT or MRI before sub-study randomization. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts as measurable only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT with contrast or MRI within 42 days before sub-study randomization. Symptomatic CNS metastases (brain or leptomeningeal) allowed if neurologically stable with stable or decreasing steroids for at least 5 days.
Able to tolerate osimertinib 80 mg daily for at least 14 days before sub-study randomization (rechallenge at 80 mg may be considered after a prior dose reduction).
No prior MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor (prior anti-MET antibody such as amivantamab allowed).

No anti-cancer drug other than osimertinib within 21 days (osimertinib may continue to the day before study treatment); no radiation therapy within 14 days; no major surgery within 14 days; no live attenuated vaccine within 28 days before sub-study randomization. No planned concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity (except alopecia and vitiligo).
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before sub-study randomization. Able to swallow tablets whole.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin above 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 2.5 x ULN (AST up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).

ECG with QTcF of 470 msec or less within 28 days. Urine protein 1+ or less on dipstick or UA (if 2+ or more, 24-hour urine protein below 1000 mg). INR no more than 1.5 seconds and PTT no more than 5 seconds above the institutional ULN unless anticoagulated.
Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better.

No signs or symptoms of pancreatitis or pancreatic injury (asymptomatic amylase or lipase elevation allowed). No uncontrolled blood pressure or hypertension within 28 days, as judged by the treating investigator.
No moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers (including St. John's Wort) within 7 days before sub-study registration or during treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission.

amendments.text: Amendment #2, the current version. Reopens enrollment for patients younger than 6 months with a new age-based revumenib dosing strategy, clarifies timing of eligibility labs, prohibits strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers throughout therapy, and updates dose modifications and drug monographs.

schema.label: Study entry
schema.text: Age 1 month to < 6 years, KMT2A-rearranged leukemia (diagnosed at < 2 years) that is refractory or in first marrow relapse, CNS1/CNS2, WBC < 50,000/µL. Single-arm phase 2 with a safety lead-in (RP2D) then an expansion phase.

schema.label: Regimen A (ALL, ALAL, or MPAL phenotype; investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycle 1: revumenib + 3-drug re-induction (prednisone/prednisolone BID days 1-28, vincristine days 1, 8, 15, 22, calaspargase pegol day 4, IT methotrexate days 1 and 8). Day 29 marrow, then callback for cycle 2 dose level. Cycle 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT day 0). Early progressive disease during cycle 1 may move straight to cycle 2, then a third FLA cycle.

schema.label: Regimen B (AML phenotype, or ALL/ALAL/MPAL by investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycles 1 and 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT).

schema.label: Revumenib dosing in combination
schema.text: Age ≥ 6 months: DL1 130 mg/m2 Q12H (DL2 160, DL0 95). Age 2 to < 6 months: 100 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 80). Age 1 to < 2 months: 70 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 56). Oral liquid; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors not allowed in combination cycles.

schema.label: Disease evaluation
schema.text: Marrow day 29 (re-induction) or days 29-35 by count recovery (FLA cycles; by day 36 regardless), with central MRD. Patients not meeting treatment failure criteria continue. May leave at any time for HSCT or cellular therapy.

schema.label: Revumenib monotherapy
schema.text: Up to 12 cycles while M1 marrow is maintained without Rel-M1: 160 mg/m2 Q12H for age ≥ 6 months (95 mg/m2 with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor azole); 100 mg/m2 Q12H for age 2 to < 6 months (60 mg/m2 with azole).

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: RP2D of revumenib with chemotherapy in R/R KMT2A-R ALL, and MRD-negative remission rate in patients older than 6 months at enrollment with R/R infant KMT2A-R ALL.

eligibility: Age 1 month to < 6 years at enrollment, with initial leukemia diagnosis at < 2 years.
KMT2A-rearranged ALL, ALAL, or MPAL (lineage switch to AML allowed if prior KMT2A-R ALL/ALAL/MPAL documented), with KMT2A-R confirmed by central cytogenetics/FISH review (submitted by day 10).

Primary refractory (no remission after at least 2 frontline courses; 2 courses plus 1 blinatumomab course allowed, nothing beyond) or untreated first marrow relapse (M3; M2 with 1 confirmatory test; or M1 with 2 confirmatory tests at ≥ 1%).
CNS1 or CNS2 with no neurologic signs of CNS leukemia; CNS3 may receive prior IT therapy to reach CNS1/2. Prior CNS chloroma requires no radiographic CNS disease. No isolated extramedullary leukemia.
WBC < 50,000/µL at enrollment; hydroxyurea and/or corticosteroids allowed for up to 7 days before enrollment.
Lansky ≥ 50% if age ≥ 12 months. Able to take enteral medication (PO, NG, NJ, ND, or G-tube).

Washouts: ≥ 14 days after cytotoxic therapy (≥ 7 days if relapse on maintenance); ≥ 7 days for non-myelosuppressive agents; ≥ 21 days for antibodies (blinatumomab ≥ 3 days); ≥ 84 days after allogeneic HSCT; ≥ 28 days after DLI or cellular therapy; ≥ 14 days after local XRT, ≥ 84 days after TBI, craniospinal RT, or ≥ 50% pelvis, ≥ 42 days after other substantial marrow RT. Prior FLA allowed.
Creatinine at or below age maximum (0.4 mg/dL at 1 to < 6 months, 0.5 at 6-12 months, 0.6 at 1 to < 2 years, 0.8 at 2 to < 6 years) or measured GFR/CrCl ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Direct bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN and ALT ≤ 135 U/L, unless disease related.
Shortening fraction ≥ 27% or EF ≥ 50%, and QTcF < 450 ms (triplicate average).
No Down syndrome, bone marrow failure syndrome (Bloom, ataxia-telangiectasia, Fanconi, Kostmann, Shwachman), or secondary KMT2A-R leukemia after cytotoxic chemotherapy for a prior cancer.
No congenital long QT, CHF, or uncontrolled arrhythmia within 6 months.

No active uncontrolled infection (positive blood culture or infectious fever within 48 hours, positive fungal culture or active invasive fungal treatment within 30 days, viral or protozoal infection needing IV therapy). HIV allowed if on non-interacting antiretrovirals with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No active acute GVHD > grade 0 or chronic GVHD > mild (skin-only exceptions); off systemic anti-GVHD agents > 7 days. No prior solid organ transplant.
No prior revumenib (other menin inhibitors allowed). No Charcot-Marie-Tooth if receiving Regimen A.
No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or moderate/strong inducers (stopped ≥ 5 half-lives before therapy), no other investigational or anticancer agents.

amendments.text: Update 1, the version date on this file. The cover page does not summarize what changed.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: BCG-exposed non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer: recurrent high-grade Ta, T1, or Tis within 24 months of the last BCG exposure, and not BCG-unresponsive.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: CIS on pre-treatment TURBT or biopsies (yes vs no); prior BCG (one induction course only vs more than one induction course, including maintenance or repeat induction); time from last BCG exposure (less than 6 months vs 6-12 months vs more than 12 months).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation. Protocol treatment must not start before randomization and should start within 28 business days after randomization.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: BCG alone: full-strength intravesical BCG once weekly for 6 weeks.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: GemBCG: intravesical gemcitabine 2000 mg twice weekly in weeks 1 and 10 and once weekly in weeks 4 and 7 (6 doses), alternating with full-strength BCG once weekly in weeks 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, and 9 (6 doses).

schema.label: Week 13 (month 3) assessment
schema.text: Mandatory cystoscopic biopsies, with or without TURBT, and urine cytology.

schema.label: Maintenance and follow-up
schema.text: Maintenance at months 3, 6, and 12. Arm A: BCG once weekly for 3 weeks. Arm B: gemcitabine 2000 mg once in the first week, then BCG once weekly for 3 weeks. Cystoscopy and cytology every 3 months through month 24, then every 6 months through month 60. Follow-up for 5 years from randomization or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: High-grade recurrence-free survival.

eligibility: Histologic high-grade Ta, high-grade T1, or Tis (CIS only) urothelial carcinoma within 120 days before randomization. Variant histology is allowed if predominantly urothelial.
No neuroendocrine component (small cell or large cell). No pure squamous cell carcinoma or pure adenocarcinoma.

All visible papillary lesions macroscopically resected by TURBT within 90 days before randomization (residual CIS allowed). If the treating urologist did not perform the TURBT, that urologist must do a cystoscopy within 45 days before randomization confirming no visible papillary disease.
High-grade T1 requires a restaging TURBT within 90 days before randomization. A restaging TURBT with no residual cancer is still eligible based on the prior TURBT.

BCG-exposed NMIBC: any high-grade recurrence within 24 months of induction-only BCG; high-grade papillary Ta/T1 recurrence 6-24 months after induction plus maintenance BCG; or high-grade CIS (with or without Ta/T1) recurrence 12-24 months after induction plus maintenance BCG. BCG-naive patients and those 25 months or more from last BCG are not eligible. TURBT up to 26 months from the last instillation is allowed if recurrence was evident or suspected within 24 months.

No BCG-unresponsive disease: persistent or recurrent high-grade Ta/T1 less than 6 months after adequate BCG, high-grade CIS recurrence less than 12 months after adequate BCG, or high-grade T1 at the first 3-month assessment after induction. Adequate BCG is at least 5 of 6 induction doses plus at least 2 of 3 maintenance doses or at least 2 of 6 repeat-induction doses within 6 months. A patient who previously met BCG-unresponsive criteria but no longer does may enroll if the urologist considers BCG re-treatment reasonable.

Prior intravesical chemotherapy (including gemcitabine, gemcitabine/docetaxel, or TAR-200) and prior systemic or intravesical agents for NMIBC (including pembrolizumab or other checkpoint inhibitors, nadofaragene firadenovec, nogapendekin alfa inbakicept, cretostimogene) are allowed. More than one prior BCG induction course or prior maintenance is allowed.

No history of intolerance to BCG (stopping induction or maintenance for toxicity) or to any other intravesical therapy. No compromised bladder function that makes further intravesical therapy unlikely to be tolerated.

No prior or current muscle-invasive (T2-T4), locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma on CT or MRI of the abdomen and pelvis within 120 days before randomization (contrast preferred, CT or MR urogram preferred; noncontrast allowed if contrast is contraindicated).

Prior upper tract urothelial carcinoma is allowed if localized Ta, T1, or Tis, definitively treated by nephroureterectomy or ureterectomy, with at least one post-treatment imaging study showing no residual upper tract disease.
Non-invasive (Ta/Tis) prostatic urethral urothelial carcinoma is allowed if TURP is done before enrollment and shows no lamina propria or prostatic stromal invasion.

HIV-infected patients on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it does not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Age 18 or older. Not pregnant and not nursing; pregnancy test within 14 days before randomization for persons of childbearing potential.

amendments.text: Initial version; the only entry in the document history of this file.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Premenopausal, resected ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer: pN0 with Oncotype RS 21-25, or RS 16-20 with high clinical risk (low grade and >3 cm, intermediate grade and >2 cm, or high grade and >1 cm); or pN1 with RS 0-25.

schema.label: Step 1: Pre-entry
schema.text: Registration. Patients qualifying by MammaPrint Low Risk/MP1 need central Oncotype DX RS before randomization; MammaPrint High Risk/MP2 are ineligible. Intended RT plan declared before pre-entry.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Nodal/RS status (pN0 RS 16-25 vs pN1 RS 0-15 vs pN1 RS 16-25), intent to receive a CDK4/6 inhibitor (yes vs no), age (18-39 vs 40 or older).

schema.label: Step 2: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified permuted blocks.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Ovarian function suppression (GnRH agonist of investigator's choice, or bilateral oophorectomy) plus aromatase inhibitor for 5 years.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Adjuvant chemotherapy of investigator's choice (NCCN- or ESMO-listed regimen), then ovarian function suppression plus aromatase inhibitor for 5 years.

schema.label: Radiotherapy (both arms)
schema.text: Whole breast irradiation required after lumpectomy (partial breast irradiation not permitted); post-mastectomy and regional nodal RT per protocol guidelines by nodal status. Allowed WBI regimens: 50 Gy/25, 42.56 Gy/16, 40 Gy/15, or 26 Gy/5, with optional sequential or concomitant boost. OFS plus AI preferably started before and given with RT, or within 4 weeks after RT.

schema.label: Other therapy
schema.text: CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib or other FDA-approved) and bone anti-resorptive therapy allowed per standard use.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Invasive breast cancer-free survival.

eligibility: Female, age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2 (or Karnofsky 60% or more).

Premenopausal: age 50 or under with menses within 12 months; age >50-60 with menses within 12 months plus premenopausal FSH and estradiol; or premenopausal FSH and estradiol if amenorrheic from IUD, uterine ablation, or prior hysterectomy.
Resected pT1-3 (T1c or higher if N0), pN0 or pN1 (pN1mi, pN1a-c) by AJCC 8th edition. ITCs count as N0; micrometastases (0.2-2 mm) count as N1.

Oncotype DX RS: pN0 requires RS 21-25, or RS 16-20 with high clinical risk; pN1 (1-3 nodes) requires RS below 26. MammaPrint Low Risk/MP1 patients need central Oncotype testing; MammaPrint High Risk/MP2 ineligible.
ER and/or PgR positive (1% or more by IHC) and HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP, local testing.

Lumpectomy, or total, skin-sparing, or nipple-sparing mastectomy. Lumpectomy margins free of invasive cancer and DCIS (no ink on tumor; positive posterior margin allowed if no further resection possible; LCIS at margin allowed). Mastectomy margins free of gross tumor; microscopic positive margin allowed if chest wall PMRT is planned.
Axillary staging by sentinel node biopsy, targeted axillary dissection, or ALND.
No more than 16 weeks from last breast surgery (including re-excision) to pre-entry.
Synchronous ipsilateral or contralateral, multifocal, or multicentric cancer allowed if the highest-stage tumor qualifies and other sites would not need chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy.

No prior RT, chemotherapy, or biotherapy for the current breast cancer. Endocrine therapy for this cancer limited to less than 6 weeks (neoadjuvant or adjuvant). Prior preventive tamoxifen and AI or GnRH for fertility preservation allowed.
No metastatic disease, pT4 or inflammatory breast cancer, or non-epithelial breast malignancy (sarcoma, lymphoma).
No prior invasive breast cancer in either breast (prior DCIS or LCIS allowed; prior ipsilateral DCIS treated with lumpectomy and RT requires mastectomy for the current cancer).
No life expectancy under 10 years from comorbidity.

No ANC below 1,200/mm3, platelets below 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, bilirubin above ULN (above 1.5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT above 3 x ULN, or GFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 on most recent routine labs.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be treated and cured or have undetectable viral load on therapy.
Prior or concurrent non-breast malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Hormonal contraception (including progestin IUDs) must be stopped before pre-entry. Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.text: Postmenopausal women or men with resected high anatomic stage ER-positive (>10%), HER2-negative breast cancer. Central Oncotype DX (Exact Sciences) unless prior Oncotype results exist. RS 0-25 proceeds to Step 1; RS 26-100 goes off study.

schema.text: Invasive breast cancer-free survival (non-inferiority of endocrine therapy plus ribociclib without chemotherapy). Secondary: 5-year iDFS, DDFS, DRFS, RFI, OS, BCSS, toxicity.

eligibility: Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2 within 28 days before pre-registration.
Postmenopausal woman (bilateral oophorectomy, age 60 or older, or age under 60 with 12 months of amenorrhea and postmenopausal estradiol and FSH) or man; premenopausal women not eligible.
Postoperative AJCC 8th stage: pT0-T3 with 3 positive nodes and no planned ALND, pT0-T3 N2 or N3, or pT3 N0-N3. Isolated tumor cells count as N0. No T4.
ER greater than 10% by IHC (ER-low 1-10% not eligible) and HER2-negative; multifocal or multicentric disease allowed if all sites meet these criteria.

Lumpectomy margins free of invasive cancer and DCIS (positive posterior margin allowed if no further resection possible; LCIS margins allowed); mastectomy margins free of gross tumor, with microscopic positive margins allowed only if chest wall RT will be given.
Axillary staging by SLNB, targeted axillary dissection, or ALND; final breast cancer surgery less than 16 weeks before pre-registration.
No locoregional or distant metastatic disease (documented within 28 days by history, exam, or imaging per NCCN).
Oncotype DX RS 0-25 required for randomization, on a specimen obtained before any endocrine therapy.

ANC 1,500/uL or higher, hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL or higher, platelets 100,000/uL or higher, bilirubin at or below ULN (under 1.5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less, eGFR 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher (within 28 days).
ECG within 28 days with QTcF under 450 msec and resting heart rate 50-90 bpm; NYHA class 2 or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.
HIV allowed with undetectable viral load on therapy within 6 months; HBV must be suppressed; HCV treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
No prior invasive ER-positive breast cancer (prior ER-negative breast cancer or ER-negative DCIS allowed if 5 or more years earlier without recurrence); synchronous DCIS or LCIS allowed.
No prior chemotherapy for this cancer, no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, no contraindication to chemotherapy or ribociclib.
No endocrine therapy (including chemoprevention) within 5 years except a short course of less than 6 weeks before pre-registration; no concurrent systemic HRT.

amendments.text: Amendment 3, the current version (rapid amendment): revised cabozantinib CAEPR (version 2.6, May 20, 2025) and consent risk language.
Amendment 2B closed the completed feasibility phase and opened the efficacy phase.

schema.label: Feasibility phase (completed)
schema.text: Closed as of Amendment 2B. Metastatic osteosarcoma with resectable primary received cabozantinib plus MAP to define the combination dose; Dose Level 2 (35 mg/m2/day, max 60 mg, under 18; 60 mg daily for adults, concomitant with chemotherapy) carried into the efficacy phase.

schema.label: Efficacy phase (phase 2/3), cohort assignment
schema.text: Cohort 1 (standard risk): non-pelvic, non-metastatic, resectable primary. Cohort 2 (high risk): pelvic primary, unresectable primary, and/or metastatic disease. Randomization stratified by cohort.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1 within each cohort
schema.text: MAP vs cabozantinib plus MAP; all patients get dexrazoxane before doxorubicin and myeloid growth factor after cisplatin/doxorubicin cycles

arms.label: Regimen A (standard risk) / Regimen C (high risk): MAP
arms.text: Induction 2 cycles MAP (weeks 1-10), primary tumor surgery (weeks 11-12), Consolidation cycles 1-2 MAP and cycles 3-4 MA (methotrexate, doxorubicin), ending about week 33. High risk: metastasis resection after Consolidation cycle 1, additional local/metastatic management after Consolidation cycle 4.

arms.label: Regimen B (standard risk) / Regimen D (high risk): cabozantinib plus MAP
arms.text: Same MAP backbone with daily oral cabozantinib weeks 1-7 of Induction, held around surgery, resumed in Consolidation cycle 2 after wound healing (at least 2 weeks after thoracic surgery in high risk), then Maintenance cabozantinib alone for six 28-day cycles (weeks 34-58).

schema.label: Local control of residual or metastatic disease (high risk)
schema.text: After Consolidation cycle 4 and before Maintenance: surgery, SBRT, conventional or hypofractionated RT, or ablation to unresected metastatic sites; definitive or post-operative EBRT (photon or proton) for unresectable primary or positive margins.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Feasibility (completed); EFS for cabozantinib-MAP vs MAP, analyzed separately in standard-risk and high-risk cohorts. Phase 2: 374 patients (252 standard, 122 high risk), expanding to 996 for phase 3.

eligibility: Age under 40 years at enrollment; BSA greater than 0.8 m2.
Newly diagnosed high-grade osteosarcoma, any extremity or axial primary site; osteosarcoma as a second malignancy allowed if no prior systemic chemotherapy.

Efficacy phase: localized or metastatic disease regardless of resectability, assigned to standard-risk or high-risk cohort. Lung metastasis: biopsy-proven, or one or more lesions 5 mm or larger, or multiple lesions 3 mm or larger; suspicious bone lesions need biopsy or confirmatory MRI/CT.

Creatinine within age/sex limits (for example 1.7 mg/dL male and 1.4 mg/dL female at 16 years or older), or measured creatinine clearance or GFR 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher (eGFR not acceptable); bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less; ALT 135 U/L or less.
Shortening fraction 27% or higher or ejection fraction 50% or higher; QTcF under 480 msec; no congenital long QT, NYHA III-IV heart failure, unstable angina, or serious arrhythmia.
ANC 1000/uL or higher, platelets 100,000/uL or higher (transfusion independent), hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL or higher, INR 1.5 or less.
HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months and not on strong CYP3A4, CYP2D6, or MRP2 inhibitors/inducers.
No prior systemic therapy for osteosarcoma or a prior cancer.
No CNS metastases; no central cavitating pulmonary lesions invading or encasing major lung vessels.

No primary tumor resection or attempted curative metastasectomy before enrollment; no other major surgery within 14 days (diagnostic thoracoscopy and port placement allowed); no serious or non-healing wound or fracture (pathologic fracture of primary allowed).

No clinically significant GI bleeding, perforation, obstruction, abscess, or fistula within 6 months; no hemoptysis, pulmonary hemorrhage, or significant bleeding within 3 months; no bleeding diathesis.
No uncontrolled hypertension requiring medication (above 95th percentile for age under 18, above 140/90 mmHg at 18 or older), uncompensated hypothyroidism, or Child-Pugh B or C hepatic impairment.

No enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants within 14 days, strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors, QTc-prolonging drugs, or warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, or platelet inhibitors (low-dose aspirin and LMWH allowed; therapeutic LMWH, rivaroxaban, or apixaban allowed if stable for 6 weeks).
Must be able to swallow tablets whole; no malabsorption condition affecting cabozantinib.
Not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

Subcutaneous pembrolizumab allowed; clinical stage T1bN1 replaces T1cN1; randomization required within 14 days of consent; QOL substudy closed to accrual; endocrine therapy allowed for ER-low disease; observation-arm calendar and sample timepoints revised; vital status by public records added; CAEPR removed (commercial supply); sensitivity analyses added (section 13.8).

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Clinical stage II-III TNBC with pCR after neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (at least 6 cycles) and definitive surgery. Randomize within 12 weeks of final surgery and within 14 days of consent.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Nodal status before preoperative chemotherapy (node-positive by FNA, core biopsy, or sentinel node vs node-negative); receipt of preoperative anthracycline (yes vs no).

schema.text: Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation. Protocol treatment begins within 7 days of registration.

arms.text: Physician choice: 200 mg IV every 3 weeks, or 400 mg IV every 6 weeks x 4 doses then 200 mg x 1 dose. Subcutaneous option: 395 mg every 3 weeks or 790 mg every 6 weeks. CCTG sites may use 2 mg/kg IV (max 200 mg) every 3 weeks.

arms.label: Arm 2: Observation x 27 weeks
arms.text: No protocol treatment. Visits at baseline, 12 weeks, and 27 weeks after registration.

schema.text: Standard adjuvant RT is allowed on study (preferably completed before registration) and may be given concurrently with pembrolizumab. It is not protocol treatment.

schema.text: 5 years from registration or recurrence, then annually for overall survival to 10 years.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Recurrence-free survival, non-inferiority of observation. Assumed 3-year RFS 94% with pembrolizumab; observation non-inferior if 3-year RFS is 91% or higher.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.
Triple-negative breast cancer: ER and PR 10% or less, HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP (IHC and FISH). If both breasts had invasive disease, both must meet criteria.
Clinical stage T1bN1-2 or T2-4N0-2 (stage II-III) before preoperative therapy, AJCC 8th edition.
pCR: no residual invasive disease in breast or nodes after neoadjuvant therapy. Residual DCIS allowed. Isolated tumor cells count as node-negative.
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab for at least 6 cycles, with all chemotherapy completed preoperatively.

No more than 12 weeks from final surgery to randomization. Adjuvant pembrolizumab before entry is discouraged; if given, no more than 6 weeks post-surgery and completed before registration. Investigational anti-cancer agents stopped by registration.

Adequate excision: total mastectomy, or breast-conserving surgery with negative margins (no ink on tumor, including DCIS). Persistent DCIS at the margin after re-excision requires mastectomy. LCIS at the margin is allowed.

Axilla: clinically N0 needs sentinel node biopsy; a positive post-treatment sentinel node makes the patient ineligible. Biopsy-proven N1 at diagnosis needs post-treatment axillary surgery; a positive pre-treatment sentinel node requires ALND after preoperative therapy.
Breast-conserving surgery patients must be planned to receive breast radiation.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before randomization).

ANC at least 1,000/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, eGFR at least 15 mL/min/1.73 m2, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert's up to 2.5 x ULN with normal direct bilirubin), AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN.
No stage IV disease and no evidence of recurrence after preoperative therapy and surgery.
No prior invasive breast cancer (ipsilateral or contralateral). Prior DCIS allowed. Other prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No known active liver disease (HBV, HCV, autoimmune hepatitis, sclerosing cholangitis). HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration.
Known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class 2B or better.

No grade 3-4 infusion reaction or hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab, murine proteins, or product components. Prior irAEs allowed if resolved to grade 1 or less without chronic steroids; grade 2 or lower endocrinopathies stable on replacement are allowed.
No condition requiring chronic systemic steroids (more than 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent) or other immunosuppression within the last 2 years. Physiologic replacement is allowed.
Diagnostic core biopsy tissue requested; inadequate tissue does not exclude.

schema.label: Primary endpoint

eligibility: Female sex assigned at birth, age 18 or older and under 51 at breast cancer diagnosis, and within 5 years of diagnosis.
First-time, non-metastatic breast cancer, stage 0, I, II, or III.

Able to understand, speak, read, and write English or Spanish; willing to take part in a 6-week mindfulness program; able to use a smartphone, tablet, or other digital device.
No history or current evidence of recurrent or metastatic breast cancer.
No current or prior other cancer, except non-melanoma skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer not treated with chemotherapy.
Not pregnant or planning pregnancy in the near future.
Not enrolled in another cancer control or behavioral intervention trial requiring frequent assessments or training.

A Phase III Randomized Trial of Pembrolizumab in Combination with Sacituzumab Govitecan-hziy vs Standard of Care in Anti-PD(L)1-Resistant Advanced Urothelial Cancer

schema.label: Randomization
schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, Bellmunt score 0-2, prior anti-PD(L)1 and prior enfortumab vedotin (unless contraindicated), with progression on or after the most recent therapy. N = 320.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Bellmunt score (0-1 vs 2); prior lines of therapy (<= 2 vs > 2); prior platinum exposure and current platinum eligibility (prior exposure vs no prior exposure and platinum-eligible vs no prior exposure and platinum-ineligible); duration of prior anti-PD(L)1 exposure (< 6 vs > 6 months).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 1 cycle = 21 days (+/- 3 days).

arms.label: Arm A: therapy of physician's choice (standard of care)
arms.text: One of: carboplatin AUC 4-5 day 1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 (maximum 6 cycles); cisplatin 70 mg/m2 day 1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 (maximum 6 cycles); docetaxel 75 mg/m2 day 1; or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 day 1 or 80 mg/m2 days 1, 8, and 15. Taxanes continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Switching cisplatin to carboplatin allowed; no switch from platinum to non-platinum.

arms.label: Arm B: sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab
arms.text: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, every 21 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity; pembrolizumab maximum 35 cycles or 2 years. G-CSF very strongly recommended.

schema.label: Treatment beyond progression
schema.text: Allowed if clinically stable, no ECOG decline, no AE requiring discontinuation, and no need for immediate alternative therapy (platinum doublets only through cycle 6).

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Response assessment until progression and survival for 5 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival.

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG 0-2; Bellmunt score 0-2.

Locally advanced (unresectable or not amenable to curative-intent therapy) or metastatic urothelial carcinoma of any urinary tract origin; variant histology allowed if >= 1% conventional urothelial histology; no neuroendocrine (small or large cell) and no pure non-urothelial histology.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 on imaging within 35 days before randomization.
Progression on or after the immediately prior anti-cancer therapy.
Prior anti-PD(L)1 (at least 1 dose, any setting, not necessarily the most recent therapy); no progression within 12 weeks of starting the first anti-PD(L)1.

At least 1 line of systemic therapy for advanced/metastatic disease, unless anti-PD(L)1 plus enfortumab vedotin was given in the localized setting (neoadjuvant/adjuvant) with progression within 12 months of the last dose.
Prior enfortumab vedotin or other Nectin-4 directed or MMAE-containing therapy unless contraindicated; prior FGFR inhibitor required for known susceptible FGFR3 alteration unless contraindicated.
No prior sacituzumab govitecan, other TROP-2 directed therapy, or topoisomerase I inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (for example trastuzumab deruxtecan).

No prior grade >= 3 immune-related adverse event on anti-PD(L)1, except endocrinopathies on replacement and clinically insignificant lab abnormalities. Prior therapy toxicities recovered to grade 1 (neuropathy within the protocol limit, alopecia, and non-significant lab abnormalities excepted).

Labs within 14 days: ANC >= 1,500/uL, platelets >= 100,000/uL, Hb >= 8.5 g/dL, albumin >= 3 g/dL, total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN (<= 5 x ULN with liver metastases), CrCl >= 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No known UGT1A1 deficiency (Gilbert's syndrome); UGT1A1 testing not required.
Treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression and no steroids > 10 mg prednisone equivalent daily for brain metastases for at least 7 days before randomization.

No systemic immunosuppressive medication, including steroids > 10 mg prednisone equivalent daily (short bursts stopped before randomization and inhaled, intranasal, intra-articular, or topical steroids allowed).

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Arm A
schema.text: Cisplatin-based chemoradiation, placebo, and the institution's standard treatment for mucositis.

schema.label: Arm B
schema.text: Cisplatin-based chemoradiation, prophylactic gabapentin titrated to 1200 mg three times a day, and the institution's standard treatment for mucositis.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: About 10 weeks: a 12-day ramp up that may start any time from randomization through day 8 of chemoradiation, 7 weeks during radiotherapy, and a 12-day ramp down.

eligibility: Squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, stage I-IV. See section 3.2.1.
Planned cisplatin-based chemoradiation, weekly or every 3 weeks. Induction chemotherapy is allowed.
Able to swallow capsules whole.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 2 or better. Not pregnant and not nursing.
No known hypersensitivity to gabapentin or its ingredients.
No dialysis and no transplanted organ.
No prior surgery or radiation for head and neck cancer, and not being treated for recurrent head and neck cancer.
No planned surgery, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy after the 7 weeks of standard chemoradiation.
No known brain metastases.
No nonprescribed opioid use, including heroin, within 6 months before registration.
No prescribed medication for chronic or long-term pain or neuropathy.
No current mefloquine.
Not taking medication for a psychiatric illness. No existing sleep apnea. No acute narrow-angle glaucoma.
No uncontrolled concurrent illness. No investigational agent within 30 days before registration. No enrollment on another systemic pain-control study.
Must be able to speak, read, or comprehend English or Spanish. Patients with impaired decision-making are not eligible.

Phase II Trial of SMO/  AKT/  NF2/ CDK Inhibitors in Progressive Meningiomas with SMO/  AKT/  NF2/ CDK Pathway Mutations

amendments.text: Update #18, the current version: adds the abemaciclib expansion cohort (Group 8, PFS6 sole primary endpoint), shortens the post-RT interval in Section 3.3.3 from 4 to 2 weeks, extends the pre-registration to registration window from 28 to 56 days, and corrects '24 weeks' to '2 weeks' on the schema eligibility page.

schema.label: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory central pathology review and biomarker testing (MGH/DFCI) of FFPE tissue to confirm meningioma and assign a mutation-matched arm. If multiple alterations, enroll to the least common (NF2 most common, SMO least). Negative for a targetable alteration, or matching cohort closed: no registration. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Closed arms
schema.text: NF2: GSK2256098 750 mg PO BID (Groups 1-2, closed July 2017). SMO/PTCH1: vismodegib 150 mg PO daily (Groups 3-4, closed February 2018). NF2/CDK pathway: abemaciclib 200 mg PO BID original cohort (Group 7, closed October 2022).

schema.label: AKT1/PIK3CA/PTEN arm (Groups 5-6)
schema.text: Capivasertib 480 mg PO BID, 4 days on and 3 days off each week. Cohorts by grade (I vs II/III).

schema.label: Abemaciclib expansion cohort (Group 8, added Update #18)
schema.text: NF2 mutation, CDKN2A copy number loss, or CDK4, CDK6, CCND1, CCND2, CCND3, or CCNE1 copy number gain; grade 2/3 by central review: abemaciclib 200 mg PO BID.

schema.label: Treatment and follow-up
schema.text: Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Off-treatment without progression: scans for up to 2 years. Survival follow-up up to 5 years from registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS at 6 months and response rate per arm/cohort; the abemaciclib expansion cohort uses PFS6 as the sole primary endpoint.

eligibility: Histologically proven intracranial meningioma (any grade) by central review, with a qualifying alteration by the central lab: SMO, PTCH1, NF2, CDKN2A, AKT1, PIK3CA, or PTEN mutation; CDKN2A copy number loss; or CDK4, CDK6, CCND1, CCND2, CCND3, or CCNE1 copy number gain.

Progressive or residual measurable disease: residual disease right after surgery, or growth of 25% or more in bidimensional area between scans no more than 25 months apart (grade I requires documented pre-operative progression). Bidimensionally measurable lesion at least 10 mm in both dimensions on MRI (preferred) or CT; multifocal and spinal meningiomas allowed.

Prior RT allowed with progression after RT: at least 24 weeks from RT completion if the progressive lesion was irradiated; at least 2 weeks if the progressive lesion is outside the RT field. Abemaciclib arm: at least 28 days and full recovery from adjuvant RT.

Any number of prior therapies. No chemotherapy, cancer-directed hormonal therapy, or investigational agent within 28 days (nitrosourea or mitomycin C within 6 weeks); no concurrent meningioma-directed therapy. Abemaciclib arm: chemotherapy washout at least 28 days with recovery to grade 1 or less.
Stable steroid dose for at least 4 days; recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy (except alopecia and fatigue); no craniotomy within 28 days before or after registration.
Age 18 or older (30 or older for SMO/PTCH1); ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.
No metastatic (extracranial) meningioma. NF patients may have other CNS tumors (schwannoma, acoustic neuroma, ependymoma) if stable for 6 months.

No known active hepatitis B or C, Child-Pugh B or C liver disease, uncontrolled gastric ulcer (grade 3 within 28 days), uncontrolled hypertension (BP >140/90), or abdominal fistula, GI perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within 28 days.

Labs: ANC 1,500/mm3 or more; platelets 100,000/mm3 or more; creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less or CrCl >50 mL/min; bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (unless Gilbert's); AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less; Na, K, and corrected Ca normal; QTcF <450 msec; resting heart rate 50-100 bpm.

Capivasertib arm: no major surgery within 28 days; no clinically important EKG abnormality or QT risk factors; no CABG, angioplasty, stent, MI, angina, or NYHA class II or higher heart failure within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypotension; LVEF 50% or more and within institutional normal; hemoglobin 9 g/dL or more; no 3+ proteinuria or >500 mg/24 h; no prior ILD or steroid-treated radiation pneumonitis; no prior allogeneic transplant or immunodeficiency.

Capivasertib arm diabetes rules: HbA1c <8.0%, no type 1 diabetes, no insulin, no more than two oral agents; fasting glucose <167 mg/dL with known type 2 diabetes or <126 mg/dL without. NF2 or SMO/PTCH1: no uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >7.5 or fasting glucose >140 mg/dL).

Abemaciclib arm: grade 2/3 by central review; hemoglobin 8 g/dL or more (transfusion allowed); no active bacterial infection needing IV antibiotics, fungal infection, or detectable viral infection (including known HIV or active hepatitis B/C); no history of cardiovascular syncope, pathologic ventricular arrhythmia, or sudden cardiac arrest.

No uncontrolled comorbidity (for example ILD, dyspnea at rest or oxygen need, major gastric or small bowel resection, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, chronic baseline grade 2 or higher diarrhea); no allergy to compounds similar to the assigned drug.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors stopped 14 days before registration, and no strong CYP3A4 inducers or CYP2D6 substrates (capivasertib); abemaciclib: avoid CYP3A inducers and strong inhibitors.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective observational cohort study. No protocol treatment: participants start standard-of-care immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy chosen by their physician. Limited to NCORP and MU-NCORP community sites since Revision #6.

schema.label: Cohorts
schema.text: Cohort 1: ICI alone (closed 05/06/2024). Cohort 2: chemotherapy plus ICI for SCLC or NSCLC, gastroesophageal cancer, or triple-negative breast cancer on listed regimens, in the advanced or neoadjuvant setting, given per NCCN Category 1 or 2A and not on a clinical trial.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Consent, baseline assessments and PROs, then start ICI within 7 days of registration.

schema.label: Evaluations
schema.text: Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52 after starting ICI, plus an evaluation at any grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event (irAE). Participation ends after the week 52 evaluation.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Develop and validate risk models for grade 3 or higher non-hematologic irAEs within the first year of ICI therapy.

eligibility: Planned to start standard-of-care ICI (Cohort 1) or chemotherapy plus ICI on a listed regimen for an eligible tumor type (Cohort 2) within 7 days after registration; not on a clinical trial for this treatment.
Prior ICI allowed only if completed at least 180 days before registration and not discontinued for an irAE.
No chemotherapy, biologic, or targeted therapy within 14 days before registration; hormonal therapy allowed.
Cohort 2: no planned targeted or non-ICI biologic therapy with the chemotherapy plus ICI regimen.
Recovered from prior treatment toxicity to grade 1 or less non-hematologic (grade 2 or less for neuropathy and alopecia) and grade 3 or less hematologic.
Palliative radiotherapy, growth factors, and osteoclast inhibitors allowed.
Age 18 or older; history and physical within 28 days before registration.
Able to complete PRO questionnaires in English, Spanish, or French; baseline PROs completed within 14 days before registration.

schema.label: Entry

arms.label: Arm 1 (control)
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 5 IV Day 1 + pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 IV Day 1 + bevacizumab (or biosimilar) 10 mg/kg IV Days 1 and 15, every 28 days. If LVEF < LLN: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8 replaces PLD, with carboplatin AUC 4 Day 1 and bevacizumab Day 1, every 21 days.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: At least 6 and up to 10 cycles unless limited by intolerable AEs. Maintenance bevacizumab may start after 6 cycles and starts in all patients after 10 cycles (or earlier if chemotherapy/SG stopped for toxicity before 6 cycles). G-CSF prophylaxis allowed in both arms for high febrile neutropenia risk.

schema.label: Maintenance (both arms)
schema.text: Bevacizumab (or biosimilar) 15 mg/kg IV Day 1 every 21 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Imaging

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival (RECIST 1.1, local investigator assessment).

eligibility: Histologic high-grade serous or endometrioid epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer.
Platinum-sensitive disease: progression documented ≥ 6 months (182 days) after the last platinum dose.
Progression during first-line maintenance PARP inhibitor for advanced disease, with no intervening therapy between PARPi progression and registration; last PARPi dose ≥ 3 weeks before registration.
Germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutation, or HRD test positive.
Measurable or non-measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
Age ≥ 18; ECOG performance status ≤ 2.
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed).
CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault); urinalysis ≤ 1+ protein or urine protein < 1.0 g/24 hr.
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 3 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT ≤ 3 x ULN.
Patients with cardiac disease history, current symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.
No prior topoisomerase-I inhibitor of any kind.
No investigational agents within 4 weeks of registration, and no concurrent non-study anticancer therapy.
Treated brain metastases allowed only with follow-up imaging 4 weeks after CNS-directed therapy showing no progression and disease stable off steroids.
No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics; no non-healing wound, ulcer, or fracture.
No intra-abdominal abscess, undiverted abdominal/pelvic fistula, GI perforation, GI obstruction, or need for drainage NG or gastrostomy tube.
No clinically significant bleeding within 28 days; no uncontrolled hypertension (≥ 160 systolic or ≥ 100 diastolic).

No unresolved prior-therapy toxicity > grade 1 (except grade ≤ 2 neuropathy, alopecia, controlled hypertension or thyroid disease, thromboembolism on anticoagulation, and lab AEs meeting the lab criteria); no major surgery within 3 weeks.
No strong UGT1A1 inhibitors or inducers; no allergy to study agents or their excipients.

HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing. Secondary or cytoreductive surgery on study before progression is not permitted.

Histologically confirmed RCC with a clear cell component, with or without sarcomatoid features, after complete radical or partial nephrectomy. Microscopically positive soft tissue or vascular margins without gross residual disease allowed.

Risk group: intermediate-high (pT2 grade 4 or sarcomatoid N0M0, or pT3 any grade N0M0); high (pT4 N0M0, or any pT N+ M0); or M1 NED (solid, isolated soft-tissue metastases, not brain or bone, resected or treated with definitive radiation or ablation synchronously or within 1 year of nephrectomy).
Surgery (nephrectomy, metastasectomy, or ablation) more than 4 and no more than 16 weeks before registration, with no ongoing surgical complications.
No evidence of disease on CT or MRI of brain, chest, abdomen, and pelvis. No prior systemic therapy for RCC.

ANC at least 1,000/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN, CrCl at least 30 mL/min, urine protein 1+ or less on UA or UPCR below 2 mg/mg.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 14 days before registration).
HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
Cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class IIB or better. No history of myocarditis or clinically significant pneumonitis.
No uncontrolled hypertension (above 150/90 on 2 readings at least 2 hours apart).
No grade 3 or higher GI, pulmonary, or GU bleeding within 1 month. No moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C).
No active peptic ulcer disease, IBD, or other GI condition with perforation risk; no abdominal fistula, GI perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within 4 weeks.
No serious non-healing wound, ulcer, or fracture within 28 days. No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics. No allogeneic organ transplant.

No autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past 2 years (replacement therapy, vitiligo, psoriasis, type 1 diabetes, stable hypothyroidism, Sjogren's allowed). No steroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent within 14 days of starting treatment or other immunosuppressants within 30 days of randomization.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers (stop 14 days before treatment). No hypersensitivity to study drugs.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment; no currently active second malignancy.

studies.title: Consolidative Use of Radiotherapy to Block (CURB2) Oligoprogression in Patients with Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer - A Randomized Phase 3 Trial

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This is an international multi-centre, open-label, randomized phase III trial in participants with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comparing: 1) systemic therapy at the investigator’s discretion and no SBRT; 2) the addition of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to extra -cranial oligoprogressive disease and continuation of first -line systemic therapy with standard of care (SOC) immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) +/- chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: First-line systemic therapy (ICI alone versus ICI and chemotherapy) Number of oligoprogressive lesions (1, 2 versus 3, 4 or 5) Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (0, 1 versus 2)

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Participants with metastatic NSCLC on first-line ICI- based systemic therapy having received at least 3 cycles Restaging studies reveal ≤ 5 extracranial oligoprogressive lesions, all of which must be amenable to SBRT* Oligoprogressive lesions are asymptomatic, not requiring palliative radiotherapy at the time of study enrollment

schema.label: Randomize

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Systemic therapy at the investigator’s discretion, no SBRT Continue with SOC treatment until disease progression** Follow-up for survival (every 12 weeks)

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: SBRT/radiotherapy* to all sites of oligoprogression followed by the same first-line SOC systemic therapy permitted. Please see Section 7.0 for further details.

schema.note: N = 320 participants If a metastatic site is best treated with hypofractionated radiation instead of SBRT, this will be See Section 8.0 for guidelines regarding disease progression.

eligibility: Metastatic disease (stage IV) detected on imaging and histologically and/or cytologically confirmed

NSCLC as per the WHO Classification of Tumours and AJCC 8th Edition TNM Classification, withoutadriver mutation with an actionable first-line targeted therapy, for whom either ICI alone or combination ICI + chemotherapy is indicated.
Oligoprogression on first -line ICI +/ - chemotherapy systemic therapy after at least 3 cycles.
Oligoprogression is evaluated independently for each lesion, and will be defined as follows
Modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST 1.1 [Eisenhauer 2009] )

1) At least a 20% increase in the longest diameter (LD) ofalesion except for lymph nodes where only the short axis is measured, taking as reference the smallest LD/short axis recorded since nadir, and ≥ 5 mm increase in the LD/short axis, OR;
2) The appearance of one or more new lesions, each ≥ 5 mm in size. OR
Modified Positron Emission Tomography Response Criteria in Solid Tumours (PERCIST [Wahl 2009] )
1) >30% increase in 18F FDG SUV max, with >0.8 SUV units increase in tumour SUV from previous baseline scan in pattern typical of tumour and not of infection/treatment effect, OR;
2) Visible increase in the extent of 18F-FDG tumour uptake, OR;
3) New 18F-FDG avid lesions typical of cancer (including new bone lesion) and not related to treatment effect and/or infection.

There is no upper limit to the number of total metastatic sites, butamaximum of 5 progressive metastatic sites, inclusive of primary disease and metastatic lesions, all of which must be extracranial. CONFIDENTIAL 14 CONFIDENTIAL PROTOCOL - UPDATE #7: 2026-JAN-07

All sites of oligoprogression can be safely treated with SBRT or ablative radiotherapy as determined by the treating radiation oncologist, including availability and tolerability of necessary technologies (e.g. active breathing control, MRLinac, fiducial insertion, etc.) and accounting for previous radiotherapy overlap. Safety must be assessed and determined byaradiation oncologist prior to enrollment.

Participants with treated CNS disease who have radiologic and clinical evidence of stable brain metastases, with no evidence of cavitation or hemorrhage in the brain lesion, are eligible providing that they are asymptomatic and do not require corticostero ids (must have discontinued steroids at least 1 week prior to randomization). Anticonvulsants are allowed. Participants with new or progressive brain metastases
Candidate for regulatory approved SOC first-line or second-line systemic therapy options.
Participants must have adequate organ and marrow function according to the relevant systemic therapies’ current Product Monographs and local / provincial / institutional formulary guidelines.
Participants must be ≥ 18 years of age.
ECOG performance status of 0, 1 or 2.
Prior Therapy Systemic Therapy

Participants that received prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant/consolidation systemic therapy (including chemotherapy and ICI) are eligible if at least 6 months have elapsed between the completion of prior therapy and start of first line treatment for metastatic disease.
Patients must meet the criteria for oligoprogression on first-line ICI +/- chemotherapy for metastatic disease as per eligibility criteria 4.1.2.
Participants must have recovered to ≤ grade 1 from all reversible toxicity related to prior systemic therapy. If participants experienced prior immune-mediated toxicity and have not yet re-initiated
ICI therapy, please contact CCTG. Please also contact CCTG if participants have ongoing toxicity be clinically insignificant.≥ grade 1 felt to Surgery
Previous surgery related to NSCLC in the curative or metastatic disease setting is permitted.

Previous major surgery is permitted provided that the participant has recovered from related clinically significant adverse events upon enrollment. CONFIDENTIAL 15 CONFIDENTIAL PROTOCOL - UPDATE #7: 2026-JAN-07 Radiation

Prior external beam radiation related to NSCLC in the metastatic disease setting is permitted provided the participant has recovered from related clinically significant adverse events upon enrollment. Participants that received prior external beam radiation therapy in the NSCLC curative disease setting (including the primary lesion) are eligible. Oligoprogressive lesions previously treated with external beam

Prior conventional, non- stereotactic radiotherapy for palliative purposes is allowed, and if the palliated lesion subsequently progressed but remains asymptomatic and does not require immediate radiotherapy, the lesion can still be counted toward one of the five oligoprogressive lesions.

Participant is able (i.e. sufficiently fluent) and willing to complete the quality of life and/or health utility questionnaires in either English, French, or Spanish. The baseline assessment must be completed within required timelines, prior to enrollment. Inability (lack of comprehension in
English, French, Spanish, or other equivalent reason such as cognitive issues or lack of competency) to complete the questionnaires will not make the participant ineligible for the study.
However, ability but unwillingness to complete the questionnaires will make the participant ineligible.

schema.label: Favorable risk
schema.text: Study entry, favorable risk, ABVD for 2 cycles, then PET2 (FDG-PET after 2 cycles of ABVD) with rapid central review. Unfavorable disease, used to leave this schema, is one or more of: large mediastinal mass (> 10 cm by CT or 1/3 of the maximum chest diameter by chest radiograph), > 3 nodal sites, B symptoms with ESR > 30, ESR > 50 without B symptoms, or age > 50 years. Anticipated randomization shares: Arms A and E 42.5%, Arms B and F 42.5%, Arms C and G 7.5%, Arms D and H 7.5%. ABVD is doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine. AVD drops bleomycin. Bv-Nivo is brentuximab vedotin and nivolumab. eBEACOPP is bleomycin, etoposide, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone, and procarbazine. eBPDac replaces procarbazine with dacarbazine. ISRT is involved-site radiotherapy. The ISRT dose is not printed on the schema.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Rapid early response. Randomize to ABVD for 2 cycles, then end of protocol therapy.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Rapid early response. Randomize to brentuximab vedotin and nivolumab for 4 cycles, then end of protocol therapy.

eligibility: Age 5 to 60 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed, untreated, histologically confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma (nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted, or not otherwise specified) with stage I or II disease.
Bidimensionally measurable disease, at least one lesion with longest diameter >= 1.5 cm.
Whole body or limited whole body PET within 42 days before enrollment. PET-CT is strongly preferred. PET-MRI is allowed if intravenous contrast-enhanced CT is also obtained.

Pediatric patients age 5-17 years with known or suspected mediastinal disease must have an upright PA chest radiograph for bulk assessment. If both CT chest and upright PA chest radiograph were done, bulk may be met by either modality.
Age >= 18 years: Zubrod 0, 1, or 2. Age <= 17 years: Lansky >= 50.

Eligibility laboratories within 28 days before enrollment unless otherwise indicated. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, creatinine, ESR, and, for known infections, HIV, HBV, and HCV if more than 28 days have elapsed before therapy.
Clinical studies, if applicable, within 42 days before enrollment and start of therapy. Disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 42 days.

Pediatric renal function (age 5-17 years): serum or plasma creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection, creatinine within 28 days, actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, multiplied by 0.85 if female.

Total bilirubin <= 2 times the upper limit of normal, and AST and ALT <= 3 times the upper limit of normal, unless due to Gilbert disease, lymphomatous involvement of the liver, or vanishing bile duct syndrome.
Shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, MUGA, or functional cardiac imaging, or ejection fraction >= 50% by radionuclide angiogram, echocardiogram, MUGA, or cardiac imaging.
DLCO >= 50% of predicted, corrected for hemoglobin. If PFTs cannot be obtained, pulse oximetry > 92% on room air.

Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic HBV must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must have been treated and cured, or, if currently treated, the HCV viral load must be undetectable.
No nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. No history of active interstitial pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease.
No poorly controlled inherited or acquired immunodeficiency requiring active medications, such as a primary immunodeficiency syndrome, and no organ transplant recipients.

No known uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would jeopardize safety, including infection, autoimmune conditions, cardiac arrhythmias, angina pectoris, and gastrointestinal disorders affecting swallowing or absorption of pills.

No systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days before enrollment. The corticosteroid threshold is equivalent to > 10 mg daily prednisone for age >= 18 years, or > 0.5 mg/kg (up to 10 mg/day) for age < 18 years. Thyroxine, insulin, and physiologic adrenal or pituitary replacement are allowed. Inhaled or topical steroids and adrenal replacement doses at or below those thresholds are allowed if there is no active autoimmune disease. Steroids for Hodgkin lymphoma symptoms are allowed but must stop by Cycle 1, Day 1.
No peripheral neuropathy > Grade 1 at enrollment and no known Charcot-Marie-Tooth syndrome.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of the regimen.

No prior chemotherapy, radiation, or antibody-based treatment for classic Hodgkin lymphoma. No prior solid organ transplant. No prior allogeneic stem cell transplantation. No live vaccine within 30 days before planned Day 1 of protocol therapy. mRNA vaccines are permitted.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. A pregnancy test within 28 days before enrollment is required for females of childbearing potential. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed from the first dose through at least 6 months after the last treatment are not eligible.

studies.title: APOLLO: A Randomized Phase II Double-Blind Study of Olaparib Versus Placebo Following Curative Intent Therapy in Patients with Resected Pancreatic Cancer and a Pathogenic BRCA1, BRCA2 or PALB2 Mutation

schema.label: Step 0 (pre-registration)
schema.text: Resected pancreatic cancer with pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline or somatic BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 mutation; local CLIA reports undergo central expert review before Step 1.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: R1 vs R0 resection; platinum vs non-platinum perioperative chemotherapy; neoadjuvant vs adjuvant therapy.

schema.label: Step 1 randomization
schema.text: Double-blind, 2:1 (olaparib:placebo) after at least 12 weeks of perioperative chemotherapy; 152 patients randomized.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID, Days 1-28, 28-day cycles x 12 cycles

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Placebo 300 mg PO BID, Days 1-28, 28-day cycles x 12 cycles

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Relapse-free survival. Follow-up for survival 10 years from Step 1 randomization.

eligibility: Age 18 or older; ECOG PS 0-2
Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma, acinar, squamous, or adenosquamous carcinoma (no neuroendocrine tumors) with no evidence of recurrence
Pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline or somatic BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 mutation by CLIA (or equivalently accredited) test; tumor-only results require germline testing
Completed at least 12 weeks (up to 6 months) of perioperative multi-agent chemotherapy; prior radiation or chemoradiation allowed
Randomization 21-84 days after the last treatment
No recurrence on scans within 4 weeks before randomization
No progression on prior platinum therapy
Prior toxicities resolved to Grade 1 or less (except alopecia and neuropathy)
WBC at least 3,000/mcL, ANC at least 1,500/mcL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, Hgb at least 9.0 g/dL without transfusion within 28 days
Bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (Gilbert's: direct bilirubin 2.5 x ULN or less); AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less; creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less or CrCl over 50 mL/min
No history of MDS or AML
No GI disorder affecting absorption of oral medication
No potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
No uncontrolled cardiac ECG abnormalities, QTc over 500 ms, or congenital long QT syndrome
No active treatment for a concurrent malignancy (adjuvant hormonal therapy and topical skin therapy allowed)
No major surgery within 2 weeks before Step 1 randomization
Not pregnant or breastfeeding; negative pregnancy test within 14 days before randomization

amendments.text: Amendment #5A, the current version (activated April 7, 2023). Rapid amendment inserting revised tovorafenib CAEPR v2.2 and clarifying that reconstituted suspension must be used within 15 minutes.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG single-arm Phase 2 of tovorafenib (DAY101) in relapsed or refractory LCH with a RAS/RAF or receptor tyrosine kinase pathway mutation. Two cohorts: BRAFV600E positive (cohort 1, up to 26 evaluable) and BRAFV600E negative (cohort 2, up to 17 evaluable).

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Tovorafenib 380 mg/m2 (max 600 mg) enterally once weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22 of 28-day cycles, up to 12 cycles. Tablet or suspension (suspension required if BSA < 0.9 m2).

schema.label: Response evaluation
schema.text: Organ-specific imaging and FDG-PET at day 28 of cycles 2, 4, and 9 and at end of therapy.

schema.label: Primary aim
schema.text: Overall response rate after 2 cycles, maintained 4 weeks later, in each cohort. Secondary aims include toxicity, 1-year EFS, PFS, OS, and durability of CR after stopping therapy.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 28 days after end of therapy, then 3, 6, and 12 months and 2 years after cycle 12; off study at 5 years from enrollment.

eligibility: Age 180 days to < 22 years at enrollment; BSA ≥ 0.3 m2.

Histologically verified LCH (original diagnosis or relapse) that is progressive, relapsed, or refractory after at least one prior systemic treatment, with measurable disease. Pathology report due for central review within 7 days of enrollment.
Pathogenic somatic mutation in CSF1R, ERBB3, ALK, RAS, or RAF by PCR or sequencing (IHC alone not sufficient).
No activating MAP2K1 mutation.
No skin-limited disease, GI-only disease, or LCH-associated neurodegeneration without parenchymal or systemic lesions.
No LCH arising with another hematologic malignancy and no history of non-histiocytic malignancy.
Karnofsky or Lansky ≥ 50% (ECOG 0-2); able to take enteral medication.
Washouts: myelosuppressive chemotherapy 14 days; investigational or other anticancer therapy, including MAPK inhibitors, 14 days; RT 2 weeks from last fraction; prior toxicities ≤ grade 1.
Steroids ≤ 0.5 mg/kg/day prednisone equivalent (max 20 mg/day) averaged over the prior month; no strong CYP2C8 inducers or inhibitors or narrow-index BCRP substrates within 14 days.
ANC ≥ 750/µL, platelets ≥ 75,000/µL, hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL (transfusion allowed with documented marrow disease).
Creatinine within age limits or GFR ≥ 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, albumin ≥ 2 g/dL unless due to histiocytic liver disease.
Fractional shortening ≥ 25% or ejection fraction > 50%; no QTc > 440 ms, active cardiovascular disease, or MI, DVT, or PE within 6 months.
No known significant ophthalmologic condition or risk factors for retinal vein occlusion or central serous retinopathy.
No prior solid organ or hematopoietic transplant.
No grade ≥ 2 CNS hemorrhage history or any CNS hemorrhage within 28 days.
No major surgery within 14 days, uncontrolled infection, malabsorption, DRESS or SJS history, or grade 3 symptomatic CPK elevation.
Not pregnant or breastfeeding; non-hormonal contraception required for 28 days after the last dose.

studies.title: Randomized Phase 2 Study of Iberdomide Maintenance Therapy Following Idecabtagene Vicleucel CAR-T in Multiple Myeloma Patients

amendments.text: Update #03, the current version: eligibility broadened to 2 or more prior lines, dose level -1.5 (0.75 mg with growth factors) added, prior lines added as a stratification factor, growth-factor washout rules for enrollment labs, pregnancy prevention training moved to CTSU CLASS.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: All patients pre-register; blood and marrow submitted only for those consenting to biobanking. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Safety run-in
schema.text: Iberdomide days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle at the assigned dose level: 0 = 1 mg (starting, no growth factors), -1 = 0.75 mg (no growth factors), -1.5 = 0.75 mg (growth factors permitted). DLT window is the first 3 cycles. Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Primary endpoint: DLTs.

schema.label: Randomized phase II: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 60 patients not in the run-in. Stratified by response before randomization (SD vs PR vs VGPR vs CR/sCR), known extramedullary disease (yes vs no), and prior lines (2-3 vs 4 or more). No crossover.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Active monitoring off therapy.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Maintenance iberdomide at the recommended phase 2 dose, days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Primary endpoint (phase II)
schema.text: PFS from randomization. Follow-up 4 years from registration.

eligibility: Multiple myeloma with SD or better by IMWG criteria at day 80-110 after idecabtagene vicleucel (ide-cel) infusion; deep remissions (CR, MRD-negative) eligible.
Ide-cel infusion within 80-110 days before registration; ide-cel adverse events resolved to grade 1 (except fatigue, alopecia, and similar low-risk events).
2 or more prior lines of MM therapy (including a PI, an IMiD, and an anti-CD38 antibody).
Prior iberdomide allowed, but not iberdomide-refractory (progression on or within 60 days of stopping iberdomide).
No MM-directed therapy since ide-cel infusion; steroids for ide-cel toxicity allowed if off steroids for >30 days by C1D1.
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 1,500/mm3 or more; platelets 75,000/mm3 or more; CrCl 30 mL/min or more by MDRD; bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less; AST/ALT 3 x ULN or less. No platelet transfusion or growth factor to meet criteria (1 week for short-acting myeloid factors; 2 weeks for platelet or pegylated factors).
No POEMS syndrome or vital-organ amyloidosis (skin, lymph node, or incidental marrow amyloid allowed); plasma cell leukemia allowed.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load if on treatment.
No active infection at registration (completed treatment for resolved infection and chronic maintenance antimicrobials allowed).
No known iberdomide allergy; able to swallow oral agents.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors must be switched with washout (ideally 3 half-lives) before C1D1.

studies.title: A Phase 2 Study Using Chemoimmunotherapy with Gemcitabine, Cisplatin and Nivolumab in Newly Diagnosed Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (NPC)

schema.label: Induction and consolidation
schema.text: Study entry, then induction chemoimmunotherapy: 3 cycles of cisplatin, gemcitabine, and nivolumab. Evaluation of response. Consolidation chemoradioimmunotherapy: radiation concurrent with 2 cycles of cisplatin plus nivolumab, followed by 1 cycle of nivolumab only. Patients may continue on protocol therapy in the absence of progressive disease or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Response-based radiotherapy dose
schema.text: On the schema, the response split is below the consolidation box and above maintenance. Both paths then go to maintenance immunotherapy, 6 cycles of nivolumab, then off protocol therapy.

arms.label: CR
arms.text: PTV1 45 Gy. PTV2 45 plus 9 Gy (54 Gy).

arms.label: PR or SD
arms.text: PTV1 45 Gy. PTV2 45 plus 14.4 Gy (59.4 Gy).

eligibility: Age <= 21 years at enrollment. No lower age bound is printed.
Newly diagnosed AJCC stage II-IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma, with histologic verification of the malignancy at original diagnosis.
Lansky >= 60% if <= 16 years, or Karnofsky >= 60% if > 16 years.
Enroll before treatment begins. Protocol therapy is projected to start no later than 5 calendar days after enrollment. Patients started on protocol therapy before enrollment are ineligible.

Eligibility laboratories within 7 days before enrollment. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, and serum creatinine before therapy if more than 7 days have elapsed. Clinical studies and disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 21 days.
ANC >= 1000/µL and platelets >= 100,000/µL, transfusion independent.

Creatinine clearance or radioisotope GFR >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 1 month to < 6 months 0.4/0.4, 6 months to < 1 year 0.5/0.5, 1 to < 2 years 0.6/0.6, 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4.
Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, and ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
Shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, or ejection fraction >= 50% by radionuclide angiogram.
No dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry > 94% if there is a clinical indication to measure it.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months and a T-cell count above the lower limit of normal is eligible. Chronic HBV must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must have been treated and cured, or, if currently treated, the viral load must be undetectable.
No prior radiotherapy to the head or neck. No prior chemotherapy or radiation for any cancer in the last 3 years; the protocol also states those patients must be in remission.

No diagnosis of immunodeficiency. No active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment in the past 2 years (disease-modifying agents, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive agents). Replacement thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroid is not systemic treatment. Well-controlled asthma with no systemic steroids for asthma in the last 12 months is not excluded.

No systemic corticosteroids above 0.25 mg/kg (10 mg) daily prednisone equivalent within 14 days, and no other immunosuppressive medications within 30 days of enrollment. Inhaled or topical steroids, and adrenal replacement steroid doses above 0.25 mg/kg (10 mg) daily prednisone equivalent, are permitted if there is no active autoimmune disease.

No history of non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids, and no current pneumonitis. No detectable viral load of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C, and no active tuberculosis, subject to the HIV, HBV, and HCV rules above. No solid organ or allogeneic hematopoietic transplant at any time.

Females of childbearing potential, defined as post-menarchal, need a negative pregnancy test. Lactating females are not eligible unless they agree not to breastfeed from the first dose through 5 months after the last dose of nivolumab.
