studies.title: Phase 1b/ 2 Trial of Pidnarulex in MYC Aberrant Lymphoma
Evaluating Adjuvant Atezolizumab or Atezolizumab and Hyaluronidase-TQJS to Prevent Recurrence in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC): A Randomized Phase III Trial (AASI-NSCLC)

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Completely resected pathologic stage IA3 or IB NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%, registered 21-77 days after surgery. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Tumor stage (IA3 vs IB); histology (squamous vs non-squamous); visceral pleural invasion (present vs absent).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified permuted blocks

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Observation with active surveillance (clinical exam and CT chest per calendar).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs 1875 mg SC every 3 weeks (preferred) or atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks, 21-day cycles, for up to 1 year from randomization (maximum 17 cycles), or until unacceptable toxicity, recurrence, or new lung primary. Route is not switched once chosen.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 10 years from registration for recurrence and survival.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Disease-free survival (recurrence, second lung primary, or death), intent-to-treat.

eligibility: Pathologic stage IA3 or IB NSCLC (AJCC 9th edition), any histology except tumors containing small-cell morphology.

Complete R0 resection by lobectomy or greater; sublobar resection (wedge or segmentectomy) allowed only if the tumor was ≤ 2 cm on clinical staging, with a CT chest confirming size within 60 days of surgery.
Adequate nodal sampling per Commission on Cancer 2020 standard: at least one hilar station (level 10 or higher) and at least three distinct mediastinal stations (levels 2-9).
PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50% by an FDA-approved assay (e.g., SP263, SP142, 22C3, 28-8) on surgical or biopsy specimen.
No EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation and no ALK fusion; purely squamous tumors do not require EGFR/ALK testing.
Registration no earlier than 21 days and no later than 77 days after resection, recovered from surgery.
No prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy for this lung cancer.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS ≤ 2 (or Karnofsky ≥ 60%).
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert syndrome < 3.0 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No current pneumonitis, no history of non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids, and no history of interstitial lung disease.
No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within the last 2 years (replacement therapy such as thyroid hormone, insulin, or physiologic adrenal/pituitary steroids is allowed).

No systemic corticosteroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days before registration (inhaled, topical, ocular, intra-articular, intranasal steroids, physiologic replacement, and brief prophylactic courses allowed).
No prior allogeneic bone marrow, stem cell, or solid organ transplant; no live vaccine within 30 days before registration; no grade ≥ 3 hypersensitivity to atezolizumab or excipients.

No uncontrolled intercurrent illness, including active infection requiring systemic therapy, symptomatic CHF (NYHA ≥ III), unstable angina, or unstable arrhythmia; patients with heart failure history or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration. No active hepatitis B or C (history allowed if HBsAg negative and HCV RNA negative); no testing required without known history.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if its natural history or treatment will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential).

studies.title: A Randomized Phase II Trial for High-Risk Multiple Myeloma that is Refractory or in First Relapse with Daratumumab, Teclistamab (DT) Versus Daratumumab, Pomalidomide, Dexamethasone (DPd) or Daratumumab, Carfilzomib, Dexamethasone (DKd)

schema.label: Randomization
schema.text: High-risk multiple myeloma, relapsed or refractory after exactly one prior line, daratumumab (or isatuximab) naive or sensitive and > 180 days from last dose, with a dominant clonoSEQ sequence. Investigator declares DPd or DKd before randomization. Accrual goal 80. Cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior anti-CD38 antibody (yes vs no); investigator's choice if assigned Arm A (DPd vs DKd).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm A: DPd or DKd (investigator's choice)
arms.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg/30,000 units SQ days 1, 8, 15, 22 cycles 1-2, days 1 and 15 cycles 3-6, day 1 cycle 7+. DPd: pomalidomide 4 mg PO days 1-21 plus dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg if age >= 75) days 1, 8, 15, 22. DKd: carfilzomib twice weekly (20 mg/m2 days 1-2 of cycle 1, then 56 mg/m2) with dexamethasone 20 mg days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16, or once weekly (20 mg/m2 cycle 1 day 1, then 70 mg/m2 days 8 and 15, then days 1, 8, 15) with dexamethasone 40 mg weekly.

arms.label: Arm B: DT
arms.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase on the same schedule plus teclistamab step-up dosing in cycle 1 (0.06 mg/kg day 2, 0.3 mg/kg day 4, 1.5 mg/kg day 8, then 1.5 mg/kg days 15 and 22), 1.5 mg/kg weekly in cycle 2, 3 mg/kg days 1 and 15 cycles 3-6, and 3 mg/kg day 1 cycle 7+. Hospitalization for 48 hours after each step-up dose and the first treatment dose recommended.

schema.label: MRD assessment
schema.text: Bone marrow clonoSEQ MRD after 6 cycles in patients with VGPR or better (no measurable SPEP/UPEP protein).

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Response until progression and survival for 10 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: MRD-negative rate after 6 cycles, DT vs DPd/DKd.

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG 0-2 (PS 3 allowed if due to pain).
Identifiable dominant sequence on Adaptive clonoSEQ assay.

Exactly one prior line of therapy (induction, transplant, and maintenance counted as one line). Prior autologous transplant allowed if infusion > 90 days before randomization; no prior allogeneic transplant.
Relapsed or refractory myeloma by IMWG progression criteria.
Daratumumab (or isatuximab) naive, or sensitive and > 180 days from the last dose.

Primary or secondary plasma cell leukemia and extramedullary myeloma allowed. No active or untreated CNS myeloma (prior CNS disease allowed if resolved by imaging or 2 consecutive negative CSF samples).

schema.label: Backbone (all arms)
schema.text: 6 cycles every 21 days with mandatory G-CSF. Age 60 or younger: CHOEP (cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 capped at 2 mg on day 1; etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3, or 100 mg/m2 IV day 1 then 200 mg/m2 PO days 2-3; prednisone 100 mg days 1-5). schema.text: First 12 patients (6 CHOP, 6 CHOEP): duvelisib 15 mg PO BID days 1-21 plus CHO(E)P x 6 cycles.

schema.text: Stratified by age (60 or younger vs older than 60); histologic subtype (AITL/TFH vs other) added for the expansion phase after the safety check. The first 12 patients per arm (6 CHOP, 6 CHOEP) form a safety check before expansion.

schema.text: 5 years from end of treatment or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: End-of-treatment complete remission rate by FDG PET/CT (Lugano 2014), duvelisib-CHO(E)P vs CHO(E)P and CC-486-CHO(E)P vs CHO(E)P.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed, previously untreated PTCL with CD30 expression <10% by local IHC, limited to: nodal TFH-PTCL, follicular T-cell lymphoma, PTCL-NOS, AITL, enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, or monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma. No ALCL, no CD30 10% or higher, no other subtypes (including large cell transformation of mycosis fungoides). Untreated concurrent B-cell lymphoma related to the T-cell lymphoma is allowed.
Measurable, FDG-avid disease by Lugano criteria.
No prior systemic therapy or radiation therapy for T-cell lymphoma (corticosteroids allowed).
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential).
Platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more if due to marrow involvement, except the first 12 patients per arm, who need 75,000/mm3 or more); ANC 1,000/mm3 or more.

AST and ALT 3.0 x ULN or less (expansion phase exception for liver involvement; 5.0 x ULN or less allowed with liver involvement in the lead-in and safety check); total bilirubin 2.0 x ULN or less unless Gilbert's or liver/pancreatic involvement (expansion phase); creatinine clearance 30 mL/min or more by Cockcroft-Gault.
No known HTLV-1/2 infection and no known CNS involvement.

No active HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. Seropositive but PCR-negative patients are allowed (HBV-seropositive, DNA-negative patients must take HBV antiviral therapy); cured HCV allowed; HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No active uncontrolled systemic fungal, bacterial, or viral infection (lymphoma-related EBV viremia allowed).

No concurrent malignancy requiring active therapy within the last 3 years, except skin basal or squamous cell carcinoma, carcinoma in situ of cervix or breast, or localized prostate cancer; adjuvant hormonal therapy after curative treatment allowed.
LVEF 45% or more. No significant cardiac disease within 6 months: NYHA class III-IV heart failure, unstable angina or angina needing intervention, or myocardial infarction.
No contraindication to any drug in the chemotherapy regimen, including grade 2 or higher neuropathy.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (stopped 14 days before registration) or strong CYP3A4 inducers (stopped 14 days before treatment).

schema.label: Assignment
schema.text: Assigned by the myeloMATCH screening protocol (MSRP). Newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD or FLT3-D835/I836del AML, age >= 60 or younger and unfit for intensive chemotherapy. N = 147. Cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Age (< 70 vs >= 70 years); FLT3 ITD VAF >= 33% vs ITD VAF < 33% or TKD only (MDNet values).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1:1 (induction, up to 2 cycles)
schema.text: All regimens: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 IV/SQ days 1-7 (or within a compressed window) and venetoclax ramp-up 100 mg day 1, 200 mg day 2, 400 mg days 3-28 (400 mg days 1-28 if a second cycle). Response marrow per regimen; no MLFS/CR/CRi/CRh after 2 cycles means off study.

arms.label: Regimen 1: azacitidine + venetoclax
arms.text: Induction as above; marrow days 14-28. Consolidation: azacitidine days 1-7 plus venetoclax 400 mg days 1-28.

arms.label: Regimen 2: azacitidine + venetoclax + gilteritinib
arms.text: Induction plus gilteritinib 80 mg PO days 1-28; marrow day 14. Consolidation: azacitidine days 1-5, venetoclax 400 mg days 1-7, gilteritinib 80 mg days 1-28.

arms.label: Regimen 3: azacitidine + venetoclax + gilteritinib (alternate schedule)
arms.text: Induction plus gilteritinib 80 mg PO days 8-21; marrow day 21. Consolidation: azacitidine days 1-5, venetoclax 400 mg days 1-14, gilteritinib 80 mg days 8-21.

schema.label: Consolidation
schema.text: Starts after ANC >= 500/uL and platelets >= 50,000/uL without transfusion and non-hematologic toxicity <= grade 1 or baseline; 28-day cycles for up to 2 years. Marrow with central flow MRD before cycles 3 and 5.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months for years 2-5, yearly to 10 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: MRD-negative CR rate within 4 cycles, each triplet vs azacitidine plus venetoclax.

eligibility: Age >= 60, or < 60 if better served by azanucleoside-based therapy than intensive cytarabine induction (performance status, organ dysfunction, or disease biology).
Morphologically confirmed AML, excluding APL with PML-RARA, AML with RUNX1-RUNX1T1, and AML with CBFB-MYH11.
FLT3-ITD, D835, or I836del mutation per myeloMATCH, and assigned to this substudy by myeloMATCH.
No prior AML therapy except hydroxyurea, ATRA, cytarabine-based emergency therapy, or leukapheresis to bring WBC < 25,000/mm3 before venetoclax. No prior hypomethylating agent or FLT3 inhibitor.
Labs within 14 days: total bilirubin <= 2 x ULN (<= 3 x ULN if due to disease or Gilbert's), AST/ALT <= 3.0 x ULN, creatinine clearance >= 30 mL/min (measured or CKD-EPI 2021).

ECG with normal QTcF (<= 450 ms male, <= 460 ms female) required if history of arrhythmia, atrial fibrillation, or abnormal QTcF, genetic long QT predisposition, or risk of electrolyte abnormalities including tumor lysis; prolonged QTcF goes to the Tier Advancement Pathway instead.
No ongoing need for a strong CYP3A4 inducer.
NYHA class 2 or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic agents. No uncontrolled infection.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

An International Phase 2 Study of Chemotherapy and Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors with Blinatumomab in Patients with Newly-Diagnosed Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive or ABL-Class Philadelphia Chromosome-Like B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

schema.label: Ph+ B-ALL
schema.text: Induction Part 1 days 1-14, then Induction Part 2 plus dasatinib days 15-29. BCR::ABL1 must be confirmed by a clinically validated assay before Day 15. Dasatinib is given continuously unless otherwise noted. End-of-induction MRD (timepoint 1): CNS2 or CNS3 at end of induction is off protocol therapy. Consolidation failure (section 3.3) is off protocol therapy. Then blinatumomab block 1 plus dasatinib, blinatumomab block 2 plus dasatinib, end-of-consolidation MRD (timepoint 2), interim maintenance I with high-dose methotrexate plus dasatinib, blinatumomab block 3 plus dasatinib, delayed intensification plus dasatinib, interim maintenance II with Capizzi methotrexate plus dasatinib, and maintenance plus dasatinib. M1 marrow at end of induction proceeds when counts recover; M2 or M3 marrow proceeds immediately. M2 or M3 marrow at end of induction, or end-of-induction MRD >= 5%, should have a marrow assessment after the first blinatumomab plus TKI cycle. Persistent testicular disease: 2400 cGy testicular radiotherapy in 12 fractions. CNS3 at diagnosis that clears by end of induction: cranial radiotherapy 1800 cGy in 10 fractions during maintenance if age >= 48 months at cranial radiotherapy; cranial radiotherapy is optional for CNS3 if age < 48 months at that time.

schema.label: ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL, assigned by fusion
schema.text: Enrollment is post-induction. Imatinib (PDGFRB) or dasatinib (non-PDGFRB) may start during induction once the fusion is identified, before enrollment. M1 marrow at end of induction proceeds when counts recover; M2 or M3 proceeds immediately. Consolidation failure is off protocol therapy. Each path is blinatumomab block 1 plus TKI, blinatumomab block 2 plus TKI, end-of-consolidation MRD, interim maintenance I high-dose methotrexate plus TKI, blinatumomab block 3 plus TKI, delayed intensification plus TKI, interim maintenance II Capizzi methotrexate plus TKI, and maintenance plus TKI. Same testicular radiotherapy (2400 cGy in 12 fractions if persistent) and CNS3 cranial radiotherapy rules as the Ph+ schema (1800 cGy in 10 fractions during maintenance if >= 48 months; optional if < 48 months). M2 or M3 at end of induction, or end-of-induction MRD >= 5%, should have a marrow assessment after the first blinatumomab plus TKI cycle.

arms.label: PDGFRB ABL-class fusions
arms.text: Imatinib with each block above.

arms.label: Non-PDGFRB ABL-class fusions
arms.text: Dasatinib. The schema lists non-BCR ABL1, ABL2, or CSF1R gene fusions as examples.

eligibility: Age at enrollment is > 365 days and < 18 years at AIEOP-BFM sites, > 365 days and < 22 years at COG sites, and > 365 days and < 46 years at ALLTogether sites.

Newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive or ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL, and leukemic blasts must express CD19. ABL-class fusions are rearrangements of ABL1, ABL2, CSF1R, or PDGFRB predicted to be sensitive to imatinib and/or dasatinib.

BCR::ABL1 must be documented by a clinically validated assay before study entry on Day 15 from the first vincristine dose. ABL-class rearrangements must be documented by a clinically validated assay, and the patient enrolled by Day 1 of blinatumomab block 1. Accepted methods include FISH, RT-PCR, and whole-transcriptome or panel RNA sequencing. Confirmation of the 5' fusion partner is not required.

Ph+ patients must already have started induction with vincristine, a corticosteroid, and pegaspargase or calaspargase pegol, with or without an anthracycline and/or other standard cytotoxic chemotherapy, and must not have received more than 14 days of systemic induction beginning with the first vincristine dose.
ABL-class Ph-like patients must have completed 4 or 5 weeks of multiagent Induction 1A.
Imatinib or dasatinib may have started before entry, but no more than 14 days of TKI for Ph+ B-ALL and no more than 35 days of TKI for ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL.
ECOG <= 2, or Karnofsky if > 16 years or Lansky if <= 16 years, >= 50%.
Eligibility laboratories within 7 days before enrollment. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, and serum creatinine before therapy if more than 7 days have elapsed.
Clinical studies, if applicable, within 21 days before enrollment and start of therapy. Disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 21 days.

Pediatric renal function (age 1-17 years): GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 by bedside Schwartz estimated GFR or by measured GFR (nuclear blood sampling or small-molecule clearance). Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault, using a creatinine within 28 days, multiplied by 0.85 if female, with weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight.
Direct bilirubin < 2.0 mg/dL (34.2 micromoles/L), and ALT and AST <= 10 times the upper limit of normal.

Shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, or left ventricular ejection fraction >= 50% by radionuclide angiogram or echocardiogram, and QTc < 480 msec. Repeat echocardiogram and electrocardiogram are not required if they were done at or after the initial ALL diagnosis and before enrollment.
No known chronic myeloid leukemia. No ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL that is CNS2 or CNS3 at the end of induction. No ALL developing after a previous cancer treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy.
No active uncontrolled infection or active systemic illness that requires ongoing vasopressor support or mechanical ventilation. No Down syndrome.
No prior TKI before study entry except imatinib or dasatinib. No congenital long QT syndrome, history of ventricular arrhythmias, or heart block. No Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

No significant CNS pathology that would preclude blinatumomab, including a severe neurologic disorder or autoimmune disease with CNS involvement. Seizures well controlled on stable anti-epileptic doses are eligible. Cerebrovascular ischemia or hemorrhage with residual deficits is not eligible; resolved deficits remain eligible.
HIV-infected patients are eligible if on effective antiretroviral therapy that does not interact with planned study agents and the viral load is undetectable within 6 months of treatment.

Female patients who are pregnant are not eligible (negative pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment for females of childbearing potential). Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: IMDC intermediate (1-2 factors) versus poor (3 or more). Planned immunotherapy: IO-IO versus IO-VEGF. Histology: clear cell versus non-clear cell. Non-clear cell accrual is capped at 48 patients.

schema.label: Randomize 2:1
schema.text: Randomization favors Arm 2. IO-IO is nivolumab plus ipilimumab. IO-VEGF is pembrolizumab plus axitinib, avelumab plus axitinib, nivolumab plus cabozantinib, or pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard immunotherapy alone.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: SABR to the primary tumor, 42 Gy in 3 fractions, plus standard immunotherapy.

eligibility: Pathologically proven renal cell carcinoma. Node-positive unresectable (TxN1Mx) or metastatic (TxNxM1), with history and physical and CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 45 days. IMDC intermediate or poor risk. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 outside the primary renal tumor. Not recommended for immediate cytoreductive nephrectomy, or refused it. A candidate for standard IO-IO or IO-VEGF therapy. Primary tumor 20 cm or less in anterior-to-posterior dimension on axial imaging.

Age 18 or older and Karnofsky performance status greater than 60 within 45 days. Within 45 days: hemoglobin greater than 8 g/dL (transfusion allowed), platelets greater than 50,000/mm3, ANC greater than 1,500/mm3, and creatinine clearance greater than 30 mL/min. For the stated African American calculation exception, CKD-EPI GFR at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 is adequate.
Hepatic function within 45 days: total bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN (under 3.0 mg/dL with Gilbert syndrome), and AST and ALT under 3 x ULN, or under 5 x ULN with liver metastases.

Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Testing is not required. Chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must be treated and cured, or current treatment must have an undetectable viral load.

Agree to highly effective contraception, including men with vasectomies who have sex with a woman of childbearing potential. Informed consent, and US authorization to release health information, before entry.

Ineligible if all metastatic disease is planned for definitive surgery, ablative radiation, or other intervention that would leave no extra-renal measurable disease. Palliative radiation sites are not used for response. Untreated or unstable brain metastases or cranial epidural disease are excluded. Treated brain metastases are eligible when no steroids are required and there is no progression or hemorrhage for at least 4 weeks, documented by MRI or CT or judged stable by the investigator.

No prior radiotherapy to the kidney that would overlap treatment of the primary. No systemic therapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma started more than 90 days before registration. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed if completed more than 3 years before registration.

No severe active comorbidity as listed in section 3.2.5, including autoimmune disease on daily corticosteroids above 10 mg prednisone equivalent or other daily immunosuppression, severe hypersensitivity to chimeric or humanized antibodies, active tuberculosis, uncontrolled hypertension above 190 systolic or 110 diastolic, major surgery with hospital admission within 28 days, a serious non-healing wound, ulcer, or fracture within 45 days, an arterial thrombotic event within 180 days, NYHA class 3-4 symptoms, Child-Pugh B or C, untreated pulmonary embolism or DVT within 180 days, unstable arrhythmia within 180 days, or fistula, perforation, abscess, obstruction, inflammatory bowel disease, or malabsorption in the windows in section 3.2.5. Treated asymptomatic pulmonary embolism, or treated asymptomatic DVT more than 30 days earlier, is allowed. Inhaled steroids and adrenal replacement above 10 mg prednisone equivalent are allowed when autoimmune disease is not active.
Pregnancy, and people unwilling to stop nursing, are excluded. A woman of childbearing potential needs a negative pregnancy test within 45 days before registration.

studies.title: Pilot Study of CBX-12 Pharmacodynamics in Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors
A Phase II/ III Study of Peri-Operative Nivolumab and Ipilimumab in Patients with Locoregional Esophageal and Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Randomize, then esophagectomy. The schema prints N=278 and does not print a randomization ratio. Treatment starts within 10 working days after registration. Day 1 of chemotherapy begins on the first day of radiation, plus or minus 2 days. Radiation is 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy to the PTV. A PTV dose from 41.4 Gy to 50.4 Gy is allowed. Photons, 3D-CRT or IMRT, and protons are allowed.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 2 IV once weekly and paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 IV once weekly during weeks 1-5, plus radiation. At most 5 doses of carboplatin and paclitaxel. A missed week may be made up in week 6 if radiation is still being given.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: The same weekly carboplatin, paclitaxel, and radiation, plus nivolumab 240 mg IV on days 1 and 15 of radiation.

schema.label: Step 2
schema.text: After surgery, randomize within 12 weeks of esophagectomy. One cycle is 4 weeks. Stratify by lymph node status (positive versus negative), pathologic complete response (yes versus no), and Step 1 arm (Arm A versus Arm B). Adjuvant therapy starts within one week of randomization. No randomization ratio is printed.

arms.label: Arm C
arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV on day 1 every 4 weeks for 13 cycles, a 12 month course. Patients already receiving adjuvant nivolumab at the time of the amendment may continue 240 mg every 2 weeks until they change to every 4 weeks.

arms.label: Arm D
arms.text: The same nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks for 13 cycles, plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks for 4 doses, given on cycle 1 day 1, cycle 2 day 15, cycle 4 day 1, and cycle 5 day 15.

eligibility: Step 1: Age 18 or older with histologically confirmed T1N1-3M0 or T2-3N0-2M0 esophageal or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (Siewert I or II), ECOG performance status 0-1, and judged a surgical candidate for esophagectomy.

Within 14 days before Step 1 randomization: ANC at least 1,500/mcL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin at or under the institutional ULN, AST and ALT at or under 2.5 x ULN, serum creatinine at or under 1.5 x ULN, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, and leukocytes at least 3,000/mm3.
No prior chemotherapy or radiation for this malignancy. No prior immunotherapy for this malignancy or for any past malignancy. No contraindication to carboplatin, paclitaxel, or radiation.

Active autoimmune disease, or a history that might recur and affect vital organ function or require systemic immunosuppression, is excluded, including immune neurologic disease, multiple sclerosis, demyelinating neuropathy, Guillain-Barre syndrome, myasthenia gravis, SLE, connective tissue disease, scleroderma, inflammatory bowel disease, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hepatitis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and phospholipid syndrome.

Vitiligo, type I diabetes, residual hypothyroidism requiring only hormone replacement, psoriasis not requiring systemic treatment, and conditions not expected to recur without an external trigger are allowed. Rheumatoid arthritis and other arthropathies, Sjogren syndrome, and psoriasis controlled with topical medication, and positive serologies without target-organ involvement that needs systemic treatment, may be eligible.

No previous or concurrent malignancy, except non-melanoma skin cancer, in situ cervical cancer, superficial bladder cancer, or breast cancer in situ, or a prior malignancy completely removed with continuous freedom from disease for more than 5 years.

No systemic corticosteroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent, or other immunosuppressive medication, within 14 days of study drug. Inhaled or topical steroids and adrenal replacement at or under 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent are allowed if autoimmune disease is not active.

Adequate cardiac function is required, including EKG and echocardiogram for heart failure history, cardiovascular risk, or cardiotoxic-drug exposure. Uncontrolled heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, or myositis requires cardiac clearance. No positive hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C RNA. Known HIV or AIDS requires an undetectable viral load on a stable antiviral regimen.

No other investigational agents. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would limit compliance is excluded. Not pregnant or breast-feeding. A person of childbearing potential needs a pregnancy test within 2 weeks before randomization, and within 24 hours before nivolumab if assigned to Arm B.
Step 2: Registration no more than 12 weeks after esophagectomy, postoperative ECOG 0-2, no evidence of disease on post-surgical CT, and an R0 resection.

Within 14 days before Step 2 randomization: ANC at least 1,500/mcL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin at or under ULN, AST and ALT at or under 2.5 x ULN, and serum creatinine at or under 1.5 x ULN.

No active, known, or suspected autoimmune disease and no condition requiring steroids or other immunosuppression, with the same allowed exceptions as Step 1. No systemic corticosteroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent, or other immunosuppressive medication, within 14 days of study drug. Section 3.2.6 prints that inhaled or topical steroids and adrenal replacement doses above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent are permitted if autoimmune disease is not active.

No other investigational agents at Step 2. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would limit compliance is excluded. Not pregnant or breast-feeding. A person of childbearing potential needs a pregnancy test within 2 weeks before randomization and within 24 hours before nivolumab, and within 72 hours before each ipilimumab dose on Arm D.

studies.title: Quadruplet Induction Followed by Teclistamab Consolidation and Doublet Maintenance in Patients with Primary Plasma Cell Leukemia: The QUANTUM Trial

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Up to one cycle of non-protocol treatment allowed before enrollment. Protocol treatment starts within 21 days of registration. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Induction (cycles 1-4)
schema.text: D-KRd: daratumumab/hyaluronidase-fihj 1800 mg SC days 1, 8, 15, 22 (cycles 1-2) then days 1 and 15 (cycles 3-4); carfilzomib 20 mg/m2 C1D1 then 56 mg/m2 weekly; lenalidomide 25 mg days 1-21; dexamethasone 40 mg weekly on carfilzomib days.

schema.label: Stem cell collection and autoHSCT
schema.text: Collection within 60 days after induction (G-CSF with or without plerixafor; chemo-mobilization allowed), then melphalan 200 mg/m2 autologous transplant per institutional standard.

schema.label: Step 2: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: After autoHSCT. Stratified by one cycle of treatment before study entry (yes vs no) and t(11;14) (yes vs no). Consolidation starts no later than 120 days post-transplant.

arms.label: Arm 1: D-KRd consolidation (cycles 5-12)
arms.text: Daratumumab 1800 mg SC days 1 and 15 then monthly (cycles 7-12); carfilzomib 20 mg/m2 C5D1 then 56 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15; lenalidomide days 1-21 at the last tolerated induction dose; dexamethasone 40 mg weekly.

arms.label: Arm 2: Teclistamab consolidation (cycles 5-12)
arms.text: Step-up 0.06 mg/kg C5D1 and 0.3 mg/kg C5D3, then 1.5 mg/kg weekly from C5D7 (+/- 2) through cycle 6; 3.0 mg/kg every 2 weeks cycles 7-10; 3.0 mg/kg every 4 weeks cycles 11-12.

schema.label: Maintenance (cycles 13-36)
schema.text: KR for 2 years, starting within 60 days after consolidation: carfilzomib 56 mg/m2 days 1 and 15 (Arm 2 starts at 20 mg/m2 on C13D1) and lenalidomide 10 mg days 1-21. Further maintenance at physician discretion.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival from randomization, teclistamab vs D-KRd consolidation. Follow-up 5 years or until death.

eligibility: Primary plasma cell leukemia by IMWG criteria (5% or more circulating plasma cells at initial diagnosis).
Measurable disease at diagnosis: serum M-protein 0.5 g/dL or more, urine M-protein 200 mg/24 h or more, or serum FLC 100 mg/L or more with abnormal ratio.
Age 18-80; ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.
No more than 1 cycle of prior induction treatment.

No severe allergic reaction (including erythema nodosum) to lenalidomide or another IMiD; no clinically significant cardiopulmonary disease from prior proteasome inhibitor therapy; no known allergy or intolerance to daratumumab/hyaluronidase, carfilzomib, lenalidomide, or dexamethasone.
No POEMS syndrome, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, or symptomatic amyloidosis (skin, lymph node, or incidental marrow amyloid allowed).
Clinically significant effects of prior surgery, radiotherapy, or other anticancer therapy resolved or stable.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load if on treatment.

No cardiac risk factors: uncontrolled arrhythmia or Mobitz II/third-degree AV block; MI, acute coronary syndrome, angioplasty, stenting, or bypass within 2 months; NYHA class III-IV heart failure; uncontrolled hypertension (persistent grade 3 or higher despite treatment); congenital long QT or QTcF >480 msec; LVEF <40%.
No grade 3 or higher neuropathy, and no grade 2 neuropathy with pain.
No major surgery within 2 weeks before registration (or unrecovered); able to swallow oral agents; no contraindication to required concomitant medications, including antivirals or anticoagulation.
ANC 1,000/mm3 or more (500/mm3 or more if due to underlying disease); bilirubin 2 x ULN or less; AST/ALT 3 x ULN or less; CrCl 30 mL/min or more by MDRD.

amendments.text: COG Amendment 6 (ANZUP protocol version 5.2), the current version. Moves the database from InForm to Flexetrials and REDCap. Earlier, COG Amendment 4 expanded accrual into Part 2 after Part 1 accrual and added biospecimen collection at COG/NCTN sites.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Age 11-50 years, intermediate- or poor-risk metastatic GCT (testis, ovary, retroperitoneum, or mediastinum) needing first-line chemotherapy. COG/NCTN arm of ANZUP 1302 (P3BEP); randomization in Flexetrials/REDCap within 10 days of starting chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: ECOG PS 0-1 vs 2-3; IGCCC intermediate vs poor; mediastinal vs other primary; brain metastases present vs absent; induction chemotherapy present vs absent; age, sex, site.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: N = 500. Total planned chemotherapy 12 weeks in both arms. Bleomycin 30 units per dose if age ≥ 16, 15 units/m2 (max 30 units) if < 16.

arms.label: Arm A: standard BEP
arms.text: 4 x 21-day cycles: cisplatin 20 mg/m2 and etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-5, bleomycin weekly x 3 per cycle, pegylated G-CSF or G-CSF.

arms.label: Arm B: accelerated BEP
arms.text: 4 x 14-day cycles: cisplatin 20 mg/m2 and etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-5, bleomycin weekly x 2 per cycle, pegylated G-CSF or G-CSF, then 4 more weekly bleomycin doses.

schema.label: Bleomycin shortfall
schema.text: If inadequate bleomycin is delivered and disease is poor risk, switch to 3-weekly VIP.

schema.label: After chemotherapy

eligibility: COG/NCTN sites use the Appendix 7 criteria, which differ from the main ANZUP protocol.

Histologically or cytologically confirmed GCT (non-seminoma or seminoma), or AFP ≥ 1000 ng/mL and/or HCG ≥ 5000 IU/L without histology when metastatic pattern, high burden, and urgency fit GCT.
Primary in testis, ovary, retroperitoneum, or mediastinum; metastatic disease or non-testicular primary.

Intermediate or poor risk by modified IGCCC: non-seminoma intermediate (testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP 1000-10,000 ng/mL, HCG 5000-50,000 IU/L, or LDH 3-10 x ULN); non-seminoma poor (mediastinal primary, non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP > 10,000, HCG > 50,000, or LDH > 10 x ULN); seminoma with non-pulmonary visceral mets and normal AFP; or ovarian MGCT FIGO/COG stage IV. ANC ≥ 1.0 x 10^9/L and platelets ≥ 100 x 10^9/L.
Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 2.0 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST/ALT ≤ 2.5 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).
Age ≥ 18: CrCl ≥ 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, or measured GFR if borderline). Age < 18: CrCl or GFR > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum.
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16). Treatment able to start within 14 days of OPEN enrollment.
No prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, except pure seminoma relapsing after adjuvant radiotherapy or 1-2 doses of single-agent carboplatin.
No other primary malignancy except treated non-melanoma skin cancer, GCT, or a cancer treated at least 5 years ago without recurrence.
No cardiac disease preventing cisplatin hydration, no respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin, no grade ≥ 2 neuropathy, and no clinically significant hearing loss or tinnitus.
No severe concurrent illness or infection. No known allergy to study drugs.
Not pregnant; negative pregnancy test within 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

amendments.text: Initial protocol.
Amendment 1, the latest date in the document history. The opening pages do not summarize what changed.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Resectable stage III or IV cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Immunosuppressed (yes vs no, defined in section 3.2). Advanced nodal disease (N3 or in-transit metastases vs other). Disease site (head and neck vs non-head and neck or eyelid).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Schema dated 12-SEP-2025.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard of care surgery, then adjuvant radiation as indicated.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Neoadjuvant cemiplimab (REGN2810) every 3 weeks for 4 doses, then response-adapted oncologic surgery, then adjuvant radiation as indicated, then adjuvant cemiplimab every 6 weeks for 4 doses. Adjuvant cemiplimab is given after adjuvant radiation when radiation is indicated.

schema.label: Pathologic complete response
schema.text: Patients with a pathologic complete response will not receive adjuvant radiation or adjuvant cemiplimab. Full cemiplimab dosing is in section 5.1 and is not printed on the schema page.

eligibility: Pathologically proven invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, or a regional lymph node or in-transit metastasis of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

WHO subtypes are eligible when the predominant histology is cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid differentiation, acantholytic squamous cell carcinoma, clear cell squamous cell carcinoma, and lymphoepithelial carcinoma. Keratoacanthoma and verrucous subtypes are not eligible.

Regional metastasis without a primary tumor requires a clinical history of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma draining to the involved nodes or in-transit metastases. If that history is ambiguous, tumor genomic sequencing suggesting a cutaneous primary is acceptable (tumor mutation burden at least 10 mutations/Mb, and/or more than 50 percent UV-related mutations, and/or signature 7). Sequencing is not required.

Previously untreated or recurrent disease. Clinical AJCC 8th edition stage III or IV for head and neck sites, or UICC stage III or IV for eyelid and non-head and neck sites. The primary site is head and neck skin, other cutaneous sites, or eyelid skin.
Mucosal squamous cell carcinoma is excluded (vermillion lip, nasal, oral, sinonasal, conjunctival, anogenital).

The tumor must be resectable with curative intent. T4b disease with bony skull base invasion and/or skull base foramen involvement is not eligible. T4b eyelid tumors staged by UICC that do not involve the brain are eligible.
At least one lesion measurable by RECIST 1.1. No definitive clinical or radiologic distant metastatic disease, and no visceral or distant nodal disease.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2.

Not pregnant and not nursing. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for persons of childbearing potential. Participants of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception during therapy and for at least 4 months after study therapy.

Required labs: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,000 cells/mm3, platelets at least 75,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention to reach that hemoglobin is allowed).

Creatinine clearance greater than 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault. Total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal (at or below 3 times that limit if Gilbert syndrome is documented). AST and ALT at or below 3 times the institutional upper limit of normal.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer, including immunotherapy currently given for a separate malignancy. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would make cumulative organ-at-risk doses exceed protocol limits.
No myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 6 months. New York Heart Association class IIb or better is required. Class III or IV is not eligible.
No active infection requiring systemic antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals. No allogeneic or autologous stem cell transplant. No solid organ transplant other than a corneal transplant.

No active, known, or suspected autoimmune disease, defined as a need for more than 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent, a need for disease-modifying agents, or significant autoimmune disease treated with systemic immunosuppression within 5 years before registration.

A brief steroid course, type 1 diabetes, endocrinopathies requiring only hormone replacement (including hypothyroidism from autoimmune thyroiditis), and skin disorders such as vitiligo, psoriasis, or alopecia that do not need systemic treatment are allowed. Physiologic replacement at or below 10 mg prednisone daily, and inhaled or topical steroids, are allowed when not given for immunosuppressive intent.
HIV with an undetectable viral load within 6 months on effective antiretroviral therapy is eligible. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia with no anti-CLL therapy within 6 months is eligible.

No history of interstitial lung disease. No active noninfectious pneumonitis requiring immune-suppressive therapy. No active tuberculosis. No live vaccines within 28 days before registration. No history of allergic reaction to the study agent or to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition, including excipients.

On-study guidance: chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when its natural history or treatment would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

amendments.text: Protocol version date on the file. CTSU posted this version on September 8, 2026. The PDF has no document history and no section-level summary of what changed.

schema.label: Muscle-invasive disease
schema.text: Histologic cT2-T4aN0 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

schema.label: Neoadjuvant therapy
schema.text: Physician's choice, limited to the FDA-approved regimens in the eligibility criteria.

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: cT0 or cT1 on a repeat TURBT with systematic biopsies. That TURBT is within 90 days before registration.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Within 90 days after the last neoadjuvant dose.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Bladder radiotherapy plus pembrolizumab for 1 year. Central radiation-plan approval is required before treatment starts. Radiotherapy is whole bladder only, 55 Gy in 20 fractions of 2.75 Gy, with no pelvic nodes and no tumor boost.

schema.label: On-study assessment
schema.text: Cystoscopy, cytology, and imaging.

schema.label: Endpoint
schema.text: 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. Follow-up continues for 5 years after registration.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T4aN0M0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts. Staging CT, MRI, or PET of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 60 days before neoadjuvant therapy.

After neoadjuvant therapy, a repeat TURBT must show cT0 or cT1. It biopsies the prior disease and systematic sites (left and right lateral walls, dome, posterior wall, and trigone), with at least 4 of 5 systematic biopsies. The TURBT is within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose and within 90 days before registration.

No cT2 or higher, N1-3, or M1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis after neoadjuvant therapy needs PET-CT within 70 days before registration. A PET-positive node is ineligible unless biopsy shows no tumor.

At least 3 and no more than 6 cycles of FDA-approved neoadjuvant therapy: cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, with or without a PD-1/L1 inhibitor; dose-dense or accelerated MVAC; or enfortumab vedotin with a PD-1/L1 inhibitor.
No small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid histology. Mixed histology is allowed when more than half of the tumor is urothelial carcinoma. No prior pelvic radiotherapy.
The primary objective is written for clinically T0 or T1 disease without multifocal CIS. That CIS phrase is not an eligibility criterion.

schema.text: Primary tumor resection (transoral, aiming for 5 mm margins) and neck surgery in the same operation, within 30 days after central PET/CT review.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy with planar and mandatory SPECT/CT lymphatic mapping. Positive SLN leads to completion neck dissection (at least levels I-III) within 6 weeks, ideally 4.

arms.label: Arm 2 (control)
arms.text: Elective neck dissection, at least levels I-III (bilateral for lesions within 1 cm of midline).

schema.text: Observation if no adverse features. Adjuvant IMRT alone for PNI, LVI, pT3/T4, close margins (< 5 mm), or pN1+ (sites may omit RT for pN1 as the only risk factor). Adjuvant chemoradiation with concurrent cisplatin (every 3 weeks or weekly) for positive margins or extranodal extension. RT covers both primary site and at-risk neck: 60 Gy in 30 fractions (PTV_6000), 56 Gy in 30 (PTV_5600), 66 Gy in 30 (PTV_6600) when used. IMRT and IGRT mandatory, protons not allowed; adjuvant treatment starts within 42 days after surgery.

schema.label: Step 1: Proband registration
schema.text: Newly diagnosed stage I-IV colorectal adenocarcinoma. Proband watches a pre-test genetic counseling video and receives upfront germline testing (Invitae 70-gene NGS panel), with results returned by genetic counselor (positive or VUS) or letter (negative). VUS or negative results end the intervention.

schema.label: Step 2: Randomization of PGV-positive probands
schema.text: Probands with a pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline variant are randomized 1:1 within 90 days of registration. FDRs are contacted with a recruitment script, consented with incomplete disclosure, and registered. Stratified by Lynch syndrome (yes vs no), number of eligible FDRs (2-4 vs 5-7 vs ≥ 8), and variant penetrance (high vs moderate/low); Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

arms.label: Arm A: Proband-mediated (usual care)
arms.text: Proband informs relatives after standard post-test counseling; FDRs receive no intervention beyond study surveys and a debrief information sheet.

arms.label: Arm B: Provider-mediated
arms.text: Site coordinator telephones FDRs directly within 1 month of randomization (up to 4 more attempts over 8 weeks), explains their risk, and gives resources for Invitae testing and counseling. Family variant testing is free within 90 days of the proband's result.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: FDR questionnaires (MICRA and cascade testing survey) at 6 and 12 months; probands followed for survival up to 3 years.

schema.label: Co-primary endpoints
schema.text: Proportion of FDRs who undergo germline testing at 6 months, provider- vs proband-mediated, separately for Lynch syndrome and non-Lynch pathogenic variants.

Proband, Step 1: no germline testing within the 2 years before enrollment and no known hereditary colon cancer syndrome.

Proband, Step 1: speaks and reads English or Spanish; no dementia, cognitive impairment, or psychiatric/developmental disorder that significantly impairs judgment.
Proband, Step 2: positive for a pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline variant in a cancer susceptibility gene.
FDR: age ≥ 18 years, no prior germline testing or known hereditary colon cancer syndrome, resides in the U.S., speaks and reads English or Spanish.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with stable disease or partial response after 4 to 6 cycles of etoposide and platinum plus atezolizumab. For induction, one cycle of etoposide and platinum without atezolizumab is allowed if the patient cannot receive concurrent atezolizumab for every induction cycle.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Number of sites receiving radiation (1 to 3 fields vs more than 3). Partial response vs stable disease. ECOG performance status 0 or 1 vs 2. Brain metastases (no vs yes).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Schema dated 09-NOV-2022, carried in the March 13, 2025 protocol. Section 5 confirms the radiation doses and the atezolizumab dose.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Atezolizumab maintenance. Section 5: atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Standard radiation, daily, to up to 5 sites, plus atezolizumab maintenance. Thoracic or liver radiation: 45 Gy or 30 Gy. Extra-thoracic radiation: 30 Gy or 20 Gy. Section 5 confirms 45 Gy in 15 fractions (3 Gy, lung or liver only, preferred for lung), 30 Gy in 10 fractions (3 Gy, any site), and 20 Gy in 5 fractions (4 Gy, extra-thoracic metastatic sites only). Radiation starts during the first 5 weeks of maintenance atezolizumab, which is the same 1200 mg every 21 days schedule as Arm 1.

schema.label: Prophylactic cranial irradiation
schema.text: PCI is optional. The schema says co-enrollment on SWOG S1827 (MAVERICK) or NRG-CC003 should be strongly considered. Section 5: PCI may be given during induction chemotherapy before randomization. If PCI is given on study, use 25 Gy in 10 fractions. Atezolizumab does not need to be delayed during PCI. Protocol treatment begins within 21 days after registration.

eligibility: Cytologic, histologic, or pathologic confirmation of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer at a primary or metastatic site.

Partial response or stable disease after 4 to 6 cycles of etoposide and platinum plus atezolizumab, documented on restaging PET/CT, diagnostic CT, or MRI at the treating physician's option. Atezolizumab should continue through randomization.

At least 3 cycles must include etoposide, platinum, and atezolizumab. One induction cycle of etoposide and platinum without concurrent atezolizumab is allowed. Randomize within 9 weeks of the last etoposide and platinum dose if PCI is not given, or within 6 weeks after PCI is completed.
Measurable disease per RECIST, 3 or fewer observable liver metastases, and no progressive disease per RECIST at enrollment.
A pleural effusion is allowed if thoracentesis is cytologically negative, or if the fluid volume is too small to sample and the effusion does not show increased metabolic activity on CT/PET.

History and physical examination within 14 days before registration. Imaging within 42 days before registration: MRI or CT of the brain with contrast, and CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis or whole-body PET/CT any time after the fourth cycle of chemotherapy and before registration.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2 within 14 days before registration.

Labs within 14 days: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,000 cells/mm3, platelets at least 75,000 cells/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, and total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal.

AST and ALT at or below 3 times the upper limit of normal, or at or below 5 times that limit if the liver is involved. Alkaline phosphatase at or below 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, or at or below 5 times that limit with documented liver involvement or bone metastases. Creatinine clearance at least 40 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault.
Upfront radiation to a symptomatic metastatic site is allowed for pain or impending fracture.

Brain metastases are eligible after whole-brain radiation given before enrollment, at any time during induction systemic therapy, with hippocampal sparing or 3D conformal technique. After that radiotherapy the patient must be neurologically stable (for example, not having uncontrolled seizures) and must not need steroids above 10 mg of prednisone daily.

Negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for women of childbearing potential. Women of childbearing potential and men must use adequate contraception before entry, during study treatment, and for 5 months (150 days) after the last dose of study agent. Women who are breastfeeding and unwilling to discontinue are not eligible.

HIV-positive patients are eligible on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months and a stable HAART regimen, and with no concurrent antibiotics or antifungal agents for prevention of opportunistic infections.
Study-specific informed consent, or consent by a legally authorized representative, is required before study entry.
Not eligible: more than 3 liver metastases, disease invading the heart, or more than 10 metastatic sites detectable after induction systemic therapy. Each visible bone metastasis counts as one site.

No concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of atezolizumab or radiation. No prior thoracic radiotherapy that would overlap fields, unless the overlap meets acceptable normal-tissue dose constraints.

No active autoimmune disease, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, antiphospholipid thrombosis, Wegener granulomatosis, Sjogren syndrome, Guillain-Barre syndrome, multiple sclerosis, vasculitis, or glomerulonephritis. Inactive autoimmune disease for more than 3 years, without methotrexate or steroids above 10 mg prednisone daily equivalent, is eligible. Autoimmune hypothyroidism on stable thyroid replacement, and controlled type 1 diabetes on stable insulin, are eligible. Eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo is excluded only when there is active disease with acute exacerbation and immunosuppressive medication within 12 months before enrollment.

No active tuberculosis. No known clinically significant liver disease, including active viral, alcoholic, or other hepatitis, cirrhosis, fatty liver, or inherited liver disease. Resolved hepatitis B (negative HBsAg and positive anti-HBc) is eligible. Hepatitis C antibody is eligible only if HCV RNA PCR is negative.

No known immunosuppressive disease, for example prior bone marrow transplant or chronic lymphocytic leukemia. No COPD requiring chronic oral steroid therapy above 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent at registration. Inhaled corticosteroids are not exclusionary.

No unstable angina or congestive heart failure requiring hospitalization within 3 months. No myocardial infarction within 6 months. No clinically significant interstitial lung disease. No history of allogeneic organ transplant. No immunotherapy-induced pneumonitis.

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG 0-2 (PS 3 allowed if due to pain).
Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma by IMWG criteria, not more than one prior cycle of treatment.

Step 1: Adaptive clonality ID result with dominant sequence identified (bone marrow aspirate or archival smears/clot section available).

Measurable or evaluable disease within 28 days: serum M-protein >= 1 g/dL, urine M-protein >= 200 mg/24 hours, involved FLC >= 10 mg/dL with abnormal kappa/lambda ratio (< 0.26 or > 1.65), or marrow plasmacytosis >= 30%. Bone marrow within 28 days if disease only in marrow, otherwise within 90 days.
Step 1 labs within 14 days: CrCl > 30 mL/min, ANC >= 1000/mm3, untransfused platelets >= 75,000/mm3, Hgb >= 8.0 g/dL, total bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN.

Prior therapy limited to one cycle (28 days or less) of chemotherapy and no more than 160 mg dexamethasone (or equivalent). Prior radiation to symptomatic lesions allowed if no residual toxicity, counts adequate, and completed at least 14 days before Step 1. Prior SMM treatment allowed except lenalidomide plus an anti-CD38 antibody.
No peripheral neuropathy grade >= 2, or grade 1 with pain.

Prior DVT/PE allowed with anticoagulant prophylaxis. No allergy or intolerance to corticosteroids, monoclonal antibodies, or human proteins. Must enroll in the Revlimid REMS program.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Three entry routes: pre-screening before progression on current therapy (tissue only), screening at progression (tissue or prior NGS results), or treatment-naive NSCLC with a designated targetable alteration (prior NGS results only, when such sub-studies are open).

schema.label: Biomarker profiling
schema.text: Tissue sent to Foundation Medicine within 5 days of registration for broad CLIA NGS profiling, or upload of a previously completed approved NGS report via the Genomic Alterations Form.

schema.label: Sub-study assignment
schema.text: Biomarker-matched sub-study if a qualifying alteration is found (lowest prevalence or randomized assignment if several match); otherwise a non-match sub-study if one is accruing. Assignment within about 16 days of tissue submission, within 1 day for prior test results; pre-screened patients receive assignment after the Notice of Progression is submitted.

schema.label: Sub-study registration
schema.text: Separate registration to the assigned sub-study, which has its own eligibility and treatment. After progression on a sub-study, a new assignment may be requested.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until sub-study registration, death, or 3 years after LUNGMAP registration; after sub-study registration, until death or 3 years.

schema.label: Primary objective
schema.text: Screening protocol: determine eligibility for the biomarker-driven and non-match Lung-MAP sub-studies.

eligibility: Pathologically or cytologically proven NSCLC; mixed NSCLC histologies allowed, but no known small cell component.
Stage IV, or recurrent or progressive NSCLC without a curative treatment option (staging per AJCC 7th edition or later).
Age ≥ 18; Zubrod/ECOG performance status 0-2 documented within 28 days before registration.

Pre-screening: tissue available for on-study profiling; currently on, or previously received, first-line standard therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease and not yet progressed on the current or most recent line. Patients using prior biomarker results cannot be pre-screened. Patients on osimertinib aiming for S1900G must not be pre-screened.

Screening at progression: at least one prior line of standard systemic therapy for stage I-IV NSCLC with progression during or after the most recent line. If no prior therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease, progression must have occurred ≤ 180 days after the last dose of stage I-III systemic therapy; if > 180 days, standard therapy for advanced disease and progression on it are required first.

Screening at progression biomarker route: tissue for on-study profiling, an approved prior NGS report, or a non-listed NGS report (or specific biomarker documentation) accepted by e-mail from LUNGMAPNGS@swog.org. For EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified disease screening for S1900G, tissue must be obtained after progression on osimertinib.

Treatment-naive route: no prior systemic therapy for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC and documentation (approved or e-mail-accepted NGS report) of a biomarker for a sub-study open to treatment-naive patients. Do not submit tissue for this route.

Tissue for on-study testing: FFPE block, or 12 unstained slides plus an H&E (or 13 unstained slides) at 4-5 microns, with ≥ 20% tumor cells and ≥ 0.2 mm3 tumor volume; no decalcified bone biopsies (cell blocks of pleural fluid acceptable). Consent to Foundation Medicine testing and banking of leftover tissue.

Prior test reports: full report available, tissue or blood specified, original report dated on or after September 1, 2019, from a CLIA/CAP/ISO-certified lab (non-listed tests need gene list and e-mail approval). A blood-only NGS report must show at least one alteration on the Genomic Alterations Form, otherwise tissue testing is required.

amendments.text: Initial protocol. The document history lists no later amendment.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Previously untreated, unresected, locoregionally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity, in patients with a contraindication to cisplatin. The cisplatin contraindication is an eligibility rule in section 3.2.5. The schema box itself names the two concurrent regimens.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: p16 status: p16-positive oropharynx vs p16-negative oropharynx or non-oropharynx. AJCC 9th edition stage: for p16-positive oropharynx, T1-2 and N2 or T3 and N0-2 (stage II) vs T4 or N3 (stage III). For p16-negative oropharynx or non-oropharynx, T1-3 and N0-2b vs T4a-b or N2c-3. ECOG and comorbidities: performance status 0 and modified Charlson comorbidity index 0 vs performance status 1 to 2 or modified Charlson index greater than 0.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Both arms are definitive radiation with concurrent systemic therapy. Section 5, not the schema box, prints the doses below.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Radiation plus concurrent cetuximab. Section 5: cetuximab 400 mg/m2 intravenously within 7 days before day 1 of radiation, then intensity-modulated radiation, 70 Gy in 35 fractions, 5 fractions per week, with cetuximab 250 mg/m2 intravenously weekly during radiation for 7 weekly cycles.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Radiation plus concurrent carboplatin and paclitaxel. Section 5: intensity-modulated radiation, 70 Gy in 35 fractions, 5 fractions per week, with carboplatin AUC 2 plus paclitaxel 40 mg/m2 intravenously weekly for 7 cycles beginning on day 1 of radiation.

schema.label: Radiation technique
schema.text: Section 5.2: intensity-modulated radiation and image guidance are mandatory. Intensity-modulated proton therapy is allowed. Passive scattered proton therapy is not allowed. Protocol treatment must begin within 14 days after registration. The prescription in section 5.2 is 7000 cGy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks.

eligibility: Pathologically confirmed, previously untreated, unresected squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity.
Local p16 status is required for all oropharynx patients before registration. Local p16 status is recommended, not required, for non-oropharynx patients.
Non-oropharynx and p16-negative oropharynx must be AJCC 9th edition stage III, IVA, or IVB: T3 N0 or T1-3 N1 M0 (III); T1-3 N2 or T4a N0-N2 M0 (IVA); T4b N0-N2 or T1-4b N3 M0 (IVB).
p16-positive oropharynx must be AJCC 9th edition stage II or III: T3 N0-2 or T1-2 N2 M0 (II); T4 N0-3 or T1-3 N3 M0 (III).

Before registration: head and neck imaging with contrast neck CT or MRI unless contrast is contraindicated, or PET/CT that includes diagnostic-quality contrast CT of the neck unless contrast is contraindicated. Chest imaging with contrast chest CT unless contraindicated, or PET/CT.
Age 18 or older. Before registration, complete the online tool at www.nrgoncology.org and record the modified Charlson comorbidity index, HNCIG omega score, and G-8 score.

A contraindication to cisplatin is required, defined as at least one of the following: creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min by the Cockroft-Gault formula, pre-existing grade 2 or higher sensory or motor neuropathy, or hearing loss (an existing need for a hearing aid, or at least a 25 decibel shift over 2 contiguous frequencies on a pretreatment hearing test as clinically indicated).

Cisplatin ineligibility may instead be age 70 or older with an HNCIG omega score below 0.80. Or age under 70 with all of the following: HNCIG omega score below 0.80, modified Charlson comorbidity index at least 1, and G-8 score 14 or lower.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2. Not pregnant and not nursing.

Participants must be able to safely receive the radiation and drug regimens per the current FDA-approved package inserts, the treating investigator's discretion, and institutional guidelines. Section 3 does not list separate absolute neutrophil count, platelet, hemoglobin, or bilirubin floors.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer. Prior systemic therapy for a different cancer is allowed. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap radiation fields. No prior surgery for the study cancer.

On-study guidance: HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. Persistent grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormalities must be reversible with replacement. Highly effective contraception is required during therapy and for 6 months after.

schema.text: Osteosarcoma with resectable oligometastatic lung disease (4 or fewer nodules per lung), newly diagnosed or at first pulmonary recurrence. Chest CT goes to rapid central imaging review within 5 days of enrollment to confirm eligibility and stratum.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Six groups: newly diagnosed poor risk vs average risk (poor risk: 2 or more metastases, bilateral lung metastases, or 10% or more viable tumor in the resected primary); recurrent poor risk vs average risk (poor risk: recurrence less than 18 months from diagnosis, 2 or more lesions, or bilateral), each split by whether post-thoracic-surgery chemotherapy is intended.

schema.text: Surgical approach to pulmonary metastasectomy

arms.label: Open surgery
arms.text: Thoracotomy or sternotomy. Bilateral disease: sternotomy or bilateral thoracotomy, same day or staged with the second side within 8 weeks.

arms.label: Thoracoscopy
arms.text: Thoracoscopic (minimally invasive) resection of all pulmonary nodules.

schema.label: Systemic therapy
schema.text: Not protocol-directed. Newly diagnosed patients receive standard osteosarcoma chemotherapy (for example cisplatin-doxorubicin or ifosfamide-based) and standard primary local control; recurrent patients receive systemic therapy per the treating oncologist. Multitargeted TKIs must be held before surgery per label or institutional guidance.

schema.label: Post-operative assessment

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Thoracic event-free survival (intrathoracic recurrence on chest CT, or death from the procedure or a related complication). Secondary: EFS and OS. Target accrual reduced to a maximum of 62 patients with Amendment 3.

eligibility: Age under 50 years at enrollment.
Histologically confirmed osteosarcoma with lung metastases at initial diagnosis, or at first recurrence after completing therapy for initially localized disease.
4 or fewer nodules per lung consistent with or suspicious for metastases, at least one 3 mm or larger and all 3 cm or smaller, confirmed by rapid central imaging review.
Nodules resectable by either thoracotomy or thoracoscopy, as judged by the institutional surgeon.

Newly diagnosed: gross resection of the primary already completed, or surgical local control planned at the same time as thoracic surgery; must be receiving or have completed within 60 days standard first-line systemic therapy (for example cisplatin-doxorubicin or ifosfamide-based).
First recurrence: must have completed standard systemic therapy for the initial primary tumor.
Chest CT within 14 days before enrollment and within 28 days before planned surgery; clinical studies (if applicable) within 21 days.
No unresectable primary tumor.
No pulmonary lesions requiring anatomic resection (lobectomy or pneumonectomy) and no central lesions (involving or proximal to segmental bronchi).
No chest wall or mediastinal metastases and no significant pleural effusion.
No progression at the primary or pulmonary sites while on initial therapy (expected variation in nodule size is not exclusionary unless judged true progression).
No extrapulmonary metastatic disease.
No prior therapeutic pulmonary surgery for lung metastasis.

schema.text: Newly diagnosed FIGO stage III-IV ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer with a pathogenic BRCA1/2 alteration (germline or somatic) or BRCA wild-type HRD-positive tumor, in PR or CR after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.

eligibility: Newly diagnosed FIGO stage III or IV ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer: high-grade serous, high-grade endometrioid, carcinosarcoma, or other epithelial histology with a BRCA1/2 alteration. Documented pathogenic or suspected pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant (tumor or germline), or BRCA wild-type with HRD-positive tumor by a CLIA-certified laboratory (for example Myriad MyChoice); report required.

No prior PARP inhibitor (olaparib, niraparib, rucaparib).

Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

schema.label: Eligibility
schema.text: Metastatic or unresectable dedifferentiated liposarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, or related poorly differentiated sarcoma; anthracycline-naive and PD-1/PD-L1-naive; ECOG 0-1.

arms.text: Doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 IV day 1 for 6 cycles, then surveillance. At progression within 5 years of randomization, pembrolizumab 200 mg every 21 days (start within 21 days of confirmed progression) for up to 2 years.

schema.label: Follow-up

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival by RECIST 1.1, analyzed separately for UPS-related sarcomas and DDLPS; OS is the key secondary endpoint (upfront vs second-line pembrolizumab).

schema.text: Completely resected (R0) stage IIA, IIB, IIIA, or IIIB (T3-4N2) NSCLC per AJCC 8th edition, EGFR and ALK negative locally, registered 30-77 days after surgery. 1 cycle = 21 days.

eligibility: Completely resected (R0, negative margins) stage IIA, IIB, IIIA, or IIIB (T3-4N2) NSCLC of any histology, AJCC 8th edition.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration/randomization
schema.text: Newly diagnosed adverse-risk (ELN 2017) AML, age 18-59. Treatment starts within 7 days.

schema.text: One induction cycle (28 days) with optional local Day 14 marrow guiding re-induction for Arms 1, 2, 4, 5; Arm 3 gets 2 cycles.

arms.label: Arm 1 (control)
arms.text: 7+3: cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day continuous IV Days 1-7 + daunorubicin 60 mg/m2/day Days 1-3. Re-induction: cytarabine Days 1-5 + daunorubicin Days 1-2 (or cytarabine 1.5 g/m2 every 12 hours Days 1-3).

arms.text: Venetoclax Days 1-11 (ramp 50, 100, 200, then 400 mg) + daunorubicin 60 mg/m2 Days 2-4 + cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day continuous IV Days 2-8. Re-induction: venetoclax 400 mg Days 1-8, cytarabine Days 2-6, daunorubicin Days 2-3.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Azacitidine 75 mg/m2/day SC or IV Days 1-7 + venetoclax 400 mg PO Days 1-28 (Cycle 1 ramp 100, 200, 400 mg), 2 cycles; optional Day 21 marrow.

arms.label: Arm 4
arms.text: Liposomal daunorubicin 44 mg/m2 and cytarabine 100 mg/m2 (CPX-351) IV Days 1, 3, 5. Re-induction: Days 1 and 3.

arms.label: Arm 5
arms.text: Liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine Days 1, 3, 5 + venetoclax Days 1-14 (ramp 100, 200, then 400 mg). Re-induction: liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine Days 1 and 3 + venetoclax 400 mg Days 1-7.

schema.label: Reassessment

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: MRD-negative CR rate, each experimental arm compared with 7+3.

eligibility: Registered to the myeloMATCH master protocol and assigned to this substudy via MATCHBox.
Newly diagnosed, untreated AML per WHO with adverse (high) risk by ELN 2017; therapy-related AML, AML from an antecedent hematologic disorder, and AML-MRC eligible if previously untreated.
No APL; no favorable or intermediate ELN risk; no FLT3 mutation (ITD or TKD); no t(9;22).
Age 18-59; Zubrod performance status ≤ 3 by H&P within 7 days.

No prior AML therapy except hydroxyurea, ATRA until APL is excluded, a single intrathecal chemotherapy dose, or cytarabine up to 2500 mg total for urgent cytoreduction. WBC must be < 25 x 10^9/L before treatment.
Prior anthracycline for any indication allowed up to a cumulative 200 mg/m2 daunorubicin equivalent.
LVEF ≥ 50% by echo or MUGA within 28 days.
CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min; AST/ALT ≤ 3.0 x ULN and total bilirubin ≤ 2.0 x ULN (≤ 5.0 x ULN with Gilbert's) within 7 days, unless due to leukemia.
Baseline CBC, bilirubin, LDH, albumin, glucose, and fibrinogen within 14 days.
CNS disease allowed (treated with intrathecal chemotherapy per institutional guidelines).
No Wilson's disease or other copper-metabolism disorder; able to swallow and absorb oral medication.
No other investigational agents; prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with assessment, with no concurrent therapy for it except hormonal therapy.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load within 28 days; HCV treated and cured or undetectable on treatment within 28 days.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Agrees to MRD specimen submission through myeloMATCH.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Potential candidates; pre-study specimens per consent.

schema.label: Step 1: Randomization
schema.text: High-risk smoldering multiple myeloma diagnosed within the past 12 months. Accrual goal 288. Cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Age at high-risk SMM diagnosis (< 65 vs >= 65 years).

schema.label: Randomize (equal allocation)
schema.text: Treatment for 24 cycles.

arms.label: Arm A: DRd
arms.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg/30,000 units SC (or daratumumab 16 mg/kg IV if SC not tolerated) days 1, 8, 15, 22 cycles 1-2, days 1 and 15 cycles 3-6, day 1 cycles 7-24; lenalidomide 25 mg PO days 1-21 cycles 1-24 (10 mg if CrCl 30-59 ml/min); dexamethasone 40 mg PO days 1, 8, 15, 22 cycles 1-6, then 20 mg cycles 7-12.

arms.label: Arm B: Rd
arms.text: Lenalidomide 25 mg PO days 1-21 cycles 1-24 (10 mg if CrCl 30-59 ml/min); dexamethasone 40 mg PO days 1, 8, 15, 22 cycles 1-6, then 20 mg cycles 7-12.

schema.label: Stem cell collection
schema.text: Peripheral blood stem cell collection suggested between cycles 4-6; therapy may be interrupted up to 6 weeks. Not required.

schema.label: Observation
schema.text: Followed for response until progression and for survival for 15 years from randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival.

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG 0-2.

Asymptomatic high-risk smoldering myeloma diagnosed within 12 months, with 2 or more of: involved/uninvolved FLC ratio > 20 (but < 100 if involved FLC >= 10 mg/dL); serum M-protein > 2 g/dL; t(4;14), del 17p, del 13q, or 1q gain by cytogenetics or FISH; > 20% marrow plasma cells.
Bone marrow within 42 days showing 10-59% clonal plasma cells.
Measurable disease within 28 days: serum M-protein >= 1 g/dL or urine M-protein >= 200 mg/24 hours. SPEP, 24-hour UPEP, and serum FLC within 28 days.

No lytic lesions, no known plasmacytoma, and no unexplained hypercalcemia (> 11 mg/dL or 1 mg/dL above ULN) on MRI and PET within 60 days; no more than one focal marrow lesion on spine or pelvis MRI (MRI excused for incompatible pacemaker/ICD).
No MGUS.

No prior or concurrent systemic or radiation therapy for myeloma, and no prior glucocorticoid therapy for myeloma (prior steroids for non-malignant disease allowed; on-study use limited to prednisone 10 mg/day equivalent).
Labs within 28 days: Hgb >= 11 g/dL, platelets >= 100,000/mm3, ANC >= 1500/mm3, CrCl >= 30 mL/min, bilirubin <= 1.5 mg/dL (< 3.0 mg/dL for Gilbert's), AST/ALT <= 2.5 x ULN.
No COPD with FEV1 < 50% predicted and no moderate or severe persistent asthma within 2 years.
No grade >= 2 peripheral neuropathy. No active uncontrolled seizure disorder or seizure within 6 months.

No uncontrolled intercurrent illness (uncontrolled hypertension, symptomatic CHF, unstable angina, uncontrolled arrhythmia), no NYHA class III-IV heart failure, no history of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and no active uncontrolled infection.
No contraindication to DVT prophylaxis/aspirin; prior DVT/PE allowed with anticoagulant prophylaxis. No concurrent erythropoietin on study.
Prior malignancy allowed if treated with curative intent and disease-free for the period appropriate for cure.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy (HBsAg positive not eligible); HCV allowed if treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
No allergy to compounds similar to daratumumab, lenalidomide, or dexamethasone. Must enroll in the lenalidomide REMS program.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

Recurrent and/or metastatic disease incurable by local therapy, previously untreated in the recurrent/metastatic setting, with measurable disease.
Platinum-refractory: progression during or ≤ 29 weeks after completing definitive chemoradiation or adjuvant (postoperative) therapy.
PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1.

Any radiation therapy completed > 10 days before registration.

Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS ≤ 2.

ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed), creatinine ≤ 1.5 x ULN or CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN or direct bilirubin < ULN, AST/ALT ≤ 3.0 x ULN (< 5.0 x ULN with liver metastases).

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment.

schema.label: Eligibility
schema.text: Metastatic EGFR-sensitizing-mutant non-squamous NSCLC, first line. Patients already on osimertinib may enroll if started within 21 days before randomization with baseline imaging done before the first dose.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Brain metastases present vs absent; EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R vs other; ECOG PS 0-1 vs 2.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Accrual goal 300. 1 cycle = 21 days.

arms.text: Osimertinib 80 mg PO daily.

arms.text: Osimertinib 80 mg PO daily plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, starting cycle 2 day 1. If bevacizumab stops, osimertinib continues.

schema.label: Duration
